name: Three Anchor Bay and Mouille Point
aka: Three Anchor Bay, Mouille Point and Granger Bay rocks
Three Anchor Bay / Mouille Point / Granger Bay rocks
area: Green Point / Mouille Point
coord_source: Nominatim bay node for Three Anchor Bay carried over from the merge step and kept as-is (it matches the cove on Beach Road). No source gives an exact stand; the fishable ground is the rocky shore either side of the cove and the Mouille Point promenade rocks to the east, not the sandy slipway itself.
bottom: Rock and kelp reef with sand gullies either side of the cove; sand at the slipway; offshore reefs that have wrecked ships lie just off this coast.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (the standard marine recreational fishing permit) for rod and line; TMNP MPA controlled-zone rules, bag and size limits and closed seasons apply. No SANParks entry fee or activity permit here; that only applies in the Cape of Good Hope section. No lobster or abalone collection.
legality: Allowed with a permit. The Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled area starts at the high-water mark at Green Point S33°54.075' E018°24.037' and runs west and south round the peninsula (Wikipedia TMNP MPA page, fetched 30 October 2026); Three Anchor Bay (S33°54.35' E18°23.83') and the rocks west of that point are inside the controlled zone, where "fishing is allowed ... subject to permits, regulations, catch limits and seasons". The nearest no-take zone is Karbonkelberg, starting at Oudekraal S33°58.757', about 9 km south-west. Granger Bay and the harbour are "just outside the MPA", ordinary coast where the same DFFE recreational angling permit is still required for any marine angling. The Robben Island MPA's outer boundary stops at S33°54' / E18°24.06', so it does not reach this shore. Anglers agree: the 2014 Mouille Point poster calls it "an MPA that allows fishing", the 2010 Fishing area thread says "sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing" (no crayfish), and Zeebo (2019) says the V&A Waterfront is private property but "Elsewhere I think you're fine".
description: A small sandy cove with a slipway on Beach Road where Green Point meets Sea Point, with rock and kelp shoreline either side and along the Mouille Point promenade to the east; the City describes it as "a small, sheltered cove between Mouille Point and Sea Point" used mainly by recreational boat owners and kayakers. Sealine anglers rate the stretch poorly: "hotties are occasionally caught off the rocks" on white mussel, but the replies say "forget lures" and "wouldn't bother spinning", and the only nearby stand they recommend is Saunders Rock, about 2 km south-west. Three Anchor Bay's own Sealine thread is about hottentot from a small boat "in a straight line off shore of Seacliff Rd", not from the shore.
hazards: Exposed Atlantic rocks: a Sealine post records that two people drowned at Wolfgat and Mouille Point in one big-swell weekend (May 2011); the Sea Point reefs have wrecked many ships
Kelp and foul ground eat tackle ("small hottentots that aren't worth the tackle loss"); crabs strip baits, so fish over sand patches
Personal safety: fine by day, "late nights carry risk" (Zeebo); a 2009 post warns of perlemoen poachers living in the area
Boats and kayaks launch from the slipway in the cove, so keep lines clear of the launch lane
The boat thread notes the bay only fishes when "there can't be any swell"
access_notes: Beach Road, Green Point, on the Sea Point promenade. The City of Cape Town lists parking, disability access, toilets and a boat launch and slipway at the cove; no fee or hours are stated (fees are referred to the Recreation and Parks tariffs booklet). Walk straight off the promenade onto the rocks. Daytime access with a rod is fine per Sealine; avoid late nights. The V&A Waterfront is private property, and whether the Granger Bay pier/breakwater is open to the public went unanswered. No bait or tackle shops in Sea Point or town: anglers buy in Goodwood or at a Maitland garage.
unverified: Facing bearing of about 330 degrees is estimated from the map, not stated by any source
No source gives a tide preference for this stretch; "any" is a placeholder
Hottentot months are extrapolated from Saunders Rock posts 1 to 2 km away; no dated catch is reported at Three Anchor Bay, Mouille Point or Granger Bay
Galjoen, blacktail and roman are only "possibly" named by a poster who said he had never fished the area
DFFE galjoen closed-season dates were not sourced in this pass
Public access to the Granger Bay pier/breakwater and the Oceana Power Boat Club shore is unanswered in the thread
Exact stand is unsourced; the coordinate is the cove node, and the rocks either side are inferred from the City's description
Parking fees or hours on Beach Road are not stated on the City page
The 2011 Mouille Point drowning is a one-line forum mention with no detail

issues: Legality holds. The Wikipedia TMNP MPA page, re-fetched 30 Oct 2026, starts the boundary at 'Green Point at S33°54.075'; E018°24.037''. It lists Three Anchor Bay as a dive site inside the MPA at 33°54.36'S 18°23.85'E, says 'Fishing is allowed in the controlled zone of the MPA subject to permits', and puts Granger Bay 'just outside the MPA'. Karbonkelberg starts at Oudekraal S33°58.757', about 9 km south-west. No restricted zone is nearby.

The record's name overreaches. Granger Bay is about 1.8 km east of the coordinate and outside the MPA, and it is largely V&A Waterfront land: Zeebo says 'V&A is private property', and access to the pier went unanswered (sealine granger-bay-fishing-sea-point.101962). The Mouille Point promenade rocks east of the Green Point lighthouse (about 18.401E) are also outside the TMNP MPA. They are still legal with the DFFE permit, but the record's line 'the rocks west of that point are inside the controlled zone' leaves out that half the named stretch is ordinary coast.

Robben Island MPA nuance. Its south-east corner (S33°54', E18°24.06') sits about 100 m north of the Green Point lighthouse, so the two MPAs meet right at Mouille Point. Three Anchor Bay (S33°54.35') is south of it, as the record says. This does not change the permit position.

The aka 'Rocklands' is wrong. Rocklands Beach is a separate rocky beach further south-west along the Sea Point promenade (voicemap and Lonely Planet results in the evidence), about 1 km or more away. The name also collides with 'Rocklands', the Simon's Town end point of the Boulders no-take zone, which could mislead a legality lookup.

The evidence is thin and only indirect. The only first-hand shore statement is saltysouti (sealine 101962, Dec 2019): the area is 'poor fishing', 'hotties are occasionally caught off the rocks', white mussel works. It does not say which rocks between Granger Bay and Sea Point. The Mouille Point thread (82659) is an unanswered question with 0 replies. 'hotties 3 anchor bay' (81257) is small-boat fishing ('in a straight line off shore of Seacliff Rd'). The Sea Point area thread (23669) names only Saunders Rock: 'saunders rock is pretty much the only spot that im aware of in this area'. This is enough to keep the record as a light-bait fallback, not enough for more.
Light-tackle fit is bait only. Both replies say 'forget lures' and 'wouldn't bother spinning', so spinning, dropshot and fly should not be rated here.

species.size: Small; the Sea Point posts call them "small hottentots that aren't worth the tackle loss". No sizes reported for this stretch; the 2 kg fish in the reports are boat catches around Robben Island.
species.bait: White mussel (saltysouti: "white mussel works well"); mussel, red bait and prawn (Zeebo); sardine or pilchard, worm, chokka strips; long-shank 1 to 2/0 hooks fished close to the kelp over sand patches to beat the crabs (general Sea Point hottentot threads)
species.notes: The only shore species anyone reports here: "hotties are occasionally caught off the rocks" (Granger Bay Fishing / Sea Point, 2019), while the same poster calls the area poor fishing. Summer months are extrapolated from Saunders Rock advice 1 to 2 km away ("Saunders Rock in summer", "the only location and species that can be caught this time of year from the rocks" in November). Both replies say to skip lures and spinning.

species.size: No sizes given
species.bait: Mussel, red bait, prawn (Zeebo)
species.notes: Speculative: "possibly blacktail or Roman" from a poster who had never fished the area; no catch reported.

species.size: No sizes given for this stretch
species.bait: Red bait or white mussel (general Atlantic seaboard galjoen baits in the Sealine threads)
species.notes: Named only as a possible "bank species" ("gallie") by Zeebo, who says he has never fished the area; the nearest reported winter galjoen catches are at Bakoven. Zeebo flags "closed season??"; check the DFFE galjoen closed season before targeting them.

species.size: No sizes given
species.bait: Mussel, red bait, prawn (Zeebo)
species.notes: Speculative: "possibly blacktail or Roman" from a poster who had never fished the area; no catch reported.

name: Saunders Rocks
aka: the rock formation at the end of Sea Point beyond the last traffic circle
area: Sea Point / Bantry Bay, Atlantic Seaboard
coord_source: photon.komoot.io query on 30 Oct 2026 returned OSM natural=beach 'Saunders Rocks Beach', Sea Point, at lat -33.9236808, lon 18.377589; identical to the merge step's Nominatim result. The usual stand, the big granite rock behind the tidal pool at the end of Beach Road, is within about 100 m of this point; the exact rock was not geocoded.

access.note: Approximate, not geocoded: street parking at the south-western end of Beach Road where it becomes one-way at the no-entry sign (Sealine directions, 2009 and 2012). From there a walkway and steps lead down to the tidal pool and the rock; you climb over rocks to the stand without getting your feet wet.

bottom: Granite boulders and reef with kelp beds and small sand patches between; foul ground, so posters warn of tackle loss and of crabs stripping baits (fish the bait on a sand patch beside the kelp).
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (the Post Office marine permit), carried on you. A separate DFFE bait-collection permit and the daily limits apply if you gather white mussel or mussel/coral worm (a poster notes worm collection is regulated down to blade size). West Coast rock lobster needs its own permit and open season, so do not use crayfish as bait without one. Galjoen, if one turns up, has a national closed season from 15 October to the end of February.
legality: Allowed with a permit. Saunders Rocks lies inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone, whose Atlantic-side boundary starts at Mouille Point / Green Point (S33 54.075 E018 24.037); the nearest restricted (no-take) zone, Karbonkelberg, only begins at Oudekraal (S33 58.757 E018 21.847), about 6 km to the south (Wikipedia MPA page fetched 30 Oct 2026, quoting the 2004 regulations, Government Gazette 26431 of 4 June 2004; the 2004 zoning summary supplied for this project agrees). The MPA page states "Fishing is allowed in the controlled zone of the MPA subject to permits", issued by DFFE Marine Resources Management. Forum posters agree the stretch is open: "from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing" (zeeQo, Sealine, Nov 2010), and a 2014 Mouille Point poster calls it "an MPA that allows fishing". No SANParks gate fee or activity permit applies here (those only cover the Cape of Good Hope section). It is a public City of Cape Town beach and tidal pool; no angling ban was found in the evidence, though fishing inside the tidal pool itself should be avoided.
description: A granite outcrop with a small tidal pool at the south-western end of Beach Road, where Sea Point becomes Bantry Bay, reached by a walkway from the street and a scramble over the rocks. Sealine regulars fish it from the big rock behind the pool or from the little bay to its left, almost only for hottentot: "Use light tackle, much more fun ... They have very small mouths so use a number 1-4 (not to be confused with 4/0)" (sparticus, 2009), with sardine, white mussel or worm, and "you can fish at Saunders Rocks behind the pool or to the left in the little bay" (Ta-aai, 2009). The fish run small with the odd 1.2 kg one, posters in the area advise against lures and spinning, and nobody confirms galjoen here.
hazards: Atlantic swell washes over the rocks: 'keep your eyes on the ocean at all times as the waves tend to come over the rocks on certain occasions' (sparticus, 2009); fish it on a small swell or when the south-easter flattens the Atlantic side
Scramble over wet granite and kelp to reach the stand; the bigger rock to the left is a longer walk
Foul ground: expect tackle loss, and crabs strip baits fast
Personal safety: fine in daylight, posters warn against late nights on this stretch and against fishing alone; a 2009 poster warns of perlemoen poachers living in the area
The Cape Town Cycle Tour (a Sunday in March) closes Beach Road and Victoria Road for the day
No tackle or bait shops in Sea Point or town (2011): bring bait with you
access_notes: From Green Point drive south-west along Beach Road past the promenade, straight on at the last traffic circle, and continue until the road becomes one-way at the no-entry sign; park on the street there (residential Bantry Bay, no car park, no gate fee, public beach and tidal pool open at all hours). A walkway leads down to the tidal pool and the big rock: 'no feet wet as you have to climb over rocks'. Fish from the rock behind the pool, the little bay to the left, or walk left to the larger rock for bigger fish. Daylight sessions advised. Bring bait: posters say Sea Point has no bait shop (Goodwood tackle shop or the BP garage in Maitland were the 2011 suggestions).
unverified: Tide preference: no source states one, so 'any' is a placeholder, not an angler's opinion
Facing bearing of about 300 degrees is estimated from the coastline orientation, not from a source
Access point coordinates are approximate, from the forum directions and the road layout, not geocoded
Galjoen at Saunders: asked about twice, never confirmed; one regular has 'never heard of galjoen there'
Blacktail and Roman appear only in a speculative list for the Granger Bay to Sea Point stretch from a poster who had never fished it
Fishing inside or from the wall of the tidal pool itself: likely barred by the City's coastal by-law, not checked
Bait shop information is from 2011 and may be out of date
Depth of 'the hole right in front of the rock' is not quantified by any source

issues: LEGALITY HOLDS, BUT THE OFFICIAL CITATION IS UNVERIFIED: lat -33.9237 lies between the Mouille Point start of the TMNP MPA (S33 54.075, about -33.901) and the Oudekraal start of the Karbonkelberg no-take zone (S33 58.757, about -33.979), so the spot is in the controlled zone under the 2004 zoning supplied for this project. A Sealine angler supports this ('from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing', zeeQo, Nov 2010, https://sealine.co.za/threads/fishing-area.34028/). However, the only Wikipedia MPA fetch in the 29 Oct cache read characters 100000-200000 and found no zoning text and no permit sentence ('The only fishing mention is a reference link to SANParks' fishing page'). The quote 'Fishing is allowed in the controlled zone of the MPA subject to permits' comes from a 30 Oct fetch that is not in the cache and could not be checked here.

TIDAL-POOL BY-LAW NOT CHECKED: the record already flags that fishing in or from the City tidal pool may be barred by the City of Cape Town coastal by-law. No City page in the evidence settles this. It does not refute the spot, because the stand is the rock behind the pool and the bay to its left, but the page should keep telling anglers not to fish the pool.

MOST OF THE QUOTES CANNOT BE VERIFIED FROM THE CACHE: thread where-to-catch-the-hotties.14704 and thread cape-town-fishing-spot.102094 have no content in the evidence file. Several quoted or specific claims depend on them: 'Use light tackle, much more fun ... number 1-4 (not to be confused with 4/0)' (sparticus 2009), the 1.2 kg fish in Feb 2009, 'keep your eyes on the ocean ... waves tend to come over the rocks', 'no feet wet as you have to climb over rocks', 'the hotties are not that big but fun none the less', 'really gooi that sinker', 'a hole right in front of the rock', Berkley Gulp sandworm working, 'Lots of hotties but ive never heard of galjoen there' (Occie 2015), and the '2min away' resident. My attempt to fetch 14704 failed with HTTP 000 (curl through the corporate proxy). They may well be genuine, but this pass could not confirm them.

HOOK SIZE IS NOT CORROBORATED: the only hook advice in the cache is general hottentot advice, not advice for Saunders: 'long shank #01-2/0 for average fish, 3/0-4/0 for bigger fish' (subaruseun, https://sealine.co.za/threads/hotties.61809/). The record's '#1 to #4' rests entirely on the unverified 2009 sparticus quote. Ranges like 3/0-4/0 also show that general hottentot rigs run heavier than the record suggests.

THREADS 104058 AND 89025 ARE ONLY QUESTIONS: in the cache they are search snippets ('0 replies', 'no answer is shown'). They show that people ask about Saunders, but they support no bait, size or season claim and should not be cited as if they do.

BAIT DETAILS ARE GENERAL, NOT SITE-SPECIFIC: chokka strips come from a kayak angler (Speedmaster, white-mussel.58422). Prawn and redbait come from general hottentot advice in hotties.61809, and the green-water and kelp-frond tips come from a spearfisher (Jacquesdw). The baits named specifically for Saunders are worm (KLIPVIS 2009, zeeQo 2010), mussel (zeeQo), white mussel salted and halved, and sardine 'better when water is cold' (Jo-Jo, who lived opposite Saunders on Seacliffe Road, 2011).

species.size: Mostly small, hand-size to about 30 cm and a few hundred grams ('the hotties are not that big but fun none the less'); the odd big one, a 1.2 kg fish reported in Feb 2009; bigger fish from the larger rock to the left if you can 'really gooi that sinker'.
species.bait: Light rod, long-shank #1 to #4 hooks, a light trace (shorter in strong water) and a bottle sinker cast short, right against the kelp or onto a sand patch beside it. Baits: sardine/pilchard (better in cold water), white mussel salted to firm it and halved, mussel/coral worm, thin chokka strips, prawn, redbait; crayfish is rated best but wasteful and needs its own permit. Berkley Gulp sandworm reportedly works, but another poster had no joy on artificials, and posters in the area say lures and spinning are not worth it.
species.notes: Present year round but posters name Saunders for summer ('Saunders Rock in summer', zeeQo 2010); catches reported Feb 2009 and Mar-Apr 2012. Fish 'a hole right in front of the rock', 'behind the pool or to the left in the little bay'. A spearo's tip: green-tinged, dirty-but-not-rough water switches them on, 'ice cold blue water shut them down', and in cold water they sit high among the kelp fronds. Galjoen is asked about but a regular says 'Lots of hotties but ive never heard of galjoen there' (Occie, 2015); the nearest galjoen spot named is Bakoven.

name: Clifton gullies
area: Clifton, Atlantic Seaboard, Cape Town
coord_source: Nominatim (fetched 2026-10-30) fixes Fourth Beach at -33.9403112, 18.3754304, the only Clifton entry it returns. The stand given is the boulder gullies at 3rd Beach, estimated about 200 m north of that fix using lekkeslaap's beach-to-beach distances (3rd to 4th 242 m, 3rd to 2nd 173 m, 3rd to 1st 356 m); the merge step's rough -33.934, 18.376 corresponds to 1st Beach at the north end. Verify on the ground.

access.note: Victoria Road (M6) roadside parking above the coves, then a steep set of stairs down to 3rd/4th Beach; 1st Beach has its own stairs further north. Approximate point.

bottom: White sand coves separated by clusters of large granite boulders; the gullies between the four beaches are sand-floored rock channels with kelp on the outer boulders.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine, sold at Post Office branches), with the national bag and size limits and the galjoen closed season (15 Oct to end Feb). No SANParks fee or activity permit for this section of the MPA. City by-law: no fishing in tidal pools or within 100 m of a signposted bathing area; clear all bait and tackle when you leave (s 6(3)).
legality: Allowed with a permit. Clifton lies inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA's controlled zone: the Karbonkelberg restricted (no-take) zone only starts at Oudekraal, about 4 km south, and the other no-take zones (St James, Boulders, Castle Rock, Paulsberg, Cape of Good Hope) are in False Bay or at the Point. Shore angling therefore needs a DFFE recreational angling permit; no SANParks entry fee applies here. Sealine anglers read the MCM map the same way in 2010: "from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing". The City of Cape Town Coastal By-law 2020 (openbylaws.org.za, fetched 2026-10-30) prohibits fishing only in a tidal pool or within 100 m of a designated bathing area where the City has erected signs to that effect (s 14(1)(e), s 11), and s 6(2) makes it an offence to use fishing gear in a way that endangers others, so keep clear of the lifeguarded bathing area at 4th Beach in season. No fishing-prohibited signage for Clifton was found online; check on site. Galjoen closed season 15 October to end February applies.
description: Four small white-sand coves separated by clusters of granite boulders, below Victoria Road between Bantry Bay and Camps Bay. FishingBooker's Cape Town guide lists Clifton Beach as "a popular destination for beach-goers and anglers alike" with "surf fishing for species such as Galjoen, Kabeljou, and White Steenbras", and Sealine anglers reported steenbras at 1st Beach "middle of winter" and "gallies in gullies at clifton 3rd beach after big storms" (2009). It is first a bathing beach, so the realistic light-tackle use is a small-hook bait rod in the boulder gullies at first light in winter, with hottentot on the rocks in summer.
hazards: Big winter westerly swells wash over the outer boulders; the galjoen gullies fish best after a storm, not during one
Wave-washed granite is slippery and the stairs down from Victoria Road are steep
Icy Atlantic water; do not wade out on the boulders
Summer bathing crowds, especially on 4th Beach: casting near swimmers breaches Coastal By-law s 6(2) and the City can post signs banning fishing within 100 m of a designated bathing area
Kelp on the outer boulders snags light line; expect tackle loss
Parking on Victoria Road is very limited in the height of summer
access_notes: Park on Victoria Road (M6) above the coves and take the steep stairs down; lekkeslaap says parking "can be limited in the height of summer" and advises arriving early. You can walk between beaches along the sand or over the boulders at low tide (1st to 4th is about 770 m: 1st-3rd 356 m, 3rd-2nd 173 m, 3rd-4th 242 m). Ablutions at 1st and 4th Beach, kiosk at 4th. No gate, no fee, no hours. Fish early morning, out of bathing hours and ideally in winter, and stay away from the bathing area at 4th Beach in season; check for City pictogram signs at the stairs.
unverified: Light-tackle suitability is inferred from the terrain and species (gully galjoen, hottentot and beach steenbras on small-hook bait); no page describes lure, fly or light-tackle fishing at Clifton specifically
Tide preference: no source states it; 'pushing' is the general gully/galjoen convention
Rip currents and typical 10-15 C water temperature are general Atlantic seaboard knowledge; lekkeslaap only says the water is 'icy'

Bag and size limits quoted (galjoen 35 cm/2, white steenbras 60 cm/1, hottentot 22 cm/10, kob 60 cm/1) are from memory of the DFFE recreational regulations; only the galjoen closed-season dates are sourced (whalecoast.info search snippet)
Gully coordinates for 1st and 3rd Beach are estimated from the Nominatim Fourth Beach fix and lekkeslaap's inter-beach distances, not geocoded directly
Whether the City has erected fishing-prohibited pictograms at the 4th Beach bathing area: none found online
Lifeguard season and Blue Flag status at 4th Beach were not confirmed by the pages fetched
The exact location of 'Clifton point' in the Sealine spearfishing thread (north or south end of the beaches) is not stated

issues: Legality holds. Clifton lies between Mouille Point and Oudekraal, so it is in the TMNP MPA controlled zone, not in any 2004 restricted zone. Karbonkelberg starts at Oudekraal, about 4 km south. Sealine 'Fishing area' (zeeQo, 11 Nov 2010) reads it the same way: 'from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing'. No SANParks fee applies here. The City Coastal By-law claims (s 14(1)(e), s 11, s 6) cite openbylaws.org.za, which is not in the 29 Oct cache. I did not re-check them, but they add limits and do not make the spot illegal.

The evidence is thin and generic, but at least one angling page names the spot. FishingBooker's Cape Town guide (updated 8 Jan 2026) names Clifton Beach for 'surf fishing for species such as Galjoen, Kabeljou, and White Steenbras'. This is a broad SEO blog from a charter platform, with no tackle, season or stand detail. The only Clifton catch evidence is a single 2009 Sealine post by gotaway. For steenbras it is hearsay ('heard about steenbras at clifton 1st beach'), and 'seen gallies in gullies at clifton 3rd beach' does not even say the fish were caught on rod and line. No source describes light-tackle, lure or fly fishing at Clifton.

The hottentot entry has abundance 'regular', which the record's own notes contradict ('No rod-caught hottentot report at Clifton itself was found'). The only Clifton-specific hottentot source is the Sealine spearfishing thread 'Clifton point' (pelagic, 19 Oct 2009), fetched today: 'I used to dive here a lot for nice hotties when I first started to spearfish... nice boulders and caves for big hotties on the inside of thew point'. That is diving, not angling. The 1.8 kg hottie later in the thread came from Oudekraal, not Clifton. The summer months 11-3 come from the diver's 'great spot for summer'. Downgrade the abundance to occasional.

The kob entry has method 'spinning' with paddle-tails and plugs at first and last light. No source supports this: FishingBooker says only 'surf fishing' and the record admits there is no Clifton method. The size claim ('shore kob on the Atlantic seaboard are mostly juvenile 40-70 cm') is unsourced. The only support for kob at Clifton is FishingBooker's 'Kabeljou'.

The galjoen months [5-9] are invented. Neither FishingBooker nor the Sealine post gives a season; gotaway says only 'after big storms'. Winter-storm timing inside the open season (March to mid-October) is a reasonable inference, but it should be listed under unverified. The size line ('typically 30-45 cm (1-2 kg)') is general knowledge, not from a source.

The galjoen sources include https://whalecoast.info/attraction/fishing/, a Hermanus/Overberg page that the record uses only for the closed-season dates. It is not evidence of galjoen at Clifton and should not appear in the species sources.

species.size: Mostly 20-30 cm pan-size fish; divers report 'big hotties' on the Clifton boulders. Minimum size 22 cm, bag limit 10 (DFFE).
species.bait: worm or mussel bait on a small hook, dropped straight down beside the boulders (the bait Sealine anglers use at the neighbouring Saunders Rocks and Maidens Cove)
species.notes: The Clifton-specific evidence is a Sealine spearfishing thread, 'Clifton point' (Oct 2009): "there are some nice boulders and caves for big hotties on the inside of thew point", a summer spot when the south-easter blows out other sites. The shore-angling reports are from the adjacent rocks: zeeQo (Sealine, Nov 2010) suggests hottentot at Saunders Rock and Maidens Cove in summer using worm or mussel bait. No rod-caught hottentot report at Clifton itself was found.

species.size: Cape shore galjoen typically 30-45 cm (1-2 kg); the odd fish over 50 cm. Minimum size 35 cm, bag limit 2 (DFFE).
species.bait: redbait, white mussel or wonderworm on a small hook, drifted in the white water of a boulder gully; the Clifton posts name no bait, this is the standard Cape gully approach
species.notes: Sealine (gotaway, 3 May 2009): "seen gallies in gullies at clifton 3rd beach after big storms". FishingBooker lists galjoen for surf fishing at Clifton Beach. Closed season 15 October to end February, so the season is March to mid-October with the best fishing after winter storms.

species.size: Beach fish are mostly 40-60 cm juveniles; bigger fish of 70 cm plus turn up in winter. Minimum size 60 cm, bag limit 1 (DFFE), so most must go back.
species.bait: sand prawn, white mussel or bloodworm on a small hook cast into the beach gutter at 1st Beach; no Clifton-specific bait is given by the sources
species.notes: Hearsay only: Sealine (gotaway, 3 May 2009): "heard about steenbras at clifton 1st beach - middle of winter". FishingBooker lists white steenbras for surf fishing at Clifton Beach.

species.size: No Clifton size data; shore kob on the Atlantic seaboard are mostly juvenile 40-70 cm fish. Minimum size 60 cm, bag limit 1 (DFFE).
species.bait: paddle-tail soft plastics or plugs at first light and dusk; FishingBooker gives no Clifton-specific method, only bait bottom fishing for the Table Bay area generally
species.notes: Named only by FishingBooker's list for Clifton Beach ('Kabeljou'). No forum catch report at Clifton; the nearest hearsay is "heard about cob at camps bay/glen beach" (Sealine, May 2009). No best months are given by any source.

name: Camps Bay rocks
aka: Camps Bay rocks (right-hand side of the beach)
area: Camps Bay
coord_source: Nominatim (OSM way 544315995, "Camps Bay Tidal Pool", centroid -33.95486, 18.37552, queried 2026-10-30), moved about 50 m seaward to the rocks just outside the south-west corner of the pool wall, which is the "behind the tidal pool" stand Johnny Blaze names. The alternative stand, the rocks at the Glen Beach end about 800 m north, is not separately geocoded.

access.note: Victoria Road street parking beside the tidal pool at the southern end of Camps Bay beach (placed from the OSM pool outline; approximate). A few steps down onto the rocks.

bottom: Granite boulders and low reef thick with kelp and loose seaweed ("there is usually lots of sea weed in the water there"), with the sand of Camps Bay beach alongside.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (sold at Post Offices). Galjoen has a national closed season from 15 October to the end of February, a daily bag limit of 2 and a minimum size of 35 cm; hottentot 10 per day, minimum 22 cm. Check the current DFFE recreational fishing brochure for kob limits and any changes.
legality: Fishing is allowed. Camps Bay lies inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA but north of the Karbonkelberg restricted (no-take) zone, which runs from Oudekraal (about 3 km south of the tidal pool) to the Hout Bay Sentinel, so this is a controlled zone where shore angling is allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit. The Sealine "Fishing area" thread agrees: "from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing" (zeeQo, Nov 2010), and the opening poster read the MCM map the same way. No SANParks entry fee or activity permit applies on this stretch. The tidal pool itself is a City of Cape Town swimming pool; fish the rocks outside it, not the pool.
description: Granite rocks at either end of Camps Bay beach: the rocks outside the municipal tidal pool at the southern end, where Victoria Road bends toward Bakoven, and the rocks at the Glen Beach end to the north. Sealine anglers say "the rocks on the right hand side of camps bay beach deliver nice size gallies with the correct conditions" and suggest fishing behind the tidal pool, with the warning that "there is usually lots of sea weed in the water there"; one regular has seen nice hottentot in the kelp in line with Pick n Pay. Open to the full Atlantic swell, with a heavy shorebreak, and shared with bathers and divers in summer.
hazards: Heavy kelp and loose seaweed in the water behind the tidal pool: constant snags and fouled lines (Johnny Blaze, Sealine 2012)
Fully exposed Atlantic swell with a powerful shorebreak; two 16-year-olds were presumed drowned in the surf at Camps Bay in September 2013 (Sealine news thread)
Slippery, wave-washed granite boulders; cold water

Crowded in summer with bathers, swimmers in the tidal pool and divers; zeeQo calls the kelp spot in line with Pick n Pay crowded, and Camps Bay is a Blue Flag bathing beach, so casting room is limited on hot days
access_notes: Public beach, no gate, no fee, open at all hours. Park on Victoria Road beside the tidal pool at the southern end of the beach (City street parking with marshals in season) and step down onto the rocks outside the pool; the rocks at the Glen Beach end are about 800 m north along Victoria Road, reached from the Glen Beach parking and steps. No drive-time statement in any source; OSRM free-flow estimate 12 min from Green Point and 29 min from Westlake (merge step, 2026-10-29). Best fished early morning or in winter when the beach is empty.
unverified: Which end 'the rocks on the right hand side of camps bay beach' refers to: assumed facing the sea, i.e. the northern (Glen Beach) end; the tidal pool rocks at the southern end are the stand Johnny Blaze names, so both ends are described.
No source states a tide preference for this spot; tide_pref 'any' is a placeholder. Galjoen anglers on this coast generally fish a rough, pushing sea in winter (general knowledge, not spot-specific).
No bait, lure or tackle is stated for galjoen at this spot; the bait list is general Cape practice.
Hottentot evidence is a diver's sighting in the kelp, not a documented rod-and-line catch here.
Kob is hearsay only ('heard about cob at camps bay/glen beach').
A fish reported as a banded galjoen from the Camps Bay area (1 Aug 2012) was judged in the same thread to be an ordinary galjoen, so banded galjoen is not listed.
Typical sizes are not given by any source.
Paid street parking with marshals on Victoria Road is general knowledge, not from an angling source.
Facing bearing (250), shelter, bottom and depth are read from the map and the kelp/seaweed remarks, not stated by an angler.

issues: Legality holds but rests on the 2004 TMNP MPA zoning given in the brief plus forum posts, not on an official page. Camps Bay tidal pool (-33.9549, 18.3755) is about 3 km north of Oudekraal, where the Karbonkelberg restricted zone starts, so it is in the controlled zone. The cached Sealine 'Fishing area' thread (zeeQo, 11 Nov 2010: 'from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing') and the Oudekraal search snippet describing the 'Karbonkelberg Restricted Zone' between the Sentinel and Oudekraal both agree. The evidence has no SANParks or DFFE page, so the record cites no official source.

Not checked: the evidence has nothing on City of Cape Town Coastal By-law or Blue Flag bathing-zone limits on angling at Camps Bay. The record already says not to fish in the tidal pool, which is right, but there may be a seasonal no-angling area inside the demarcated swimming zone. Flag as unverified rather than claim 'open at all hours' with no limits.

The key galjoen quote was NOT in the 29 Oct cache: the cached search snippet for camps-bay.49798 said 'No species or bait'. I fetched the thread today (2 Nov 2026) and the quote is real: gotaway, post #3, 23 Apr 2011, 'the rocks on the right hand side of camps bay beach deliver nice size gallies with the correct conditions!!!' (post #4 is a duplicate). Cite it as opened on 2 Nov 2026, not 29 Oct.

The Johnny Blaze 'behind the Camps Bay tidal pool' tip (bakoven-sea-point.63306, 20 Apr 2012) is verified in the cache, but it names no species. It is a stand recommendation only, so it should not be read as a galjoen or hottentot source.

The record misdescribes the banded galjoen thread (banded-galjoen.66723). It does not settle that the fish was 'an ordinary galjoen': whalerider says it is not banded, Blanky thinks it was banded, flippy is unsure ('could also of been a baby poensie'), and later posts refer to 'die dam' and Strandfontein. No post says it was caught from the shore or how it was caught, and the opening poster's handle is 'speartackle'. Location is only 'Camps Bay area'. This is not evidence of a rod-and-line shore catch at these rocks.

Galjoen months [5-9] are invented for this spot: gotaway gives no season, only 'with the correct conditions'. The winter months come from other spots (Bakoven, Llandudno, Clifton). The legal open season is 1 Mar to 14 Oct. The '1-2 kg typical' size is general knowledge, and the record does say so.

species.size: No weights given; "nice size gallies" (gotaway, 2011). Cape shore galjoen typically run 1-2 kg (general, not spot-specific).
species.bait: Not stated for this spot. Galjoen on this coast are taken on bait (redbait, white mussel, sea lice) rather than lures; zeeQo, who fishes Bakoven and Camps Bay, tried artificial baits in Cape Town without success and prefers real bait for the scent.
species.notes: gotaway (Sealine, 23 Apr 2011): "the rocks on the right hand side of camps bay beach deliver nice size gallies with the correct conditions!!!" A galjoen was also caught "in the Camps Bay area" on 1 Aug 2012 (first reported as a banded galjoen, then judged in-thread to be an ordinary galjoen). Winter fish on this seaboard: the same angler community reports gallies at Bakoven and Llandudno in winter and in the Clifton gullies after big storms. Closed season 15 Oct to end Feb.

species.size: Not stated; "nice hottentot" seen by a diver.
species.bait: Worm or mussel on small hooks (zeeQo's advice for hotties on this seaboard).
species.notes: zeeQo (Sealine, 18 Nov 2010): Camps Bay "by the kelp, in line with Pick n Pay" is crowded, so he dives there instead and has seen nice hottentot. This is a diver's sighting, not a documented shore catch at this exact spot; the same angler fishes hottentot in summer at Saunders Rock and Maidens Cove on worm or mussel.

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: Not stated by the source.
species.notes: Hearsay only: gotaway (Sealine, 3 May 2009) "heard about cob at camps bay/glen beach". No method, bait, season or size given; no documented catch.

name: Maiden's Cove
area: Clifton, Atlantic Seaboard
coord_source: Stand placed on the outer granite seaward of the Maiden's Cove tidal pools using OpenStreetMap features fetched through Overpass on 2026-10-30: tidal pools (ways 693077947 at -33.94428, 18.37326 and 693077948 at -33.94486, 18.37346), "Maiden's Cove Beach" (way 693077946 at -33.94467, 18.37367) and the "Maiden's Cove" bay node (1646282104 at -33.94292, 18.37077). Car park is OSM parking way 695640090 (70 bays) at -33.94408, 18.37430. Nominatim returns only the MyCiTi bus stop on Victoria Road (-33.94432, 18.37621), which is what the merge step had. No angling source gives a precise stand.

access.note: Public surface car park (about 70 bays on OSM) at the end of the Maiden's Cove access road off Victoria Road, between Clifton 4th Beach and Glen Beach; the granite rocks and the two free tidal pools are a 50-100 m walk west of it. A neighbouring 100-bay lot is tagged private on OSM.

bottom: Granite boulders and low reef with kelp beds off the point; a small sandy cove ("Maiden's Cove Beach" on OSM) between the point and Clifton 4th. Read from the mapped features and the character of this coast, not from an angling source.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine), bought at a Post Office and carried on you. No SANParks entry fee or activity permit on this stretch (those apply only in the Cape of Good Hope section). Galjoen closed season 15 October to end February. National bag and size limits apply: hottentot 10 per day with no minimum size, galjoen 2 per day over 35 cm, kob and white steenbras 1 per day over 60 cm (limits from memory of the DFFE recreational list, not fetched this pass; check the current list).
legality: Allowed with a permit. Maiden's Cove is inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA but about 4 km north of Oudekraal, the northern boundary of the Karbonkelberg restricted (no-take) zone; the stretch from Oudekraal north to Mouille Point is a controlled zone where shore angling is allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit. Sealine locals say the same in practice: "from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing" (zeeQo, Nov 2010) and "The cut-off is at the Kramat just before the 12 apostles hotel" (Jo-Jo, Aug 2011). Checked against the 2004 TMNP MPA zoning list supplied with this task and the two Sealine threads. No City of Cape Town by-law restricting angling at Maiden's Cove was found; the two tidal pools are public bathing pools and should not be fished.
description: Granite point with two free tidal pools between Clifton 4th Beach and Glen Beach, with a large public car park right behind the rocks off Victoria Road. Two Sealine locals list it among their regular Atlantic seaboard spots with Saunders Rock and Bakoven, mainly for hottentot off the rocks in summer on worm or mussel bait; galjoen, kob and white steenbras are reported from the neighbouring Clifton and Glen beaches rather than the point itself. It is open Atlantic water on a kelp-fringed granite shore, so it is a small-swell, calm-day spot rather than a big-sea one.
hazards: Open Atlantic swell washing over low granite ledges; the surf on this stretch has drowned swimmers (Sealine news thread on two teens lost off Camps Bay, 2013), so stay off the low rocks in a westerly or south-westerly swell
Cold water, usually 10-14 C, and slippery weed-covered granite
Dense kelp close in snags lures and rigs; locals on this stretch fish bait rather than artificials for hottentot
Crowds of beach-goers and braaiers on summer weekends and public holidays, and thefts from cars along Victoria Road (general Atlantic seaboard caution, unsourced)
access_notes: Turn off Victoria Road at the Maiden's Cove entrance between Clifton 4th Beach and Glen Beach into the public car park (about 70 bays on OSM, with further small lots along Victoria Road); the rocks and the two free tidal pools are a 50-100 m walk. MyCiTi 'Maiden's Cove' stops on Victoria Road are right at the entrance. No gate fee. City of Cape Town public open space with picnic lawns and braai spots, so it fills on summer weekends and public holidays and Victoria Road parking is scarce then. Fish the open granite, not the tidal pools. No published opening hours or car-park locking times were found.
unverified: Tide preference: no source states one; 'pushing' is the general Cape rock-angling default for hottentot, not a Maiden's Cove claim
Bearing, shelter, bottom and depth are read from the OSM features and the character of this granite-and-kelp coast, not from an angling source
The stand coordinate is placed on the rocks seaward of the westernmost tidal pool from OSM features; no angler gives a precise stand
Galjoen, kob and white steenbras come from 2009 hearsay about the adjacent Clifton and Glen beaches and a non-local FishingBooker guide; nobody reports them from the Maiden's Cove rocks themselves
No lure or fly reports exist for this spot; the one angler who commented said artificial baits had not worked for him in Cape Town

Typical sizes, and the hottentot, galjoen, kob and white steenbras bag and size limits, are from general knowledge of the DFFE recreational regulations and were not fetched this pass (the galjoen closed season is from the merge's legality note)
Picnic lawns and braai facilities, MyCiTi route numbers, car-park hours, the Victoria Road car-theft caution and the 'tidal pools are not for fishing' point were not sourced this pass
Water temperature range is general Atlantic seaboard knowledge, not from a source for this spot

issues: Legality holds. At lat -33.9446 the stand is about 4 km north of Oudekraal, the northern limit of the Karbonkelberg restricted zone in the 2004 TMNP zoning supplied with the task, so it falls in the controlled zone where angling with a DFFE permit is allowed. Both Sealine threads agree: zeeQo (fishing-area.34028, 11 Nov 2010) says 'from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing', and Jo-Jo (western-seaboard-cape-town.54115, 30 Aug 2011, re-fetched 2 Nov 2026) says 'The cut-off is at the Kramat just before the 12 apostles hotel'. Even kRiLLin's stricter guess in the same thread, 'just past bakoven is the end point', puts the boundary south of Maiden's Cove. No official SANParks, City or DFFE page is in the evidence, so the zoning check rests on the task's reference list.

Evidence holds, and the quotes are accurate. The cached fishing-area.34028 summary confirms zeeQo, 12 Nov 2010: 'hottentot at Saunders Rock (Sea Point) and Maidens Cove in summer, using worm or mussel bait'. That is light bait fishing, which fits the light-tackle brief. The Jo-Jo quote 'I normally fish Saunder rock, Maidens cove and Backoven' was not in the evidence file, only the thread's search snippet. I re-fetched the thread and it is verbatim, but Jo-Jo names no species, bait or tackle. Both sources are 15-year-old forum posts.

The FishingBooker quote checks out. The page is 'Cape Town Fishing: The Complete Guide for 2026' by Lisa, updated 8 Jan 2026, and it says of Clifton Beach: 'You can enjoy surf fishing for species such as Galjoen, Kabeljou, and White Steenbras.' It never mentions Maiden's Cove, Glen Beach, Camps Bay or Bakoven. It is a generic guide written by a non-local, not a spot report.

No source names galjoen for Maiden's Cove. gotaway's line (16372, May 2009) is about Clifton 3rd Beach, 'seen gallies in gullies at clifton 3rd beach after big storms', which is a separate beach several hundred metres north beyond 4th Beach. The record's galjoen months [5,6,7,8,9] are made up: the source gives only 'after big storms', with no season.

No source names white steenbras for Maiden's Cove. gotaway's line is 'heard about steenbras at clifton 1st beach - middle of winter', about 1 km north. That is hearsay, and the months [6,7,8] come from that other beach.

Kob is not reported for Maiden's Cove either. The only line is 'heard about cob at camps bay/glen beach' (gotaway, 2009, hearsay). The method given, 'spinning' with paddle-tails and plugs at dusk, has no source. zeeQo actually says artificials had not worked for him in Cape Town.

species.size: Mostly 25-35 cm (0.3-0.8 kg), the odd fish over 40 cm; typical Cape shore hottentot, no size stated by the Maiden's Cove sources
species.bait: Worm or mussel on small hooks, fished tight to the kelp and gullies off the granite. The one angler who commented said artificial baits had not worked for him in Cape Town and he prefers real bait for the scent.
species.notes: The only species named for Maiden's Cove itself: zeeQo (Sealine, 12 Nov 2010) suggests 'hottentot at Saunders Rock (Sea Point) and Maidens Cove in summer, using worm or mussel bait'. Jo-Jo (Sealine, 30 Aug 2011) lists Maiden's Cove with Saunders Rock and Bakoven as his regular spots without naming a species.

name: Bakoven rocks
area: Bakoven / Camps Bay, Atlantic seaboard
coord_source: Nominatim query for "Bakoven Beach, Cape Town" on 2026-10-30 (OSM way, natural=beach): -33.9602392, 18.3731473, which matches the merge-step coordinates. The stand is the granite rocks either side of the Bakoven Beach cove; no source pinpoints the "palm tree" rocks zeeQo refers to, so the beach centroid is used.

access.note: Victoria Road (M6) runs directly above the cove; roadside parking and a short walk down between the bungalows. Approximate, not confirmed by any source in this pass.

bottom: Granite boulders and kelp reef with sand gullies, around a small sandy cove whose sand level shifts with the swell. Bakoven Rock offshore is listed as a dive site on the Wikipedia TMNP MPA page.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (the marine recreational fishing permit sold at Post Offices), which covers angling in the MPA's controlled zone; no SANParks fee on this stretch. Galjoen is subject to the national closed season (15 October to end of February, open 1 March to 14 October), a bag limit of 2 and a 35 cm minimum size; hottentot bag limit 10, minimum 22 cm. Those national limits are from the MLRA recreational regulations as remembered and were not re-checked against a DFFE page in this pass; forum posters only say the galjoen season opens in March. West Coast rock lobster needs its own permit and is out of scope.
legality: Allowed with permit. Bakoven cove (33°57.61'S, 18°22.39'E) is inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, which "extends from Mouille Point in the north west", but it is about 2.1 km north of the Karbonkelberg restricted (no-take) zone, whose northern limit is "offshore from the high-water mark between Oudekraal at S33°58.757'; E018°21.847'" and runs south to the Hout Bay Sentinel (Wikipedia TMNP MPA page, read 2026-10-30; same boundary in the 2004 regulations). Everything north of Oudekraal is controlled zone, where angling is allowed "on condition that one has a valid permit". Forum posters agree: "from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise sea point clifton camps bay bakoven alright 4 fishing" (zeeQo, Sealine 2010); "The cut-off is at the Kramat just before the 12 apostles hotel" (Jo-Jo, Sealine 2011); one 2011 poster (kRiLLin) thought the line was at Bakoven itself and admitted being "not very sure", but the official Oudekraal boundary puts the whole cove in the open zone.
description: Small granite-boulder cove and rocky points on Victoria Road between Camps Bay and Oudekraal, inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone and about 2 km north of the Karbonkelberg no-take boundary. Sealine anglers name it as the Atlantic seaboard's galjoen spot in winter ("Bakoven for gallies"; galjoen caught "at Bakoven in winter... by the palm tree"; "a couple of gallies maybe") and one of the places they go for hottentot, and a lure angler in 2013 had heard it was "ok" for drop-shot. It takes open Atlantic swell straight in, so hottentot are a calm-day fish here ("there can't be any swell") while the winter white water is the galjoen time.
hazards: Open Atlantic swell washing over the granite: a boat angler fishing off Bakoven says "there can't be any swell", and a Saunders Rock poster on the same seaboard warns to watch the ocean because waves wash over the rocks
Kelp and loose weed in the water fouling line and lures (posters note heavy seaweed behind the Camps Bay tidal pool next door)
Sand level in the cove shifts with the swell, changing where you can stand ("if all the sand is gone")
Cold Atlantic water and slippery granite (general, not from a source)
access_notes: Public shoreline on Victoria Road (M6) between Camps Bay and Oudekraal, inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone but outside the pay-at-the-gate Cape of Good Hope section, so no gate fee or hours apply. Sealine posters treat it as a quick option from the CBD and Sea Point side: Jo-Jo (2011) "normally fish Saunders Rock, Maidens Cove and Bakoven", and Occie (2015) calls it "Bakhoven just down the road" from Saunders Rock. Parking is roadside on Victoria Road (unverified). Merge-step OSRM free-flow estimate: 13 min from Green Point, 29 min from Westlake (2026-10-29). Sand level in the cove changes with the swell (JD, 2012: "don't know if the beach has washed open yet and if all the sand is gone").
unverified: Exact position of the "palm tree" rocks zeeQo fishes for galjoen; the stand is given as the Bakoven Beach cove
Parking and walk-in details and the access coordinates (Victoria Road roadside, approximate)
Galjoen closed season dates (15 Oct to end Feb) and the galjoen and hottentot bag and size limits, quoted from memory of the national regulations, not from a page read this pass
No source gives a tide preference for Bakoven; "any" records that absence, not an angler's statement
Depth (medium) and bottom detail beyond granite boulders, kelp and a sandy cove are inferred from the dive-site listing and the forum sand comment
Typical fish sizes for both species are general Cape figures, not Bakoven catches
Drop-shot suitability rests on one 2013 post that only says "I hear Bakoven, Kommetjie and Cape Point are ok" with no replies
The merge also cited https://sealine.co.za/threads/olifantsbos-guest-house.34177/ for this spot; it was not re-read and is not included in sources

issues: Legality holds. Bakoven, about S33 57.6, is roughly 2.1 to 2.3 km north of the Karbonkelberg no-take limit at Oudekraal (S33 58.757 E018 21.847, from the 2004 boundary in the task's reference list). That puts it in the TMNP MPA controlled zone, where angling is allowed with a DFFE permit and no SANParks fee applies. The cached Sealine 'Fishing area' thread (zeeQo 2010: "from oudekraal onwards you cant fish but otherwise ... bakoven alright 4 fishing"; angelos citing the MCM map: allowed north of Oudekraal) agrees. Nothing in the evidence shows a local bylaw or a no-fishing sign at Bakoven.

The Jo-Jo (2011) and kRiLLin (2011) quotes ('normally fish Saunders Rock, Maidens Cove and Bakoven', 'The cut-off is at the Kramat') come from https://sealine.co.za/threads/western-seaboard-cape-town.54115/. The 29 October cache only holds a search snippet for that thread, saying 'No answer is visible'. I could not check these quotes within budget, so they should be marked unverified or dropped. The Wikipedia TMNP MPA page and the Nominatim result are also missing from the cache, so they rest only on the writer's own 2026-10-30 reads.

Hottentot method 'dropshot and soft plastics also cast here' has no support for Bakoven. The only drop-shot mention is kravkof (2013), who asks a question with no replies, names no species and says only 'I hear Bakoven ... ok'. sparticus's dropshot was at Saunders Rock. zeeQo (2010) says artificials have not worked for him in Cape Town. The method should be light bait with small hooks only.

The shore evidence for hottentot at Bakoven is thin. It is one 2009 post (Jazz, in a 'where to catch the hotties' thread, re-fetched and confirmed: 'think the area is called bakeoven'). The 2014 poster who 'usually fish off Bakoven' does it from a small boat, which is out of scope. 'regular' abundance is overstated; 'occasional' fits better. The months [11,12,1,2,3] come from zeeQo's summer advice for Saunders Rock and Maidens Cove, not from Bakoven.

Galjoen at Bakoven is supported by four anglers. JD 2012 'Bakoven for gallies' and zeeQo 2010 'caught galjoen at Bakoven in winter' / 'by the palm tree' are in the cache. Occie 2015 'Bakhoven just down the road you could get a couple of gallies maybe' and Jazz 2009 'at bakeoven there have been rumors of the odd gallie too' were confirmed by re-fetch. Two of the four are hedged ('maybe', 'rumors of the odd gallie'), so 'regular' is generous; 'occasional' is more honest.
Galjoen months [5-9] leave out April. Both JD (2012, for a 27 April trip) and Occie (2015, for mid-April) recommend Bakoven in April, and the season is open from 1 March.

species.size: Not stated for Bakoven; Cape shore galjoen typically run 1-2 kg (35-45 cm, legal minimum 35 cm), with the odd fish over 3 kg (general figure, not from these sources).
species.bait: No Bakoven-specific bait is given. The Cape standards the same posters recommend buying for the area are white mussel and red bait (flippy, 2015), with worm or mussel bait the general advice for this seaboard (zeeQo, 2010); fish a small hook on light tackle.
species.notes: Four independent Sealine posters: JD (2012) "Bakoven for gallies"; zeeQo (2010) has caught galjoen at Bakoven in winter and suggests "Bakoven by the palm tree in winter"; Occie (2015) "Bakhoven just down the road you could get a couple of gallies maybe"; Jazz (2009) "at bakeoven there have been rumors of the odd gallie too". Closed season 15 October to end of February (national regulation, not re-checked this pass), bag limit 2, minimum 35 cm. Best in winter white water.

species.size: Not stated for Bakoven. On the same seaboard Saunders Rock hotties are "small but fun" (roughly 25-35 cm), with a 1.2 kg fish reported there in 2009.
species.method: light bait with small hooks; dropshot and soft plastics also cast here
species.bait: For hottentot on this seaboard posters use white mussel, sardine, coral worm or Berkley sandworm on size 1-4 hooks and light tackle because "hotties have small mouths" (sparticus, 2009, for Saunders Rock); zeeQo (2010) says worm or mussel and that artificials have not worked for him in Cape Town. No Bakoven-specific bait is given.
species.notes: Jazz (2009), answering where to catch hotties: "i either go to just the other side of camps bay think the area is called bakeoven" or the end of Beach Road, Sea Point. A 2014 poster who "usually fish off Bakoven" for hottentot does so from a small boat and says "there can't be any swell". Shore posters rate Saunders Rock and Maidens Cove higher for hottentot in summer (zeeQo 2010, Occie 2015). Bag limit 10, minimum 22 cm (national, not re-checked).

name: Hout Bay harbour wall
aka: Hout Bay harbour-side shore before the sewage works (Hangberg side)
Hout Bay Beach / Disa River mouth (leopard statue end)
area: Hout Bay
coord_source: Estimate, not a sourced pin: placed mid-way along the main (southern) breakwater using the harbour's position relative to OSM features (Harbour Road centroid -34.0492, 18.3455 on the harbour's north side; Hangberg/Harbour Heights -34.0563, 18.3431 to the south-west). Nominatim (30 Oct 2026, q=Hout Bay Harbour) returned only Harbour Road, Harbour Heights and a guest house, no breakwater; the merge pin (-34.0492, 18.3455) is Harbour Road, and mondo.surf's "Hout Bay Harbour Wall" pin (-34.0476, 18.3492) sits on the harbour's north shore. Verify the breakwater pin on a map before publishing; expect it within about 200 m.

access.note: Harbour Road at the west end of the harbour, by Snoekies fish market: 'Rather park at Snoekies and walk the short distance onto the wall' (will101, Sealine 2010). Coordinates are Nominatim's centroid of Harbour Road, within about 150 m of Snoekies. Do not park on the wall.

bottom: Concrete breakwater with rock/dolos armour at its foot; sand harbour floor inside the wall; reef and kelp outside (will101: a reef with "fat hottentot" reached by casting "exactly 70m out to sea" from 25 m back from the end of the southern wall; posters say to fish close to the kelp). The Hangberg-side shore stand is rocky with kelp ("kelp not too bad") and a round rock 60-80 m out.
permit: The harbour belongs to the Department of Public Works and Infrastructure; no official statement on angling from the walls was found, although anglers have fished them for decades. Follow the harbour master's signs and keep clear of working boats. The Karbonkelberg no-take zone starts on the Sentinel side of the bay, west of the harbour. DFFE recreational angling (marine) permit, bought at Post Office branches; no SANParks fee applies to this section of the MPA. Rod, reel and line only; standard DFFE bag and size limits (hottentot, bronze bream, kob). Posters say crayfish may not be netted from the wall ("No crayfishing allowed from Melkbos to Die Josie"), which is not checked here and is not an angling matter.
legality: Allowed with a permit. The harbour and the inner-bay shore east of the Sentinel lie in the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone: the Karbonkelberg restricted (no-take) zone runs "offshore from the high-water mark between Oudekraal at S33°58.757'; E018°21.847' and Hout Bay at S34°03.660'; E018°20.252'" (about -34.061, 18.338, at the seaward foot of the Sentinel, roughly 1 km south-west of the harbour), and "The remainder of the MPA is designated as a Controlled Area" where angling is allowed with a valid permit (Wikipedia TMNP MPA page quoting the regulations). Sealine posters agree: "i understand the mpa ends at fish on the rocks" and will101 describes a no-take zone starting 1 km from Fish on the Rocks with a boundary sign there. Western Cape Government: "You need a permit to fish along the shoreline" and "rod, reel and line only". Not found: any Hout Bay harbour-authority (DFFE/Public Works) rule on recreational angling from the breakwater; posters fished it in 2010 without mentioning a restriction.
description: Hout Bay's working fishing harbour under the Sentinel, with a long southern breakwater that anglers walk onto from Snoekies. Outside the wall the Sealine posters report hottentot, maasbanker, gurnard and the rare kob, while float-fished sardine inside the wall, cast toward the light tower on the North mole, gives "endless" 10-15 cm hottentot, "great fun for the kids"; a 2009 poster fished it "with my lighty". A second shore stand past the sewage works on the Hangberg side produces bigger hottentot (a 2.4 kg fish was released there in 2010), cast 60-80 m to a round rock just before the Karbonkelberg no-take boundary.
hazards: Working fishing harbour: trucks, forklifts, boats and fish-factory traffic on the quays; do not park on the wall
Big south-west swells break on and over the outer breakwater (the 'Hout Bay Harbour Wall' surf break works in big SW swells, winter, especially June); keep off the outer wall in a large swell

Personal safety: posters advise going in a group and not fishing alone; the Hangberg harbour area has a history of unrest (2018 protests; an undated DAFF notice diverted commercial landings from Hout Bay because of unrest)
Polluted water: City E. coli warnings for the Disa River mouth on the beach beside the harbour; a 2010 poster called the harbour water polluted
Broken concrete and debris where the wall begins on the right-hand side (raised by a poster in 2010)
Kelp outside the wall and along the Sentinel-side shore snags tackle; use a lighter sinker trace
Fishing past the sewage works puts you within about 100 m of the Karbonkelberg no-take boundary; stay on the harbour side of the sign
access_notes: Park at Snoekies on Harbour Road and walk onto the main (southern) breakwater; posters say not to park on the wall itself. Mondo.surf: "Parking and access are straightforward" because the spot is within the harbour area. It is a working DFFE fishing harbour with no stated hours or gate fee, but no official statement on recreational angling from the breakwater was found. Second stand: the harbour-side shore past the sewage works on the Hangberg side, reached by driving through the harbour residential area; cast 60-80 m to a dome/round rock (visible about 2 hours after high tide), and stay on the harbour side of the Karbonkelberg no-take boundary sign, which posters put about 1 km along the shore from Fish on the Rocks. Safety: "I'd suggest going in a group and not alone" (will101); speartackle also advises not fishing alone. Drive: no source gives a time; OSRM free-flow (2026-10-29) estimates 22 min from Westlake and 25 min from Green Point.
unverified: Whether the harbour authority (DFFE/Public Works, Hout Bay proclaimed fishing harbour) permits recreational angling from the breakwater: no official source found; posters simply fished it in 2010 and the thread does not answer the opening question 'Is fishing allowed off houtbay harbour wall'
Stand coordinates (-34.053, 18.347) are an estimate on the southern breakwater; Nominatim and mondo.surf gave only Harbour Road and a north-shore pin
Facing bearing of about 190 is estimated from the southern wall's orientation, not measured

No-take boundary sign at Fish on the Rocks and the zone starting about 1 km along the shore: poster statements from 2010, not checked against the gazette; the gazetted Karbonkelberg shore point is S34°03.660' E018°20.252'
Klipvis and gurnard at Hout Bay rest partly on a newcomer's list that lumps Hout Bay with Kalk Bay and Hermanus; shy sharks from the same list are noted here only

Generic listing pages (fishingreminder, fishingbooker, westerncape.gov.za) credit Hout Bay with yellowtail, snoek, elf, roman, geelbek and tuna; no angler report supports any of these from the harbour shore, and snoek and tuna are boat catches
Historical claims of white steenbras to 50 kg, yellowtail and cob 'back in the day' (will101, Slash) are nostalgia, not current
All shore reports are from 2009-2012; no recent catch report from the wall was found
Current security situation at the harbour and whether the DAFF landings diversion is still in force
The 8 kg kob 'taken in the bay' is not stated to have been caught from the shore

issues: Legality holds. The gazetted Karbonkelberg shore point is S34°03.660' E018°20.252' (about -34.061, 18.3375), and the record pin (-34.053, 18.347) is about 1.3 km north-east of it, inside the bay. Per the Wikipedia TMNP MPA page in the cache, the rest of the MPA is a Controlled Area where angling is 'allowed on condition that one has a valid permit'. speartackle agrees in sealine 52668 ('The entire area from the Sentinel Point to Oudekraal is a no take zone'), which puts the harbour on the controlled side. No SANParks fee applies here.

The core source cannot be checked against the cache: sealine.co.za/threads/houtbay-harbour-wall.28658 appears nowhere in the evidence file, which stopped at its 90 KB cap after 79 matching records. That thread is the source for every will101 and p49 quote, Snoekies parking, the North mole light, the float-fished sardine, 'great fun for the kids', maasbanker and gurnard from the wall, the 8 kg kob, bronze bream and the boundary sign at Fish on the Rocks. Thread 14482 ('launching from Hout Bay') is cached only as a search snippet: 'a paddle-ski angler mentions fishing off the harbour wall with light tackle... cut off before naming species or bait'. That snippet does support the 'with my lighty' line, but not 'there is cob in the bay' or the mullet at the river mouth. Thread 58286 is also snippet-only. These details may be genuine, since the record author fetched other pages after the cache date, but this pass could not confirm them.

Angling evidence in the cache still clears the bar, but it is mostly for the Hangberg-side shore stand, not the wall. In speartackle (52668, 2011) the hottentot are 'just before the sewerage plant at the far end of the harbour side', cast about 60 m to a round rock. In 44419 (2010) he reports a 2.4 kg hottentot released 'past the sewage treatment plant', cast about 5 m short of a dome rock roughly 80 m out. In 61809 (2012) he fishes 'towards the Sentinel, past Hout Bay Harbour' with white mussel. Casting 60-80 m with a sinker to a reef rock is medium bottom tackle rather than light tackle. Only the float fishing inside the wall (in the uncached 28658) and the 14482 snippet are clearly light tackle.

The record leaves out negative reports from the cache. In 44419, speartackle says the area holds 'precious little' and BigBen (Dec 2010) says fishing there is poor, with plenty of crayfish. The thread 'Harbour Fishing' (29176), which asks for sheltered light-tackle spots at Hout Bay harbour, has 0 replies. Rating hottentot 'common' ignores this.

The two speartackle posts disagree on the location ('just before' the sewage plant in 52668, 'past' it in 44419) and on the distance (about 60 m vs about 80 m). The record uses 'past' throughout and merges the two distances into '60-80 m'.

The hazard saying that fishing past the sewage works 'puts you within about 100 m of the Karbonkelberg no-take boundary' has no source. No cached page gives that distance. The gazetted shore point is at the seaward foot of the Sentinel, roughly 1 km south-west of the harbour. The claims of a boundary sign 'about 1 km from Fish on the Rocks' and 'the mpa ends at fish on the rocks' come from the uncached 28658. Read literally, the second would put the stand past the sewage works inside the restricted zone, so the two poster statements conflict with each other. The gazette point is what should be shown.

species.size: Inside the wall, toward the North mole light, hottentot of 100-150 mm; outside the wall and on the reef 70 m off the end of the southern wall 'fat hottentot', with 2 kg-plus fish reported years back and a 2.4 kg fish released at the Hangberg-side shore stand in 2010
species.method: light bait: sardine under a float inside the wall; light bottom rig near kelp outside
species.bait: Sardine on a float ('sardine float bait', p49); white mussel (speartackle); general hotties baits from the Sealine hotties thread: prawn, pilchard, worms, white mussel, redbait on long-shank 1/0-2/0 hooks, fished close to the kelp
species.notes: will101 (2010): outside the wall for hottentot and maasbanker; inside the wall, casting toward the North mole light tower, 'great fun for the kids'. speartackle (2011): 'You can land some FAAAT hotties just before the sewerage plant at the far end of the harbour side', casting about 60 m to a round rock visible about 2 hours after high tide. Roper (2010): big hottentot in the area, usually caught on fish bait. No source gives a season; p49 suggests a fresh south-easter brings fish back.

species.size: Not stated by sources
species.bait: Sardine fished on the bottom: 'Sinking the bait brings many gurnards' (p49)
species.notes: Named by p49 and will101 in the harbour-wall thread, and by a 2011 newcomer who lists gurnard among catches at Kalk Bay, Hermanus and Hout Bay. No season stated.

species.size: Not stated by sources; a small fish, typically 20-30 cm
species.bait: Not stated separately; the thread's rig is sardine under a float, which also takes maasbanker. Small pilchard strips on small hooks.
species.notes: will101 (2010): outside the wall for hottentot and maasbanker. A 2011 newcomer lists maasbanker among catches at Kalk Bay, Hermanus and Hout Bay. No season stated.

species.size: Not stated by sources
species.bait: Not stated by sources
species.notes: Slash recalls 'bronsies and cob, back in the day'; will101 (Jan 2010) says bronsies are still present. No catch report with size or bait.

name: Kommetjie (the Kom)
aka: Kommetjie: the Kom and Slangkop rocks
area: Kommetjie
coord_source: Stand = the rock shelf at the foot of the Slangkop lighthouse; coordinates are the lighthouse's own, from https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slangkop_Lighthouse (34°08′55.0″S 18°19′10.0″E = -34.148611, 18.319444), fetched 30 October 2026. A Nominatim query for "Slangkop Lighthouse Kommetjie" returned an empty result. The Kom basin itself (the slipway bay in front of the village, roughly -34.137, 18.326) and the lighthouse parking position are from the researcher's map knowledge and are unverified; the merge step's -34.1403, 18.3292 is the Wikipedia town centre, not a stand.

access.note: Roadside parking on Lighthouse Road beside the Slangkop lighthouse, then the wooden boardwalk down to the lighthouse and the rocks. Position approximate (map knowledge, unverified). For the Kom, Beach Road runs along the basin and the crayfish-factory slipway has tarred parking.

bottom: Rock and reef with thick kelp (Wikipedia: "wherever the bottom is rocky, the shallower waters are thick with giant kelp forests"); sand in the Kom basin and towards Long Beach to the north.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (annual or temporary, bought at the Post Office) for rod-and-line fishing from the shore. Crayfish (West Coast rock lobster) needs its own recreational permit and is limited to open-season days ("open from November to April on certain days" per kommetjie.org). National galjoen rules (bag limit, minimum size and the closed season from mid-October to the end of February) apply but are not in the cached sources; check current DFFE regulations.
legality: Allowed with a permit. The shoreline lies inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone: the Wikipedia MPA page places "the Kommetjie small-craft site inside the MPA, and no restricted zone is described there". The nearest no-take zones are Karbonkelberg, which ends at Hout Bay (S34°03.660' E018°20.252'), and Cape of Good Hope, whose northern edge is Schusters Bay Point at Scarborough (S34°16.490' E018°22.194'); the Slangkop lighthouse at S34°08.9' E018°19.2' lies between them. It is outside the SANParks Cape of Good Hope pay section, so no entry fee or activity permit applies. The Western Cape government page says "You need a permit to fish along the shoreline" and "You need to use a rod, reel and line only". A 2015 Sealine thread reports conflicting "no fishing" signs between Baileys and Soetwater, but no source places a restriction at Kommetjie.
description: Kelp-fringed rock on the open Atlantic side of the Peninsula: the Kom is the shallow reef-and-kelp basin in front of Kommetjie village with the small-craft slipway, and the Slangkop lighthouse rocks are about a kilometre south along Lighthouse Road. Sealine anglers treat it as a lure and light-bait shore spot: a drop-shot angler had heard "Bakoven, Kommetjie and Cape Point are ok", a spoon-and-plastics angler touring the Peninsula in 2010 found "too much seaweed", and a regular who had "gone there for years collecting wonder worm" recommends Kommetjie/Soetwater over Noordhoek to a light-tackle visitor after hottentot and galjoen. The Melkbosstrand galjoen derby area runs "from Kommetjie Light House to Ysterfontein Harbour wall", so winter galjoen on bait is the obvious target, with hottentot in the shallow kelp water.
hazards: Open Atlantic swell and surge on the lighthouse rocks; Sealine posters call the Kommetjie side rough in a strong north-westerly.
Thick kelp and drifting seaweed snag lures and foul lines: Kommetjie had "too much seaweed" on a 2010 lure tour, and kelp covers the water at times along this stretch.
A strong south-easter can end a session ("the Cape Doctor arrived and literally blew us off the beach"); cold water and slippery kelp-covered rock are the usual Atlantic-side cautions.
An active crayfish-poaching coast with compliance patrols (poachers arrested at nearby Soetwater): carry your DFFE permit.
access_notes: Kommetjie is reached on Kommetjie Road (M65) from Sun Valley, or over Chapman's Peak Drive (toll, closes in bad weather) from Hout Bay. For the lighthouse rocks, park on Lighthouse Road beside the Slangkop lighthouse and take the wooden boardwalk down; the lighthouse is a tourist attraction, no gate or entry fee (outside the SANParks pay section). For the Kom, Beach Road runs along the basin, and the crayfish-factory slipway had a "new slipway and tarred parking" in 2010. Bait: wonder worm is collected locally; white mussel and red bait are easier to buy in Fish Hoek or Simon's Town (posters name the Fish Hoek "Great White" shop), and bait is "very hard to come by" around Noordhoek. Most visitors come for crayfish, which needs its own permit and open-season days.
unverified: The Kom basin coordinates (about -34.137, 18.326) and the lighthouse parking position are from map knowledge, not a source; only the lighthouse itself is sourced.
Hottentot from the shore at the Kom or lighthouse rocks: the sources give boat reports of hottentot in shallow water off Kommetjie and a light-tackle recommendation, not a shore catch.
Galjoen at the lighthouse rocks specifically: supported only by the derby boundary, a Sealine recommendation and a regional winter report.
White steenbras and stumpnose as shore (rather than boat) catches: the government page is ambiguous.
Which species lure anglers take here: the drop-shot and spoon posts name none.
Tide preference (pushing) is inferred from the neighbouring Soetwater report of fishing the incoming tide behind the kelp and rock shelf (sealine thread 53665), not from a Kommetjie statement.
Facing bearing (250) and exposed shelter are from map geometry; the Kom basin is partly sheltered by its reef and kelp (described as a safe harbour for small craft).
Typical sizes are general Cape ranges; no source gives sizes for this spot.
Galjoen closed season and bag limit are national regulations not present in the cache.
Snoek and yellowtail are named for Kommetjie waters by tourism and boat sources; no shore catch reported, so they are left off the species list.
flippy's attached photos (kommetjie.jpg, kommetjie 2.jpg) marking the recommended spot could not be viewed.

issues: Legality holds. The cached Wikipedia TMNP MPA page (opened 29 Oct 2026) says 'Kommetjie: Controlled... no restricted zone is described there'. The nearest no-take zones are Karbonkelberg, which ends at Hout Bay (S34 03.660), and Cape of Good Hope. The record puts that zone's northern end at Schusters Bay Point (S34 16.490); the task reference puts it at Olifantsbos. Both are about 12 km or more south of the lighthouse (S34 08.9), so the difference does not matter. The record is also right that the site is outside the SANParks pay section. The westerncape.gov.za permit quotes are verbatim in the cache. One small gap: the rocks just south of the lighthouse run into Soetwater, a City of Cape Town resort with a gate (sealine Soetwater search: 'gathered at the gate'; 'entrance as Slangkop Road'). The record does not mention this possible City gate or fee.

The record's strongest 'light tackle' claim is misdescribed. The 'fishing-cape-town-april.89025' thread, which is not in the evidence file (it fell past the 90 KB cap), was fetched on 2 Nov 2026. The original poster (200ts) planned 'a Poseidon light 3-5 ounce stick', which is a light surf rod casting 3-5 oz sinkers, not light tackle in this project's sense. flippy's post reads 'i know kommetjie/soetwater far better having gone there for years collecting wonder worm and the spot id recommend'. That is collecting bait plus a recommendation, not a fishing report. The spot he marked is only in an attached photo and may be Soetwater rather than the Kom. Nobody in the thread reports fishing or a catch at Kommetjie. Occie's 'Lots of hotties but ive never heard of galjoen there' refers to Saunders Rock/Noordhoek, not Kommetjie.

The lure evidence is weak or negative. sealine 78843 is a single unanswered post: 'I hear Bakoven, Kommetjie and Cape Point are ok' (hearsay, with no species, lures or replies). sealine 33033 is a lure angler who found that Kommetjie 'had too much seaweed'. The cache excerpt does not support the record's 'spoon-and-plastics angler', which is only a search snippet. Evidence is not refuted, because the Melkbosstrand galjoen derby area running 'from Kommetjie Light House' plus these posts are angling-specific. Still, no source reports a shore catch at the Kom or the lighthouse rocks.

Coordinates hold for the lighthouse rocks. A Nominatim reverse geocode of -34.148611, 18.319444 (fetched 2 Nov 2026) returns 'Slankop lighthouse, Lighthouse Road, Soet Water' at -34.1486088, 18.3195128. The OSM object is tagged amenity/parking. So the 'stand' is really the lighthouse car park, a few tens of metres from the rock shelf, which is acceptable. However, the point is about 1.2 km from the Kom basin (about -34.137, by map knowledge), so it does not land on 'the Kom' that leads the name. OSM also places the point in the Soet Water area, which means this stand overlaps the neighbouring Soetwater shore. If a separate Soetwater record exists, check for a duplicate.
