Hottentot: abundance 'regular' and months 1-12 are invented. The only Kommetjie mentions are boat-based. sealine 64186 is a rubber-duck skipper asking where to find 'hotties' in shallow water, which is a question, not a report. In sealine 52668, Irie ivan suggests boating 'toward Kommetjie and Scarborough' for snoek and hottentot. The 200ts/Occie hottentot talk is about Saunders Rock/Noordhoek. Keep the species, since the sources tie it to Kommetjie waters, but mark the abundance as unverified or occasional and drop the month list.

Galjoen: 'regular' and months 5-9 are regional inference. The jacita June 2025 report covers 'Cape Town to Hangklip', and the derby gives a boundary only. The record cites fishingreminder.com for galjoen, but that page lists galjoen for Cape Point and Table Bay. Its only Kommetjie mention is in the Hout Bay entry ('consistent shore and kayak catches'), with no species, so it should not be cited as galjoen support for Kommetjie.

species.size: Not stated for this spot. Cape shore galjoen are typically 30-45 cm (1-2 kg), with the odd fish over 50 cm.
species.bait: Red bait, white mussel or wonder worm on a small hook under a light sinker; the regional June 2025 report says "Bring red bait, white mussels, or worms".
species.notes: Winter fish. The Melkbosstrand Angling Club galjoen derby area runs "from Kommetjie Light House to Ysterfontein Harbour wall" (28 July 2018), and a Sealine regular steers a light-tackle galjoen/hottentot visitor to Kommetjie/Soetwater. No catch report from the lighthouse rocks themselves. National bag limit, minimum size and closed season (mid-October to end-February) apply; check current DFFE regulations.

species.size: Not stated for this spot; pan-size 25-35 cm is usual on the Peninsula's kelp rocks, with 2 kg+ fish reported on reefs off Hout Bay by boat.
species.bait: Red bait, white mussel, chokka or wonder worm on small hooks; small paddle-tails on a dropshot rig in the kelp gaps.
species.notes: Boat anglers target "hotties in shallow water" off Kommetjie and run "toward Kommetjie and Scarborough" for snoek and hottentot; a light-tackle visitor hoping for hottentot and galjoen was pointed to Kommetjie/Soetwater. Shore catches at the Kom itself are inferred from these, not reported. No seasonal statement in the sources.

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: White mussel, wonder worm or sand prawn on a small hook.
species.notes: The Western Cape government fishing page lists "Kommetjie Bay: white steenbras, stumpnose, tuna and albacore by boat" without saying which are shore catches. A surf species, most likely on the sand of Long Beach north of the Kom rather than on the kelp rocks. No season given.

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: White mussel or wonder worm on a small hook.
species.notes: Listed as "stumpnose" for Kommetjie Bay by the Western Cape government page, shore or boat unspecified; sandy ground in the Kom basin and towards Long Beach.

name: Soetwater
area: Kommetjie, Atlantic side of the Cape Peninsula
coord_source: Nominatim/OSM "Soetwater Tidal Pool" (way, leisure/swimming_pool, De Anker Road, Soet Water), queried 2026-10-30; the stand is taken as the rock ledges beside the tidal pool inside the resort. The resort gate on Lighthouse Road was not separately geocoded.
bottom: Flat rocky banks and low ledges with dense kelp beds, kelp gullies and sand patches; two artificial tidal pools on the shore. "Dense kelp beds line the shore" (City of Cape Town); "the seaweed is in abundance" and hooked fish go "straight for the rocks" (Sealine, 2013).
permit: DFFE recreational marine angling permit (post office). Resort access: the City refers bookings and tariffs to its Recreation and Parks Tariffs Booklet, so expect a day-visitor fee (amount unconfirmed). Species rules to check against current DFFE limits: galjoen closed season 15 October to end of February and bag limit 2; white steenbras 1 per day, minimum 60 cm. No boat launching from Soetwater.
legality: Allowed with a permit. Soetwater lies on the Atlantic side of the peninsula between Slangkop lighthouse and Witsand, inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA but outside every restricted zone in the 2004 regulations (Karbonkelberg ends at the Hout Bay Sentinel well to the north; the Cape of Good Hope restricted zone starts at Hoek van die Bobbejaan/Olifantsbos well to the south), so it is a controlled zone where angling is allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit. The City of Cape Town's Soetwater Beach page (fetched 2026-10-30) lists "Fishing and angling" among the activities, and Sealine threads record SSEC:WC club competitions held from the resort (2013 to 2015). Boat launching from Soetwater is not permitted (Western Cape Government, via cached search summary). Not in the Cape of Good Hope section, so no SANParks entry fee or activity permit applies, but the resort itself is gated.
description: Gated resort on Lighthouse Road immediately south of Slangkop lighthouse at Kommetjie, with flat rock ledges, dense kelp beds and two artificial tidal pools facing the open Atlantic. Shore anglers fish light bait tackle off the ledges and kelp gullies for galjoen in winter and white steenbras and stumpnose in the warmer months, and the resort has long been an SSEC:WC club competition venue. Kelp makes lure fishing hard, big kob and gully sharks turn up in summer, and the spot gets crowded on good weekends.
hazards: Dense kelp and seaweed: constant snags, lost sinkers and traces, and hooked fish bury themselves in the weed and rocks (the 2013 report "lost many sinkers, many traces" and fished until the sinkers ran out).

Open Atlantic swell onto low flat ledges; on big-swell days anglers fish the kelp-sheltered rock shelf and watch the sets (2011 report fished large swells on the incoming tide, sheltered by kelp beds and a rock shelf).
Crowded on good weekends and club competition days ("Soetwater was very crowded", 2010).
December is a poor month here ("not recommended in December", 2018 thread).
Snakes in the coastal scrub and driftwood: a 2011 trip report is titled "Galjoen and the Cape Cobra".
Gated resort: confirm gate hours with the district office before an early or late session.
access_notes: Resort gate on Lighthouse Road (Slangkop Road) just south of Slangkop lighthouse; park inside the resort by the tidal pools and walk over flat rock to the ledges. Gate position not geocoded. Soetwater Resort, Lighthouse Road, Kommetjie, immediately south of Slangkop lighthouse. Drive through the resort gate and park inside; the City lists parking, toilets, two artificial tidal pools, picnic and braai areas, disability access, and camping and caravan sites, with bookings and tariffs through the Recreation and Parks Tariffs Booklet (general enquiries 021 444 6769 / 021 444 6770, district office 021 788 1929). A day-visitor fee is likely but the amount and gate hours are unconfirmed: both westerncape.gov.za facility pages returned 404 on 2026-10-30. Short walk over flat rock from the car park to the ledges and kelp gullies. SSEC:WC club comps have met at the gate on winter mornings and started fishing around 07:30. No boat launching from Soetwater (ramps at Kommetjie and Witsand). Bait is hard to come by locally; nearest tackle shops named are Great White (Main Road, Fish Hoek) and Brays (Muizenberg).
unverified: Resort day-visitor fee and gate hours: https://www.westerncape.gov.za/facility/soetwater-resort and https://d7.westerncape.gov.za/facility/soetwater-resort both returned 404 on 2026-10-30; the City page only points to the Recreation and Parks Tariffs Booklet.
Merge note that a 37 cm galjoen won the SSEC:WC July 2014 competition at Soetwater Resort: the cached thread excerpt names no species and the full thread was rate-limited on 29 October 2026.
Galjoen closed season (15 Oct to end Feb), bag limit 2, and white steenbras 1 per day / 60 cm minimum are quoted from the national recreational regulations as remembered, not from a cached page.

Best months per species are inferred from the dates of the forum reports (galjoen trips April to August; steenbras October and January; stumpnose January; kob "summer"), not from a seasonal guide for this spot.
Facing bearing (245) and shallow depth are read off the map and the shoreline description, not stated by any source.
No source reports a lure-caught fish at Soetwater; lure fishing on this stretch is reported only negatively (kelp-heavy, 2013 lure thread), so spinning here is unproven.
The stand coordinate is the Soetwater tidal pool; the exact ledges and gullies anglers prefer within the resort are not described in the sources.

issues: The record's main evidence is wrong. The reason field says the Jan 2013 kRiLLin light-tackle trip (1/0 hook, 4 oz sinker, white mussel) 'produced white steenbras, stumpnose and galjoen'. I re-fetched the full thread (https://sealine.co.za/threads/schooled-in-scratching.71930/) on 2026-11-02. He fished Soetwater from 16:30 to about 20:30 and landed nothing. Fish were hooked and lost in the kelp and rocks, and he lost sinkers and traces until he ran out. The line 'steenies, stumpnose, and galjoen ... caught on this bait' is from a later post (Jan 12) about how he rigs mussel, and it is not tied to Soetwater.

That leaves one light-tackle report for Soetwater, and it caught nothing. Kelp beat the light gear. The 2013 lure thread (https://sealine.co.za/threads/lure-fishing-the-surf.80509/) calls the Soetwater/Kommetjie stretch kelp-heavy or poor. No lure catch is reported anywhere. The light-tackle fit is therefore weak, though the evidence is not refuted: the krillin report does describe light bait fishing from shore here.

Kob: Pslatarix's 15 kg PB kob 'was caught there' (Soetwater area), but he fished 'shimmi exage with 8oz tip' in summer. That is rock-and-surf weight gear, not light bait as the record's method says. The record's 'tackle up' paraphrase hides this.

White stumpnose: no source ties it to Soetwater. The only mention is kRiLLin's general bait-rigging post, not about Soetwater. The Western Cape Government page is cited for Kommetjie Bay, which the record itself admits is not Soetwater. That page is also not in the cached evidence.

White steenbras is supported for the spot: a 9 kg fish in Oct 2009 (https://sealine.co.za/threads/soetwater-and-steenies.24975/). But the bait and rig attributed to it ('strip or whole white mussel on a 1/0 hook with a 4 oz sinker') come from the fishless 2013 trip. The 2009 report gives no bait. Mengs' 'heard its good for steenies?' is a question with no location.

Galjoen at Soetwater is thinly supported. There is a 2011 galjoen trip excerpt (Galjoen and the Cape Cobra) with no catch, bait or conditions stated. The 2013 'Galjoen' thread is only a plan to fish here. The 2010 'Soetwater.' thread is about galjoen being speared, which is spearfishing, not angling. The galjoen bait note ('as in the 2013 report') implies a galjoen catch on that trip, and there was none.

species.size: Pan-size fish of 1 to 2 kg are typical; bigger ones come in rough winter water. Sizes are not stated in the cached Soetwater reports.
species.bait: White mussel (whole mussel twirled onto a 1/0 hook and tied with cotton, as in the 2013 report); red bait and worms are the usual Western Cape galjoen baits.
species.notes: Winter target: Sealine galjoen trips to Soetwater are planned for April to August. kRiLLin (Jan 2013): "I decide to take some light tackle with ... First cast, 1/0 hook, 4 ounce sinker" and "steenies, stumpnose, galjoen, caught all of these on this bait". Kelp-covered water puts galjoen off (2010 thread asks for a kelp-free spot); a 2008 thread says the Atlantic side from Bakoven to Misty Cliffs fishes well after heavy swells. Closed season 15 Oct to end Feb (check DFFE).

species.size: Mostly small fish under the 60 cm legal size, with the odd big one: a 9 kg fish was landed here in October 2009 and a larger fish lost for want of a gaff.
species.bait: Strip or whole white mussel on a 1/0 hook with a 4 oz sinker (2013 report); mussel is said to be "good for steenies".
species.notes: Dated reports are October (2009) and January (2013), so the months are inferred, not stated. Bag limit 1, minimum 60 cm (check DFFE). The Western Cape Government fishing page lists white steenbras and stumpnose for "Kommetjie Bay", the sandy bay north of the lighthouse, rather than Soetwater itself.

species.size: Big fish possible: a 15 kg personal-best kob was reported here; most are taken on bait by anglers who have tackled up for summer.
species.bait: Mussel, mussel and kreef, or mussel and chokka (Pslatarix); no paddle-tail or dropshot catches are reported here and a 2013 lure thread calls this stretch kelp-heavy or poor for lures.
species.notes: Pslatarix (Jan 2013): "my pb kob of 15 kg was caught there and they box hard!" and "when fishing this area in summer i always tackle up". Sharks on bait, kept out of the species list: "there are plenty spotties around that area" (spotted gully sharks, the biggest about 20 kg on mussel) and "if its dead you'll only get skaamies" (shysharks).

name: Misty Cliffs
area: Misty Cliffs / Scarborough, Atlantic side of the Cape Peninsula
coord_source: Nominatim village relation 11643228 "Misty Cliffs" (-34.1846150, 18.3644011; bounding box -34.18659 to -34.18221, 18.35927 to 18.36637), re-queried 2026-10-30 and identical to the rough merge-step node, so the merge coordinates are kept. The village straddles the M65 and the ledges and gullies lie directly below the road on the west side within about 150 m; no angler-supplied coordinates for the actual stand exist.

access.note: Roadside parking along the M65 (Main Road) through the village; the City of Cape Town lists parking as the beach's only facility but gives no position, so the exact lay-by is not sourced.

bottom: Rock ledges and foamy gullies with kelp, boulders and rock pools; a sand bank about 120 m off the ledges; a small beach at the Witsand end of the village ("closer to the beginning of Misty's, where the beach is").
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (Marine Living Resources Act, sold at Post Offices). Galjoen: closed season 15 October to end February (cached posts confirm the season "opens" in March and was closed in February), bag limit 2, minimum size 35 cm. White steenbras: bag limit 1, minimum size 60 cm. The limits and exact dates come from the national recreational regulations and were not confirmed from a cached page in this pass.
legality: Allowed with a permit. Misty Cliffs (S34 11.08, E018 21.86) is on the Atlantic coast of the Table Mountain National Park MPA between the Karbonkelberg restricted zone (ends at the Hout Bay Sentinel, about 20 km north) and the Cape of Good Hope restricted zone (starts at Olifantsbos, about 9 km south), so it is in the controlled zone where shore angling is allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit; the reserve fence at Schuster's Bay (S34 12.27) is also south of it. The City of Cape Town's own Misty Cliffs Beach page lists "Fishing and angling" as the beach's activity (fetched 2026-10-30), and the SSEC:WC club held shore competitions here in August 2013 and July 2014 (Sealine). It is outside the Cape of Good Hope section of the park, so no SANParks gate fee or activity permit applies. Galjoen closed season applies.
description: A string of rock ledges and foamy gullies below the M65 at the small village of Misty Cliffs, between Scarborough and Witsand on the Atlantic side of the peninsula. Sealine anglers know it as a galjoen venue: "one of the fishing spots I know of for Galjoen" (Wayne, 2011), "some very big gallies out Misty Cliffs way" (Captain Sparrow, 2013), fished with fresh white mussel on light bait tackle into the white water, "look for a nice gully with lots of foamy water moving in and out. Short casts only." It is "normally a high tide spot" that "runs deep very quickly", takes the full south-west swell, is kelp-heavy, and nobody reports lure fishing here: "I have never heard of much other than Galjoen coming out of Misty Cliffs" (Sealine, 2013).
hazards: Open Atlantic swell breaking onto the ledges: "please be very careful here as the waves can get pretty hectic onto the rocks" (Captain Sparrow, Sealine 2013); the rough days galjoen anglers want are the dangerous ones
Kelp beds foul lures and line; Misty Cliffs to Noordhoek is described as kelp-heavy or poor for lures (Sealine, 2013)
Wet, slippery rock ledges and boulders; the water "runs deep very quickly" off the ledges (Sealine, 2011)
Scout the gullies at low tide before fishing the push, and keep casts short
Frequent sea mist ("its always misty there") and cold water; no lifeguards listed
The City's Witsands page next door warns of powerful waves and rip currents, so do not wade
access_notes: Park in the roadside lay-bys along the M65 (Main Road) through the village; the City of Cape Town lists parking as the only facility, no toilets or lifeguards, and notes the shore is rocky with boulders and "access is limited within the village", so you walk down short paths between the houses to the ledges. No gate and no fee stated. Reach it from Westlake over Ou Kaapse Weg to Kommetjie and south through Witsand, or from Simon's Town over Red Hill ("its along the mountain when travelling from red hill to kommetjie"). Other spots lie "closer to the beginning of Misty's, where the beach is (not the one by the kreef factory)". Galjoen season only, 1 March to 14 October.
unverified: Exact galjoen closed-season dates (15 Oct to end Feb), bag limit 2 and 35 cm minimum, and the white steenbras limits, are from the national recreational regulations; cached posts only say the season opens in March and was closed in February
Which lay-by on the M65 anglers use and the exact path down to the ledges; the stand coordinates are the Nominatim village node, not a surveyed stand
That the SSEC:WC competitions held here (2013, 2014) were rock-and-surf bait events; the cached competition snippets give no species or tackle
Typical galjoen size here: "some very big gallies" (2013) is the only size statement
The facing bearing of about 235 degrees and the medium depth are read from the coastline and from "runs deep very quickly", not from a surveyed source
Drive times are OSRM free-flow estimates, not an angler's statement
The claim that lure fishing is poor here rests on one 2013 Sealine thread; no page reports anyone trying lures or fly at Misty Cliffs

issues: Legality holds. At -34.1846, 18.3644 (S34 11.08 E018 21.86, a correct conversion), Misty Cliffs lies on the Atlantic side between Witsand and Scarborough. That is south of the Karbonkelberg restricted zone (which ends at the Hout Bay Sentinel) and north of the Cape of Good Hope restricted zone (Olifantsbos and further south), so it is in the TMNP MPA controlled zone. The City of Cape Town's Misty Cliffs Beach entry lists 'Activities: Fishing and angling' with the M65 address (WebSearch snippet in the cache). Small fix: the Hout Bay Sentinel is about 14-15 km north in a straight line, not 'about 20 km' (20 km only works if measured along the coast). The Schuster's Bay fence point (S34 12.27) does not appear anywhere in the cache and was not checked.

Both key thread quotes were re-fetched on 2026-11-02 and are accurate. sealine 51014: Wayne 30 May 2011 ('one of the fishing spots I know of for Galjoen', 'normaly a high tide spot', 'runs deep very quickly', 'all round spot high or low', 'where the beach is (not the one by the kreef factory)'); FISHWORX ('its along the mountain when travelling from red hill to kommetjie', 'its always misty there'); lushwill 31 May 2011 ('white mussell is all you really need there', 'some wonderworm maybe', sand bank about 120 m out, steenbras on fresh prawns). sealine 76420: Captain Sparrow 21 Jun 2013 (every quoted line, including 'Short casts only' and 'low to high tide'). Note that the 29 October cache had none of these threads' text: the 76420 fetch hit a session limit, and 51014 only appeared as a search snippet. These quotes were therefore unverified until this pass.

The 'white steenbras' species entry is not supported as written. lushwill says only 'steenbras', and in one reply ('if you can cast that far you could pic up a steenbras... with fresh prawns'), so 'white' is an inference. More importantly, a 120 m cast to a sand bank is rock-and-surf distance, outside the site's light-tackle scope. Drop the entry, or at most mention it in the notes.

The galjoen bait list includes 'red bait', but no Misty Cliffs source names it. Red bait appears only in a beginner thread that names no location (sealine 34834 snippet) and in the regional Jacita July 2025 report. Misty Cliffs sources give fresh white mussel (lushwill, Captain Sparrow), wonderworm (lushwill), dug worms (Wayne) and freeze-dried bloodworm (BOF, a plan, not a catch).

The record calls the tackle 'light bait tackle', but no source states any tackle: both threads say nothing about rod, line, hook or sinker. The light-tackle fit is an inference from 'Short casts only' into foamy gullies. That inference is reasonable, but the record should not present it as sourced.

The reason field says an SSEC:WC club competition names Misty Cliffs 'as a shore galjoen venue'. The cached competition snippets (84820, 77818, 77652) give no species or tackle at all, so they show only that club competitions were held there in Aug 2013 and Jul 2014.

species.size: Not stated beyond "some very big gallies out Misty Cliffs way" (2013); Cape shore galjoen are typically 1 to 2 kg, with a 35 cm minimum size
species.bait: Fresh white mussel ("white mussell is all you really need there"), red bait, wonderworm or bloodworm (a 2013 beginner planned freeze-dried Australian bloodworm); small hooks, short casts into foamy gullies
species.notes: The spot's target species. Wayne (30 May 2011): "one of the fishing spots I know of for Galjoen", "normaly a high tide spot" but "an all round spot high or low" as it "runs deep very quickly". Captain Sparrow (21 Jun 2013): "Best time is when the NW wind is blowing False bay flattish, which usually roughs up the Misty Cliff side. The rougher the better"; "Look for a nice gully with lots of foamy water moving in and out. Short casts only"; "I like fishing from low to high tide, so I can check for those gullies while still lowish." Open season 1 March to 14 October; trips and club competitions reported April to August. A 2013 lure thread: "I have never heard of much other than Galjoen coming out of Misty Cliffs."

name: Scarborough beach
aka: Schuster's Bay (the bay south of the beach, fishable only north of the reserve fence)
area: Scarborough, Cape Peninsula (Atlantic side, south of Misty Cliffs)
coord_source: Nominatim/OSM way 222096831 "Scarborough Beach" (natural=beach) centroid, queried 2026-10-30. The merge step's -34.1983, 18.3756 was the Wikipedia village centre, up the hill from the sand. No car-park coordinate was verified.
bottom: Sand beach with mussel-covered rock banks and reef at either end, kelp beds beyond the break; sand holes scour out between the banks after a big swell ("North wind over last few days has made sea rough out Scarborough way ... This has started to clean out some holes").
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (Marine Living Resources Act): the MPA page says extraction in the controlled zone is allowed "on condition that one has a valid permit" for angling. National galjoen rules apply: closed season 15 October to end February (finder note; a forum poster planned to be "heading that way in March when Gallie Season opens"). Bag and size limits for galjoen and white steenbras are national rules not found in the evidence (see unverified). No SANParks activity permit or gate fee outside the reserve fence.
legality: Allowed with a permit. The beach is inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone. The Cape of Good Hope restricted (no-take) zone begins at Schusters Bay Point, Scarborough (S34 12.271 E018 22.194, about -34.2045, 18.3699) and runs south to Hoek van die Bobbejaan, with its seaward edge running due south from that point (2004 regulation text as cached from Wikipedia on 29 October 2026); the older 1998 reg 10(f)(i) closed area likewise started at "the boundary fence of the Cape of Good Hope Nature Reserve at Schuster Bay, Scarborough" (acts.co.za, cached). The beach centroid (-34.2013) is roughly 350 m north of that line, so the village beach and the banks north of the reserve fence are controlled zone where angling is allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit; water south of the fence is no-take. The task's reference summary describes the zone as Hoek van die Bobbejaan to Olifantsbos, which would place the boundary even further south; the village beach is outside the zone under either reading. No SANParks entry fee applies because the village is outside the Cape of Good Hope section gate.
description: A west-facing Atlantic surf beach below Scarborough village, with mussel-covered rock banks and reef at either end and thick kelp beyond the break. Shore anglers treat it as a winter galjoen spot that fishes "in the right conditions" once a big swell has scoured the sand holes, and locals occasionally land a big steenbras; the kelp makes it a bait spot rather than a lure spot, and one 2010 poster admitted "a lot of anglers think this area does not produce any fish". The Cape of Good Hope no-take zone starts at the reserve fence just south of the beach, so fish only north of it.
hazards: Open Atlantic surf with powerful waves and rip currents (the City of Cape Town gives this warning for the adjacent Witsands beach); cold water.
Mussel-covered banks and rocks are slippery and wash over in swell; surf guides flag rocks as the hazard at Scarborough Point.
Thick kelp close in snags lures and line; the stretch is rated poor for lure fishing.
The Cape of Good Hope restricted zone starts at the reserve fence at Schusters Bay Point just south of the beach; fishing south of the fence is an offence.
access_notes: Scarborough village is on the M65 coast road between Misty Cliffs and the Cape Point reserve. Park on the village side of the beach off the main road (exact car park not verified; the City's beach page returned 404) and walk onto the sand or along it to the banks at either end. No gate, hours or fee outside the reserve fence. It is a surf beach, so pick a day the swell is dropping and stay off rocks that are washing over. Drive: no source states a time; OSRM free-flow on 2026-10-29 gave about 31 minutes from Westlake and about 53 minutes from Green Point.
unverified: Hottentot and yellowtail at Scarborough: the merged notes listed them, but the thread they came from (spots-around-simons-town.83339) names them for Chappies, Rooikrans and the Glencairn stretch, not Scarborough; dropped from the species list.

Light tackle: no page says what tackle is used at Scarborough; galjoen fishing here is bait fishing with small hooks, and the lure-fishing thread rates Misty Cliffs/Scarborough/Soetwater/Kommetjie as kelp-heavy or poor for lures.
Bait choices for galjoen (red bait, white mussel, bloodworm) come from general Cape galjoen threads on the same forum, not from a Scarborough catch report.
Typical sizes: no source gives sizes for Scarborough galjoen or steenbras.
Tide: no Scarborough-specific tide preference found; the one nearby report (Misty Cliffs, August 2012) fished a dropping tide with a good swell and got bites quickly.
Bag and size limits from the national regulations (galjoen 2 at 35 cm minimum, white steenbras 1 at 60 cm minimum) were not in the evidence.
Parking location, lifeguards and dog rules: the City of Cape Town Scarborough Beach page returned HTTP 404 at both URL patterns tried.
Facing bearing (265), shelter, bottom and depth are read from the map and the forum descriptions of banks, holes and kelp, not from a page that states them.

How far the sand runs south before the reserve fence: the no-take boundary coordinate is about 350 m south of the OSM beach centroid, so the southern end of the beach may be at or very near the line; the fence on the ground is the marker to use.
"Steenbras" in the 2014 post is assumed to be white steenbras.
The tourism claim that Scarborough offers "some of the best fishing and surfing on the peninsular" (sa-venues, via a cached search summary) is promotional and gives no species or spot detail.

issues: Legality holds. The 2004 regulation text, cached from Wikipedia on 29 Oct 2026, puts the Cape of Good Hope restricted zone's northern point at Schusters Bay Point, Scarborough (S34 12.271 E018 22.194, about -34.2045, 18.3699), with the seaward edge running 180 degrees true from that point. The record's point (-34.2013, 18.3723) is about 350 m north of it and east of the line, so it sits in the TMNP controlled zone. The older acts.co.za reg 10(f)(i) also starts the closure at 'the boundary fence of the Cape of Good Hope Nature Reserve at Schuster Bay, Scarborough'. Neither source puts the village beach in a no-take zone. The task's reference summary (Hoek van die Bobbejaan to Olifantsbos) would put the line even further south.

The aka 'Schuster's Bay' is misleading and a legal hazard. Both regulation texts use Schusters Bay Point and the reserve fence at Schuster Bay as the start of the no-take zone. Calling Schuster's Bay another name for this fishing spot invites anglers onto the boundary or into the closed water. Remove it from aka.

The record's main forum quotes are NOT in the cached evidence. These are 'Scarborough and Misty Cliffs produce good Galjoen in the right conditions', 'some locals who go there often have caught some big Steenbras there as well', 'musselcovered banks', 'North wind over last few days has made sea rough out Scarborough way', and 'a lot of anglers think this area does not produce any fish'. I grepped the full salvage cache (research_cache.jsonl, species-first.jsonl, falsebay-east.jsonl). 'right conditions' appears only for Strand and Kleinmond/Betty's Bay threads, not Scarborough. The cached snippet of thread 30031 says only that the poster 'Scouted Misty Cliffs and Scarborough and found "a few good reefs." Asks about winter galjoen fishing' (a question, not a catch report). The cached snippet of thread 83339 is 'Newcomer from Kommetjie asks about fishing spots around Simon's Town', with no Scarborough or steenbras content.

Live re-fetches of https://sealine.co.za/threads/galjoen-angling-between-scarborough-and-cape-point.30031/ and https://sealine.co.za/threads/spots-around-simons-town.83339/ on 2026-11-02 both failed with no connection (curl HTTP 000, corporate proxy), so the quotes above remain unverified.

https://sealine.co.za/threads/fishing-this-weekend.51481/ is cited as a source but does not appear anywhere in the cached evidence for this spot. The 'North wind ... Scarborough way' quote attributed to it cannot be checked.

Angling support in the cache is thin and is mostly questions rather than reports. These are: sealine Galjoen thread 5869 (2008), saying after heavy swells the Atlantic side 'from Bakoven to Misty Cliffs, Scarborough area' was 'looking really good'; thread 30031, asking about winter galjoen; the Guatengaleng thread (2007) and 'Atlantic side of the peninsula' (2013), both asking whether galjoen are caught at Scarborough with no answer shown; and the lure thread 80509, which rates Misty Cliffs/Scarborough/Soetwater/Kommetjie as 'kelp-heavy or poor'. That is enough to show anglers fish for galjoen here, so the evidence is not refuted, but it is weak.

species.size: Not stated for Scarborough; the sources only say it produces "good Galjoen in the right conditions". Cape galjoen typically run 1 to 2 kg with the odd fish over 3 kg (unverified for this spot).
species.bait: Red bait, white mussel or bloodworm on small hooks, fished into the sand holes beside the mussel banks and reef; these bait choices come from general Cape galjoen threads on the same forum, not from a Scarborough catch report. Lures are reported as poor here because of kelp.
species.notes: Season is 1 March to 14 October, with winter the stated time ("fish these waters for galjoen in winter"; "one of the fishing spots I know of for Galjoen" for the adjoining Misty Cliffs). Fishes after a swell has cleaned out the holes between the mussel-covered banks. A 2010 poster noted "a lot of anglers think this area does not produce any fish" and had only "seen a few anglers around last Winter", so expect patchy results.

name: Gifkommetjie (Cape Point)
area: Cape of Good Hope section, Table Mountain National Park (Atlantic side, between Hoek van die Bobbejaan and Platboom)
coord_source: The OSM node for Gifkommetjie (-34.3241, 18.4203) comes from the merge step and was not re-checked, because the Photon query this pass returned nothing. I compared it with the 2004 regulation point for Hoek van die Bobbejaan, 34°18.393'S 18°24.258'E (about -34.3066, 18.4043), quoted on Sealine thread 55681. That point is about 2 km north-west of the node. The coordinates of the car park at the end of the Gifkommetjie road were not found.
bottom: Rock with gullies, opening onto a bay. Anglers fish the white water close in. This is inferred from the thread's talk of gullies and the bay; no source describes the bottom outright.
permit: Inside the Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park: as well as the DFFE permit you need a SANParks line-fishing activity permit (Level 3, day or annual) and the park entry fee, and the gate hours limit when you can be there. Gifkommetjie lies south of Hoek van die Bobbejaan, outside the Cape of Good Hope no-take zone. A DFFE recreational angling permit (controlled zone of the TMNP MPA), plus the SANParks conservation fee at the Cape Point gate and the SANParks activity permit for this section of the park. A Sealine poster bought a Wild Card to cut entry fees. For galjoen, the national rules are a closed season from 15 October to the end of February, a 35 cm minimum size and a bag limit of 2 per day. I did not re-check these against a source this pass.
legality: Allowed with a permit. The boundary of the 2004 TMNP MPA "Cape of Good Hope Restricted Zone" is quoted on Sealine thread 55681 (Oct 2011): "between Hoek van die Bobbejaan and the fence at Scarborough, and extending approximately one nautical mile seawards", with boundary points 34°12.271'S 018°22.194'E and 34°18.393'S 018°24.258'E. This matches Wikipedia's "Hoek van die Bobbejaan to Schusters Bay Point, Scarborough" and the brief's Hoek van die Bobbejaan to Olifantsbos stretch. The OSM Gifkommetjie node at -34.3241 lies about 2 km south-east of Hoek van die Bobbejaan (-34.3066), so the bay is in the controlled zone. There, angling is allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit, plus the SANParks conservation fee and activity permit for this section of the park. One merge note marked the spot PROHIBITED; that note put Gifkommetjie inside the no-take zone, which the regulation coordinates do not support. Anglers who walk right (north) from the path towards Hoek van die Bobbejaan will enter the no-take zone. I did not check the current gazette or SANParks pages, and I did not resolve whether the older MLRA closed-area text (Schuster Bay to Cape Point, 500 m seaward) still applies.
description: A rocky, exposed bay on the Atlantic side of the Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park. You reach it by driving to the end of the Gifkommetjie road and walking down a steep path. Sealine anglers fish it for galjoen with white mussel, wonderworm and red bait: "Gifkommetjie is great, take the left path and fish the whole bay", and "rolling water pushing tide and full moon were my best days". The Cape of Good Hope no-take zone starts just to the north at Hoek van die Bobbejaan.
hazards: Exposed Atlantic shore: full south-west swell, and waves wash over the rocks. The best fishing is in 'rolling water', so watch for sets.
Steep path down from the car park and a hard climb back up. Jo-Jo warns: "make sure your cardio levels are good".
The Cape of Good Hope no-take zone begins at Hoek van die Bobbejaan just to the north. Walking right (north) along the shore takes you into it.
Reserve gate hours: you must be out before the gate closes.
Remote shore with no facilities. Baboons are active in the reserve (general knowledge, not sourced).
access_notes: Car park at the end of the Gifkommetjie turn-off inside the Cape Point gate. A Sealine poster calls the road 'the 2nd circular drive'. From there a steep path leads down to the shore. Coordinates of the car park were not found. Enter through the Cape Point gate of the Cape of Good Hope section of TMNP. A conservation fee is charged, and a Wild Card reduces it according to a Sealine poster. Take the Gifkommetjie turn-off ('the 2nd circular drive', per Press On), drive to the end and walk down. "There is a path u can either walk left or right, both are good." gotaway: "take the left path and fish the whole bay". Left (south) stays in the controlled zone. Going right (north), stop before Hoek van die Bobbejaan. The walk back up is steep. Gate opening hours and fee amounts were not checked this pass.
unverified: Whether the stand really lies south of Hoek van die Bobbejaan. That rests only on the OSM node (-34.3241, 18.4203), which I could not re-check (the Photon query returned nothing). No angler gives a position, and the car park coordinates were not found.

Whether the older MLRA closed area (Schuster Bay to Cape Point, 500 m seaward, seen by finders on acts.co.za) was fully replaced by the 2004 TMNP MPA zoning. The current gazette and the SANParks fishing pages were not checked.
SANParks gate hours, the conservation fee amount and the activity-permit requirement for angling in the Cape of Good Hope section.
Galjoen closed season (15 Oct to end Feb), 35 cm minimum size and bag limit of 2 per day: national rules from general knowledge, not from the cached pages.

The quotes credited to threads 3740 and 83339 ('This time of the year you could get some nice Galjoen at Gifkommetjie'; Olifantsbos and the road to Cape Maclear) come from the merge notes. I did not re-open those threads this pass.
Bottom type (rock and gullies) and the 235-degree seaward bearing are inferred from the coastline geometry between Hoek van die Bobbejaan and the OSM node, not stated by any source.
Any lure, fly or non-galjoen species at Gifkommetjie: no source mentions any.
Baboon hazard is general knowledge for the reserve, not sourced for this spot.

issues: The cached evidence file (gifkommetjie.evidence.md) holds no angling text about Gifkommetjie. It has only two failed web searches, the Wikipedia TMNP MPA page (which says it does not mention Gifkommetjie) and a Sealine search for 'Platboom' (which says none of its hits cover Gifkommetjie). None of the record's angling or legality quotes come from that cache. I re-fetched Sealine thread 30031 to check them.

Re-fetching Sealine thread 30031 (Feb 2010) confirms these quotes: Press On ('2nd circular drive to gif kommetjie', 'path u can either walk left or right', 'rolling water pushing tide and full moon', 'take lots of sinkers and hooks'), gotaway ('Gifkommetjie is great ,take the left path and fish the whole bay', 'start stocking with wonderworm'), martin67 ('sw wind and spring high'), Jo-Jo ('first Gallie at Gifkommetjie... wt mussel and red bait combo', the cardio warning), jade fish (the cold-water warning) and John van Tonder (the Wild Card for entry fees). The re-fetch notes that jopad's name is attached to Press On's text in later quotes, so the attribution may be slightly off.

The re-fetch of thread 30031 did not turn up three quotes the record uses: 'there are enough gallies for all' (credited to Press On), 'white mussel and wonderworm are the baits of choice', and lushwill's 'the whole stretch will deliver gallies'. They may be in posts that don't say 'Gif', but they are unconfirmed. The 'common' abundance rests mainly on the 'enough gallies for all' quote.

The quotes credited to threads 3740 and 83339, and the regulation boundary coordinates credited to thread 55681, are not in the evidence cache and were not re-opened. The legality argument therefore rests on an uncached forum quote of the 2004 regulations, plus the brief and Wikipedia, which both put Hoek van die Bobbejaan at the southern (Atlantic) end of the Cape of Good Hope no-take zone. If 34°18.393'S 18°24.258'E for Hoek van die Bobbejaan is correct, the Gifkommetjie node (-34.3241, 18.4203) lies about 2.4 km to the south-east (about 1.9 km south and 1.5 km east), in the controlled zone. Nothing in the evidence contradicts this, and the 2010 Sealine anglers (fishing after the 2004 zoning) raise no no-take concern. Not refuted, but the boundary point is second-hand.

Light-tackle fit is marginal. The only angling is bait fishing for galjoen in rolling white water on a fully exposed Atlantic shore, with 'lots of sinkers and hooks' because it snags. That is usually medium rock-and-surf work, not light tackle. The sources don't state rod or sinker weight, so this does not show the spot is heavy-gear only, but the method 'light bait' is generous. No post mentions lures, spinning or fly fishing at Gif. John van Tonder's spinning mention is about Simon's Town, and his 'crays and perlie' at Gifkommetjie was diving.

The months [3..10] include October, but galjoen season closes on 15 October, so October is only half open. The closed season, 35 cm minimum size and bag limit of 2 are not sourced in the evidence (general knowledge). The spot is out of season for galjoen as of today, 2 Nov 2026.

species.size: No source gives a size for this spot. The legal minimum is 35 cm (national rule, not re-sourced this pass).
species.bait: White mussel and wonderworm are the main baits ("white mussel and wonderworm are the baits of choice"; gotaway says to stock up on wonderworm). Jo-Jo caught his first galjoen here on a white mussel and red bait combo. Press On says to "take lots of sinkers and hooks".
species.notes: Press On: "there are enough gallies for all". He says rolling water, a pushing tide and a full moon gave his best days. martin67 says a south-west wind and a spring high tide work best, though he has also caught fish in fairly flat water. jade fish advises avoiding very cold water, because the galjoen don't seem to like it at Gif. lushwill: "the whole stretch will deliver gallies" (Gif round towards Platboom and Cape Maclear). The months shown are the open season (closed 15 Oct to end Feb). No angler names best months, apart from a merge-note quote that "this time of the year you could get some nice Galjoen at Gifkommetjie".

name: Platboom (Cape Point)
area: Cape of Good Hope section, Table Mountain National Park (Atlantic side, between Hoek van die Bobbejaan and the Cape of Good Hope)
coord_source: Rough coordinates from the merge step, kept and not verified. Nominatim found nothing for "Platboom" on 29 Oct 2026, and a Photon query today came back empty. The rough point is about 2.5 km south of the Hoek van die Bobbejaan boundary point in the gazette (S34 18.393 E018 24.258), which fits Platboom being in the controlled zone. The exact stand and car park positions are unknown, and the point may sit slightly inland of the shoreline.
bottom: Rocky reef with a dense kelp forest, gullies and an outer reef. A Sealine poster called it "as foul as anything, all the kelp etc", and a diver remembered "a huge kelp forest". There are small sandy patches at the beach.
permit: Inside the Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park: as well as the DFFE permit you need a SANParks line-fishing activity permit (Level 3, day or annual) and the park entry fee, and the gate hours limit when you can be there. Platboom lies south of Hoek van die Bobbejaan, outside the Cape of Good Hope no-take zone; Olifantsbos, to the north, is inside it. You need a DFFE recreational angling permit, plus the SANParks conservation or entry fee for the Cape of Good Hope section and a SANParks activity permit. SANParks lists line fishing as a Level 3 activity, sold as an annual or day permit or as My Activity. The SANParks Marine Species Access Permit (R1,135 for 12 entries, sold at the Tokai office, DFFE permit required) is for crayfish and similar species. A 2012 report says it does not cover line fishing. Galjoen have a closed season, and one 2010 poster says it "opens in March".
legality: Fishing is allowed with permits. Platboom is on the Atlantic shore south of Hoek van die Bobbejaan (S34 18.393 E018 24.258). That point is the southern end of the Cape of Good Hope restricted (no-take) zone, which runs north to Schusters Bay Point, Scarborough (2004 TMNP MPA regulations, as quoted on the Wikipedia TMNP MPA page). Platboom therefore falls in the controlled zone, where "Fishing is allowed in the controlled zone of the MPA subject to permits". Anglers posted about fishing here in June and July 2014. Caveat: the older MLRA regulation 10(f)(i) on acts.co.za describes a 500 m closed area from the reserve fence at Schuster Bay to the Cape Point lighthouse, "except on the authority of a permit". This looks like the pre-2004 closure that the MPA zoning replaced, but I could not confirm that it was repealed.
description: A kelp-choked rocky shore and small beach on the Atlantic side of the Cape Point reserve, south of Hoek van die Bobbejaan. Anglers on Sealine fish it for galjoen with white mussel on light 10 ft rods, casting into gullies "not even 20m off the side in less than 2m of water". The ground is "as foul as anything, all the kelp", so expect to lose tackle.
hazards: Very foul ground with dense kelp and reef, so expect heavy tackle loss ("as foul as anything, all the kelp etc")
Fully exposed to Atlantic swell and wind; anglers report fishing in hail, rain and "a blustering wind"
Large fish, probably big spotted gully sharks or smooth-hounds, take galjoen baits close in and can strip about 150 m of line or cut a 25 lb trace on the outer reef
Slippery rocks: one angler had to jump down off the rocks to land his fish
Remote spot inside the reserve, with closing times at the gate
access_notes: Reached by the Platboom turn-off from the Cape Point reserve road, after the Cape Point (Cape of Good Hope section) entry gate. The car park position has not been verified; use the rough spot coordinates. The spot is inside the paid Cape Point (Cape of Good Hope) section of Table Mountain National Park. You pay entry at the gate, and you need a SANParks activity permit for line fishing as well as a DFFE angling permit. The gates have set opening and closing times, which limits dawn and dusk sessions (Sealine 2007: \"the entrance fee to the reserve might be prohibitive\", gates close at a set time). Prices in a 2012 report (R90 entry, R360 Level 3 permit) are out of date. Check current fees and gate hours with SANParks (Tokai office, +27 21 712 7471). Parking and the length of the walk to the rocks were not found in any source.
unverified: Exact stand and car park coordinates: the merge point is rough, and both geocoders returned nothing
Facing bearing of about 230 degrees (SW): estimated from the NW-SE run of the coast between Hoek van die Bobbejaan and the Cape of Good Hope, not from a source

Tide preference: no Platboom post gives one. 'Pushing' is borrowed from posts about nearby Gifkommetjie on the same stretch (Press On: "rolling water, a pushing tide, and a full moon"; martin67: "a sw wind and spring high produces the best")
Whether MLRA regulation 10(f)(i), the closed area from Schuster Bay to the Cape Point lighthouse, has been repealed and replaced by the 2004 MPA zoning
Exact galjoen closed-season dates (only 'opens in March' is sourced) and current bag and size limits
Current SANParks entry fee, activity permit price and gate hours
White musselcracker and white steenbras: posters only say divers have seen them here ("there are cracker in that area"). No shore catch is reported, so they are left out of the species list
Sharks: big spotted gully sharks are said to be "apparently common there", and smooth-hound was suggested, both hooked on galjoen bait. Under the brief they belong in notes, not the species list
Any light-tackle spinning or fly fishing at Platboom: no source mentions it, only bait fishing for galjoen

issues: Legality holds. The gazette coordinates quoted on the Wikipedia TMNP MPA page close the Cape of Good Hope restricted zone at Hoek van die Bobbejaan, S34 18.393 E018 24.258 (-34.3066). From there the boundary runs west along that latitude to E018 23.500. The record point (-34.329) and the whole of OSM's Platboom Road (-34.321 to -34.335) lie 1.6 to 3 km south of that line, so Platboom is in the controlled zone. That page says "Fishing is allowed in the controlled zone of the MPA subject to permits". The brief's shorthand describes the zone as Hoek van die Bobbejaan to Olifantsbos, which is north of Hoek van die Bobbejaan, so Platboom is outside either way.

One legal caveat is still open, and the record already flags it. MLRA regulation 10(f)(i) on acts.co.za closes 500 m seaward from the reserve fence at Schuster Bay to the Cape Point lighthouse 'except on the authority of a permit', and that area covers Platboom. Nothing in the evidence shows it was repealed by the 2004 MPA notice. The wording allows fishing under a permit, and SANParks sells line-fishing Level 3 activity permits for this section, so it does not refute 'allowed with permits'. It does need checking. SANParks' 2026 'Coastal-zones-map.pdf' (2027 management plan) shows up in the search results but was never opened, so a proposed rezoning has not been ruled out.

Coordinates are roughly right but sit on the access road, not the shore. A Nominatim reverse geocode of -34.329, 18.444 returns 'Platboom Road' (highway/service, OSM way 35911632), snapped to -34.3289, 18.4442. The road leaves the main reserve road at about -34.3212, 18.4531, runs SW to its most westerly point at about -34.3274, 18.4436, then runs SE parallel to the coast and ends in a small loop at about -34.3345, 18.4490, which is probably the car park (not confirmed). The shoreline is likely a few hundred metres W/SW of the record point. A test geocode at -34.329, 18.436 found no mapped feature. I could not show the point is more than 500 m off, so coords_refuted is false, but the point should be labelled 'access road', not 'stand'. Overpass returned 502 Bad Gateway, so no named beach or bay node could be checked.

Evidence holds. The fetched Sealine thread 'What was it?' (sealine.co.za/threads/what-was-it.84563/, 17 Jul 2014) describes a shore angler at Platboom fishing for 'Gallies' with fresh white mussel, hooked 'not even 20m off the side in less than 2m of water'. The ground is described as 'as foul as anything, all the kelp etc', and a big spotty is 'apparently common there'. That is shore bait fishing for galjoen, which fits light bait fishing.

'Light 10 ft set up' is not verified. The only gear in the evidence is from the same angler in the fetched thread: a 10 ft Blue Marlin Raptor, Stradic FJ 5000, 30 lb braid and 25 lb hook trace. That is a medium rock outfit, not obviously light tackle. The quote 'light 10 ft set up' is not in the evidence file. It would come from thread 83885, and only a search snippet of that thread is cached.

Several quoted claims cannot be traced to the evidence file: the 37 cm galjoen 'landed' in June 2014, 'found a nice spot at platboom, with white muscle', fishing in hail and wind with bites on the first casts, the angler jumping down off the rocks to land his fish, lushwill (2010) 'i've never had or heard of anybody landing gallies on that side using red bait', the 'opens in March' closed-season quote, a diver's 'huge kelp forest', and the Gifkommetjie tide quotes from Press On and martin67. The cached search snippet for thread 83885 in fact says the angler 'landed a bite, and lost a fish near the shore', which conflicts with a 37 cm fish being landed. The galjoen-angling-between-scarborough-and-cape-point thread (30031) does not appear anywhere in the cached Platboom evidence.

species.size: One report gives a 37 cm fish (June 2014). Typical sizes for this spot are not sourced.
species.bait: Fresh white mussel is the main bait, with wonderworm as the alternative. lushwill (2010) says of this stretch: "i've never had or heard of anybody landing gallies on that side using red bait." A white mussel and red bait combo did work at nearby Gifkommetjie.
species.notes: June 2014: "found a nice spot at platboom, with white muscle" on a "light 10 ft set up", in hail and wind, with bites on the first casts and one 37 cm galjoen landed. July 2014: an angler fishing "for Gallies" with fresh white mussel was hooked "not even 20m off the side in less than 2m of water". lushwill (2010) says the whole stretch from Gifkommetjie to Cape Point, including Platboom, produces galjoen. The best months are inferred from these winter reports and from the season opening in March.

name: Muizenberg corner
area: Muizenberg / St James
coord_source: Stand placed on the sand just seaward of the OpenStreetMap building named "Surfers' Corner" (way 674476918, centre -34.10769, 18.47032) returned by an Overpass query on 30 October 2026; the merge-step coordinates (-34.1085, 18.47) agree to within about 50 m. Bailey's Cottage itself is not named in OSM: its rocky point is about 450 m south-west along the Main Road, estimated at about -34.1105, 18.4658 from the OSM "Baileys Kloof" cliff node above it (-34.11264, 18.46254) and the Main Road parking at -34.11021, 18.46739. A bounded Nominatim search for "cottage" in the Muizenberg box returned nothing.

access.note: Free paved surface car park directly behind Surfers' Corner (OSM way 863783602, fee=no, unlit, 30 Oct 2026). Larger beachfront car parks by the Pavilion at about -34.1075, 18.4716 and a gravel lot at -34.1090, 18.4686; the Main Road lay-by at -34.1102, 18.4674 is the closest parking to the Bailey's Cottage rocks.

bottom: Flat sand beach with gutters ("find the holes") running north-east from a rocky point with boulders and reef under Bailey's Cottage, "the little house on the rocky point". Harders (mullet) are netted on the corner sand for bait.
mouth: Not applicable, open sea beach. The Zandvlei mouth is about 1 km east of the Pavilion and is a separate spot.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine) for everyone fishing from the shore here; no MPA activity permit or SANParks fee applies at Muizenberg. Standard DFFE bag and size limits apply to kob, elf and white steenbras (figures not sourced in this pass, see unverified). Permit outlets reported in search snippets: the DFFE e-permit site (fishing.dffe.gov.za) or the Post Office.
legality: Allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit. The beach from Bailey's Cottage north-east to the Pavilion lies outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA: the Wikipedia MPA page (opened 29 Oct 2026) states the controlled area's eastern limit is at Bailey's Cottage, Muizenberg, matching the 2004 regulations (controlled zone from Bailey's Cottage round Cape Point to Mouille Point). The nearest no-take zone, St James, runs from the Kalk Bay tidal pool (S34 07.567 E018 27.050) to the St James tidal pool (S34 07.123 E018 27.568) and ends about 0.9 km south-west of Bailey's Cottage; the finders' note on the older MLRA R1111 closed area (Neptune's Corner to the St James tidal pool north wall, acts.co.za) also ends at the St James pool, so neither boundary reaches this corner. The Bailey's Cottage rocks themselves sit at the controlled-zone boundary, where angling with the DFFE permit is allowed. The City of Cape Town's Muizenberg Beach page (opened 30 Oct 2026) lists "Fishing and angling" among the beach's activities. A Sealine poster's 2014 question "Does that mean that Bailey's Cottage is outside the no take zone?" is answered yes by the regulations.
description: The western end of Muizenberg beach, from the Surfers' Corner sand round to the rocky point under Bailey's Cottage: "Baileys is the cottage at the corner where Muizenberg beach starts". Sealine anglers fish it light: elf "at high tide with a surface lure or Iron Candy" in the Bailey's Cottage area, kob "on paddletail and spoon caught off the beach at ... muizenberg pavilion" on the odd day they run, and "bait fishing with light gear" for steenbras and night kob along the flat sand, where "Kob come in really close sometimes". It fires "after the SE has been blowing for a while" and fishes best in the evenings; by day it is a busy Blue Flag surf and bathing beach.
hazards: Night safety: Sealine posters warn 'just don't fish it alone at night' and to 'Watch out for fishermen along that stretch' (Baileys to Strandfontein); fish in a group after dark.
A strong south-easter brings 'big swell for Baileys' onto the rocky point; stay off the rocks in a big SE sea.
Busy Blue Flag surfing and bathing beach with lifeguards and surf schools at the corner by day; cast well clear of surfers and swimmers (posters say the beaches fish better in the evenings).
White sharks: Muizenberg is reported as a Shark Spotters beach with a flag and siren warning system (search-result claim, no page opened).
St Joseph and small sharks are taken on bait here (St Joseph landed at Baileys, Sealine Jan 2008); handle with care.
access_notes: Main Road, Muizenberg (City of Cape Town page). Several beachfront car parks within 100 m of the sand; the rocks under Bailey's Cottage are about 450 m south-west along the beach or the seafront walkway (the City page notes a seafront walkway from Muizenberg to St James). Blue Flag beach: the City lists parking, toilets, lifeguards and path/walkways; dogs on leads allowed; no gate and no fee (the SANParks entry fee applies only in the Cape of Good Hope section, not here). Bait and tackle: Brays store in Muizenberg, "the shop on the left adjacent to the turn off for the muizenberg beach" (Sealine, Nov 2013). Safety: Sealine posters say "just don't fish it alone at night" and "Watch out for fishermen along that stretch" (Baileys to Strandfontein), and recommend fishing in numbers. The corner is a busy surfing and bathing beach by day; posters say "The Beaches are definitely more productive in the evenings". Drive: the angling sources give no drive times; the merge step's OSRM free-flow estimate (2026-10-29) is about 7 min from Westlake and 30 min from Green Point.
unverified: Shark Spotters presence and flag/siren system at Muizenberg: from a cached search-result summary, no page opened.
Exact position of Bailey's Cottage: not named in OSM; estimated at about -34.1105, 18.4658.

DFFE bag and size limits (from memory, not sourced in this pass): kob 1 per day at 60 cm from the shore; elf 4 per day at 30 cm with a closed season 1 October to 30 November; white steenbras 1 per day at 60 cm. Check the current DFFE recreational fishing brochure.
Permit outlets (DFFE e-permit site, Post Office): from search snippets only.
Typical fish sizes: no source gives measurements beyond 'nice size elf'.
Facing bearing (150 degrees) and 'semi' shelter: derived from the map geometry, not stated by any source.
Slippery, kelp-fringed rocks at Bailey's Cottage: inferred from 'rocky point', not stated.
Drive times are the merge step's OSRM estimates; no angling source gives a drive time.
All angling evidence is forum posts from 2008 to 2016; no report from the last five years was found.
legal_note: the shore from opposite Muizenberg Station (Surfer's Corner) south to St James is a closed area in the 1998 fishing regulations (regulation 10(f)(iii): 500 m out to sea, no fishing 'except on the authority of a permit'). DFFE's current brochure no longer lists it and anglers fish the corner, but no official page confirms it is open. The beach north-east of the station, towards the Pavilion and the Zandvlei mouth, is outside it. The City's by-law also bans fishing within 100 m of a signed bathing area.

issues: Legality holds. The stand (-34.1082, 18.4700) lies north-east of Bailey's Cottage, so it is outside the TMNP MPA or at most on the controlled-zone edge. The cached Wikipedia MPA fetch (29 Oct) says Muizenberg is controlled and that the controlled area's eastern limit is at Bailey's Cottage. The St James no-take zone ends at the St James tidal pool (S34 07.123 E018 27.568 = -34.1187, 18.4595), about 1.5 km south-west of the stand, so no restricted zone reaches it. The cached search summary says the City of Cape Town lists 'Fishing and angling' as a Muizenberg Beach activity. However, the City page itself (cited as opened 30 Oct) is not in the 29 Oct cache.

Legality caveat that was not checked: this is a lifeguarded Blue Flag bathing beach, and City coastal or beach rules may bar casting inside the flagged swimming area while lifeguards are on duty. No source in the evidence covers this. Add it as unverified rather than claiming angling is allowed anywhere on the sand at all hours.

Permit and bag-limit note is likely wrong for this coast. The record's from-memory 'kob 1 per day at 60 cm from the shore' is the rule for shore and estuary catches EAST of Cape Agulhas, which is how the cached search summary (species-first, 'sealine.co.za Cape Town shore fishing spots...') words it. Muizenberg is west of Cape Agulhas. The only Muizenberg-specific figure in the evidence is the non-official koolasun.co.za page, which gives 50 cm and 5 per day for kob. Fix the unverified note and point readers to the DFFE brochure.

Three cited quotes are not in the 29 Oct cache given for this spot, so they could not be checked against a cached page: 'Baileys still produce Kob, Steenbras and Elf when the conditions are right' and 'after the SE has been blowing for a while' (spots-around-simons-town.83339, which the cache holds only as a thread-list row: 'Newcomer from Kommetjie asks about fishing spots around Simon's Town'), the 2014 'Does that mean that Bailey's Cottage is outside the no take zone?', and 'kob on paddletail and spoon ... muizenberg pavilion' (kob-on-lure-plastics-false-bay.93538). The paddle-tail quote appears only in the merge step's candidates.json, not in a cached page record. The Overpass result (30 Oct) is also not in the cache.

The angling evidence that does check out in the cache is enough to keep the spot. Sealine 'Lure fishing the surf' (Dec 2013): 'Bailies Cottage area, at high tide with a surface lure or Iron Candy for elf'. Sealine 'Simon's Town to Kalk Bay' (Jan 2008): 'Some nice size elf have been coming out at Kalkies and at Baileys', 'Baileys is the cottage at the corner where Muizenberg beach starts', and 'Muizenberg corner through Strandfontein beaches' recommended for 'bait fishing with light gear' and night kob. Sealine 'Newbie beach fishing' (2010): 'From Baileys right down to Strandfontein works'. Two further threads mention Baileys as a spot without species: 79832 ('the little house on the rocky point') and 55386 ('Strong SE wind with big swell for Baileys').

The light-tackle fit is modest. The same lure thread says 'Artificial lures and spoons in False Bay is not very popular south of Muizenberg' and 'I have never seen guys using artificial baits in False Bay yet'. The elf angler there planned a 12 ft rod rated 3 oz, and a 45 g Iron Candy is surf-spinning weight, not truly light gear. The description should not imply that lure fishing is established here.

species.size: Not stated by the sources beyond 'nice size elf' at Baileys (Jan 2008).
species.method: spinning (surface plugs, spoons) or light bait
species.bait: Surface lure or a 45 g Iron Candy casting spoon in the Bailey's Cottage area on the high tide; bait anglers use fish baits (sardine, pike, mullet).
species.notes: 'Some nice size elf have been coming out at Kalkies and at Baileys in the week' (Sealine, Jan 2008); 'Bailies Cottage area, at high tide with a surface lure or Iron Candy for elf' (Dec 2013); 'Baileys still produce Kob, Steenbras and Elf when the conditions are right', i.e. 'after the SE has been blowing for a while' (May 2014). Season given as December to February or March by two posters.

species.size: Not stated by the sources.
species.method: light bait at night; spinning with paddle-tails and spoons
species.bait: Paddle-tail soft plastics and spoons off the beach at the Pavilion; bait anglers use chokka with pilchard or anchovy (an occy leg if available), fished at night.
species.notes: 'There have been and I have caught kob on paddletail and spoon caught off the beach at macassar and muizenberg pavilion', but only 'on the odd day' when the kob run and 'very hit and miss' (Sealine, Mar 2016). 'Muizenberg corner through Strandfontein beaches' recommended for night kob: 'Kob come in really close sometimes' (Jan 2008). Season 'Sept till March' / 'end of August till March', mostly at night though day catches happen (2010). Baileys 'still produce Kob' when conditions are right (2014).

species.size: Not stated by the sources.
species.bait: Bloodworm ('my favourite bait in that area'), prawn or a chokka/sardine combo on small hooks; keep baits 'small and long', 'long and thin' with a small piece of float; wade out and fish the low on the open beach.
species.notes: 'Steenbras: throughout the year' (Sealine, Aug 2010, for the Baileys-to-Strandfontein stretch); 'Baileys still produce Kob, Steenbras and Elf when the conditions are right' (May 2014). 'dont be afraid of fishing low tide, just wade as far as you can and cast out a bloodworm'.

name: Zandvlei mouth and Sunrise Beach
aka: Bailey's Cottage / Baileys (far west end of the same beach)
Muizies corner / Surfers' Corner (far west end)
area: Muizenberg
coord_source: The record's coordinates are the Surfers' Corner building, about 830 m from the Zandvlei mouth and 1.5 km from Sunrise Beach, and they sit opposite Muizenberg station, where the record's own closed-area caveat begins. The reserve extent from photon puts the outlet at the beach at about -34.1046, 18.

access.note: Surfers' Corner car park at the west end of the beach (merge's OSM point). For Sunrise Beach itself use the Sunrise Circle car park at the end of the M5 (Prince George Drive): parking, toilets, disability access and the False Bay Lifesaving Club building are there per the City page; its coordinates are not sourced.

bottom: Sand: a flat surf beach with shallow banks that anglers wade across at low tide ("the flats"); the Zandvlei outlet channel cuts the beach when open; rock only at the Bailey's Cottage point ("the little house on the rocky point") at the far west end.
mouth: Managed. Wikipedia: the mouth is open "throughout winter"; in summer "the mouth is manually closed by a sand bar to contain the water" and "opened monthly for a few days at full moon to maintain salinity levels and then closed again". The page does not name who does the opening; the vlei is the Zandvlei Estuary Nature Reserve (City of Cape Town by name, manager of the mouth unverified). A Flytalk post says water on the yacht-club side is "very discoloured, lots of foam and silt" just after an opening, cleaner near the footbridge.
permit: DFFE marine recreational angling permit (e-permit at fishing.dffe.gov.za or Post Office) for the beach; bag and size limits per the current DFFE recreational list (the merge's secondary sources quote kob and leervis limits that should be checked against it). In the vlei and mouth channel: the Zandvlei reserve's "standard fishing permit" (Wikipedia) and, per the Zandvlei Trust, catch-and-release of leervis. A Sealine moderator adds "Don't eat any fish from the vlei, heavy metal pollution".
legality: Allowed with a DFFE marine recreational angling permit. The TMNP MPA controlled zone runs "between Green Point and Bailey's Cottage, Muizenberg" (Wikipedia MPA page, cached 29 Oct 2026), so Sunrise Beach and the sea side of the Zandvlei mouth are outside the MPA and none of the six restricted zones is near; the corner and catwalk west of the station are inside the controlled zone, where angling is allowed with the same permit. The City of Cape Town lists "Fishing and angling" at Muizenberg Beach (search snippet, page not opened); its Sunrise Beach page (fetched 30 Oct 2026) lists water sports, dog walking, safe swimming and lifesaving, with no fishing prohibition. Inside the vlei and mouth channel the Zandvlei Estuary Nature Reserve applies: "A standard fishing permit is required" and "Fishing is popular, with many large garrick having been landed" (Wikipedia Zandvlei page, fetched 30 Oct 2026); the Zandvlei Trust says leervis must be released by law and a permit is obtainable at Post Offices or tackle shops (cached search summary only). Caveat for the far west end only: MLRA 1998 Reg 10(f)(iii) lists a 500 m closed area from Neptune's Corner (opposite Muizenberg station) to the St James tidal pool "except on the authority of a permit"; anglers fish the corner openly in 2008-2022 Sealine threads, and it does not touch Sunrise or the mouth.
description: The sandy east end of Muizenberg beach, from the Zandvlei outlet along to Sunrise Beach, fished on light bait for kob, elf and white steenbras, with leervis hunting the shallows at the mouth when the vlei is open. A Sealine thread names "the flats in front of Sunrise Beach, at night on low tide" and advises "dont be afraid of fishing low tide, just wade as far as you can and cast out a bloodworm". The far west end of the same beach, Surfers' Corner to Bailey's Cottage, is where anglers throw surface lures and spoons for elf at high tide.
hazards: Night fishing: 'just don't fish it alone at night' (Sealine 2010) and 'DEFINITELY not alone there after sunset its dangerous' (merge note); 'Watch out for fishermen along that stretch' from Baileys to Strandfontein; fish 'in safety with numbers'
Lifeguarded bathing beach with the False Bay Lifesaving Club in peak periods and a crowded surf break at the corner: fish away from bathers and surfers
Shark Spotters operate at Muizenberg (search summary); wading out on the low-tide banks is part of the tactic here, so watch the flags
Dogs run off the leash east of the lifesaving building (City page)
Vlei fish carry heavy-metal pollution: 'Don't eat any fish from the vlei' (Sealine moderator)
Water on the vlei side is 'very discoloured, lots of foam and silt' just after a mouth opening (Flytalk)
Elf teeth: use a short wire trace (search summary)
access_notes: Public beach, no gate or fee listed. Sunrise Beach: Sunrise Circle, Muizenberg, at the end of the M5 ('take the M5 to the end, through the circle into the parking area', merge note from the Sealine newbie thread); City page lists parking, toilets, disability access, lifeguards (False Bay Lifesaving Club, peak periods) and dogs on leads, off-leash east of the lifesaving building; no opening hours given. The west end has the Surfers' Corner / Pavilion car parks; a 2011 Sealine post says 'Your so close the the beach you can fish from your car' along the beach-road parking. Bait: pump prawn and worms at '1ste and 2de baai' (merge note); Brays store, 'the shop on the left adjacent to the turn off for the muizenberg beach', sells tackle and bait (Sealine 2013). Zandvlei mouth: walk east along the sand from the Pavilion or west from Sunrise Circle; the vlei side of the mouth is inside the Zandvlei Estuary Nature Reserve.
unverified: Galjoen (winter): listed by the merge, but no page in the evidence ties it to this beach; the Bailey's Cottage rocks are the likely place

'Bailey's Cottage produces kob, steenbras and elf after south-easterly wind, when warm water collects in the bays' (merge note, 2014): the cached extract only has 'Strong SE wind with big swell for Baileys'
'DEFINITELY not alone there after sunset its dangerous': merge note, thread not identified in the evidence
capeflyfishing.blogspot.com 2013 post cited by the merge for this spot: its content was lost to the 90 KB evidence cap, so it is not in sources
Who operates the mouth (City reserve staff, rubble weir and bulldozer): not stated in the pages opened
Zandvlei Trust 'catch and release of indigenous species such as leervis is required by law': seen only in a cached search summary, not checked against the reserve by-law
Facing bearing (155) and semi shelter are derived from the beach alignment at the top of False Bay, not from a source
Mouth (about -34.106, 18.478) and Sunrise Circle car park (about -34.104, 18.486) coordinates are estimates; the record's lat/lon is the merge's Surfers' Corner car park
Bait pumping at '1ste and 2de baai' reached via the M5 to the end: merge note attributed to the newbie thread, not in the cached extract
'Zandvlei problem!!' (2012, licence to stand at the mouth) and 'Harders in Cape Town' (2013, throw-netting at the mouth): seen only in the Sealine search-listing summary
City of Cape Town Muizenberg Beach page listing 'Fishing and angling': search snippet only, page not opened

issues: Coordinates: the record's point (-34.1077, 18.4699) is the 'Surfers' Corner' building on Beach Road, according to a photon reverse geocode (https://photon.komoot.io/reverse?lat=-34.1077&lon=18.4699, fetched 2 Nov 2026). It is not the Zandvlei mouth or Sunrise Beach. Photon's extent for the Zandvlei Estuary Nature Reserve (leisure=nature_reserve) runs to a south-east corner at -34.1046, 18.4792, which is where the outlet meets the beach. That puts the record's point about 830 m WSW of the mouth and about 1.5 km from Sunrise Beach, well over the 500 m tolerance.

The record's point sits opposite Muizenberg station, which is where its own MLRA 'Neptune's Corner to St James tidal pool' closed-area caveat begins. That regulation does not appear anywhere in the evidence file. So the pin is at the edge of a possible closed area, while the record says the spot it names is clearly open. Moving the pin east to the mouth or Sunrise removes this conflict.

Legality holds. The whole stretch is east of Bailey's Cottage, so it is outside the TMNP MPA, and the Wikipedia MPA extract in the evidence puts the controlled area's eastern limit at Bailey's Cottage. None of the six restricted zones comes near it. The City of Cape Town listing of 'Fishing and angling' at Muizenberg Beach is only a search snippet; no City page was opened in the cache.

Permit field overstates: the record treats the Zandvlei 'standard fishing permit' as an extra reserve permit. The Zandvlei Trust summary in the evidence says the permit is 'obtainable from any Post Office or some fishing tackle shops', which describes the ordinary DFFE recreational angling permit. No source in the evidence shows a separate reserve permit. The leervis catch-and-release 'by law' claim is also search-summary only, and AllTrails calls release only 'encouraged'.

The record's verdict rests on Sealine 'Garrick\Leervis' thread 99149 ('the shallows near the mouth', 'Sunset and sunrise was always best'), and that thread is not in the evidence file. The same goes for the Wikipedia Zandvlei page fetch, the City Sunrise Beach page fetch, grunter thread 41688, the Flytalk page and the harders search listing. The evidence file stopped at its 90 KB cap. None of their quotes can be confirmed from the cache.

The main angling source (Sealine 'Newbie beach fishing, Muizenberg/Sunrise Beach', 2010) supports shore bait fishing at Sunrise Beach, 'the flats' and 'The Horses' opposite the 7/11. But its cached extract says outright 'Zandvlei mouth: Not mentioned by name'. Nothing in the cache ties sea-side fishing at the mouth itself to any thread. The same extract also says 'The thread gives no specific light-tackle recommendations', so the light-tackle fit is inferred from 'keep it small and long' baits and from wading the low-tide flats with bloodworm.

species.size: Not stated by the sources.
species.bait: Fish baits, 'Sardine, pike or mullet', on a short wire trace; at the Bailey's Cottage end 'a surface lure or Iron Candy' (45 g casting spoon) at high tide
species.notes: 'Elf: Dec till March. Bait mostly fish' (Joker 2010). Lure thread (2013): 'Bailies Cottage area, at high tide with a surface lure or Iron Candy for elf'; Roachy fishes the Iron Candy from about 4 pm on overcast days at low tide with calm seas, rod tip low, fast retrieve then slow near the shore break where most pick-ups happen. Same thread: 'Artificial lures and spoons in False Bay is not very popular south of Muizenberg'.

species.size: Not stated for this beach. False Bay shore kob are 'mostly undersize/small fish coming out' (Sealine 2022); a regional news snippet reports 'some good-sized kob caught at Muizenberg'.
species.bait: Chokka with pilchard or anchovy, plus occy leg if available (Sealine 2010); the 2013 lure thread's poster targeted kob at the Bailey's end with spoons but reported no kob on lure
species.notes: 'Cob is my target from end of August till March' (Willem du Toit); Joker: 'Sept till March', 'normally at night is best time for cob', some caught by day. Night sessions here are a fish-with-company affair: 'just don't fish it alone at night'.

species.size: Not stated by the sources.
species.bait: Bloodworm first ('bloodworm is my favourite bait in that area'), prawn, or a chokka/sardine combo; baits 'small and long' with a small piece of float
species.notes: 'Steenbras: throughout the year' (Joker). Caught 'at nite in front of that flats on low tide' (Dafishking); alanlloyd: 'dont be afraid of fishing low tide, just wade as far as you can and cast out a bloodworm', many of his best steenbras there came on the low; AF took steenbras on fresh worm at The Horses. 2022: 'you can throw bloodworm for steenbras' from Baily's toward the start of Muizenberg beach.

species.size: 'Many large garrick having been landed' (Wikipedia) and 'a resident population of good-sized fish' (The Mission Fly Mag); no measurements given.
species.bait: Lures and flies in the vlei (YouTube title 'Leervis(Garrick) caught on lure, Zandvlei'; an old Sealine post suggests 'a pink clouser or a flipper'); no lure named for the surf side of the mouth
species.notes: Sealine 2017, moderator: 'Caught them at the bridge by the mouth, in the canals in the upper reaches', they move around and 'don't hang out anywhere in particular'; look for them 'hunting' in 'the shallows near the mouth'; 'Sunset and sunrise was always best at sandvlei for them'; 'No real tidal flow in that vlei so tides should not make a difference'. No months given by the sources; the vlei fish are described as resident. Mouth-side fish are inside the reserve: its permit and the Zandvlei Trust's release rule apply, and 'Don't eat any fish from the vlei, heavy metal pollution'.

species.size: The one reported fish was over 5 kg (2010).
species.bait: Not stated for the fish reported; prawn and bloodworm are the baits the thread names
species.notes: Captain Sparrow (Aug 2010) landed 'a host of fish in that area' and a spotted grunter over 5 kg, 'the first he had seen there'. A grunter was also netted at the Sandvlei mouth (Sealine grunter thread, 2010, per the merge notes).

name: Kalk Bay harbour wall
area: False Bay west shore, Kalk Bay
coord_source: Nominatim (30 Oct 2026) puts Kalk Bay Harbour at -34.12823, 18.44969 (harbour water centroid); an Overpass query returned the red harbour light at the breakwater head, OSM node 54745778 at -34.12832, 18.45124, and the green entrance light at -34.12815, 18.45079, but no breakwater way. The stand given is the mid-point of the main breakwater's seaward face interpolated between the head and the shore, accurate to roughly 50 m; the merge step's rough -34.129, 18.449 was within 100 m of it.
