access.note: Harbour precinct car park off Main Road (M4) at the landward end of the breakwater; position estimated from the harbour centroid, not verified. Kalk Bay station is beside the harbour.

bottom: Vertical concrete breakwater face dropping onto sand with kelp beds and rock along the foot of the wall ("hotties at the kelp near the middle of the wall"; "romans are found on the vertical wall"); sandy harbour basin inside.
permit: The harbour belongs to the Department of Public Works and Infrastructure; no official statement on angling from the walls was found, although anglers have fished them for decades. Follow the harbour master's signs and keep clear of working boats. The wall lies just south of the St James no-take zone, which ends at the Kalk Bay tidal pool: do not fish north of the harbour. DFFE recreational marine angling permit (Post Office). Standard bag and size limits apply; a Sealine poster notes "the bag limit and size limit is different" for white and Cape stumpnose. Squid: a 2010 thread gives a daily limit of 20 and a closed season of 25 October to 22 November; whether that closed season still applies to recreational jigging is unverified.
legality: Fishing is allowed with a permit. The harbour lies inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone (Bailey's Cottage round Cape Point to Mouille Point), where angling is permitted with a DFFE recreational angling permit. The nearest no-take zone is St James, whose south-western limit is the Kalk Bay tidal pool at S34 07.567 E018 27.050 (-34.1261, 18.4508), per the 2004 regulations as reproduced on the Wikipedia TMNP MPA page (opened 29 Oct 2026); the breakwater head is at -34.1283, 18.4512, about 245 m south of that line, so the wall and the water in front of it are outside the no-take zone (Wikivoyage, via a cached search, likewise places the "Kalk Bay restricted zone" north of the harbour). MLRA Regulation 10(f)(iv) on acts.co.za (opened 29 Oct 2026) ends the St James-Kalk Bay closed area at "the northern wall of the tidal pool situated opposite Kalk Bay Station" and does not mention the harbour. A 30 Oct 2026 search found no published harbour-master or DFFE rule on shore angling from the breakwater, and the 2008 to 2022 threads describe anglers fishing the wall openly with no restriction mentioned ("Rules or harbour-master restrictions: None mentioned").
description: The main breakwater of Kalk Bay's working fishing harbour on the west shore of False Bay, with the lighthouse at its eastern head and the harbour entrance facing north-east towards the Brass Bell. Sealine anglers describe it as a summer spot that fishes "only really ... during the summer months when the SE wind has been blowing": small elf, maasbanker and hottentot at the kelp mid-wall, white stumpnose and the odd kob at night on the high tide, chokka on jigs around dusk, and very occasionally a yellowtail. Catches are mostly small; a 2022 regular rates it as a place for "the kids catching hotties at the kelp near the middle of the wall" rather than an edibles spot.
hazards: Big south to south-east swells break over the breakwater; the seaward face is a sheer drop with no rail (a cached source calls the harbour "very exposed to the massive swells that come down the bay")
Wet, slippery concrete, often fished at night in a crowd
Working DFFE fishing harbour: boats offloading, nets and vehicles on the quay
Seals habituated to scraps hang around the quay and slipway; keep bait and catch away from them
Blowfish (puffers) are a common nuisance catch at night
Casting north-east from the lighthouse end, the St James no-take line at the Kalk Bay tidal pool is only about 250 m away; do not fish the tidal pools
access_notes: Public access onto the breakwater through the harbour precinct off Main Road (M4); the Harbour House and Polana restaurants sit at the base of the wall. Parking inside the harbour and along Main Road, crowded at weekends and at lunchtime. No gate fee or opening hours found; anglers fish it at night. Kalk Bay station is beside the harbour. Nearest tackle shops named by anglers: Brays in Muizenberg and Great White on Main Road, Fish Hoek (2013).
unverified: Mackerel runs at the Kalk Bay wall (merge hint): the only mackerel mention in the evidence is for Simon's Town
Which thread holds the quoted 'Stumpies and the odd Kob' post: it appears only in a cached Sealine search summary
The exact May 2025 jacita.co.za post reporting chokka 'in full force around Kalk Bay' (boat-based)
Any harbour-management rule on angling from the breakwater: none published was found and the DFFE harbour office was not contacted
Parking layout and fees at the harbour car park, and the car park position
Whether the 25 October to 22 November chokka closed season quoted in 2010 still applies to recreational jigging
Exact position and line of the main breakwater: OSM holds no breakwater way, so the stand is interpolated from the harbour centroid and the breakwater-head light
The 15 kg kob of 2009 (hearsay in the thread)
Lure fishing for elf and kob at this wall: the threads only describe bait and squid jigs

issues: Legality holds up. The cached Wikipedia TMNP MPA page gives the St James restricted zone as running from the Kalk Bay tidal pool (S34 07.567 E018 27.050 = -34.1261, 18.4508) north-east to the St James tidal pool, with its southern edge along latitude 34 07.567 S. The breakwater head light (-34.1283) and the stand (-34.1286) are about 240 to 280 m south of that line, so they sit in the controlled zone. The cached acts.co.za Reg 10(f)(iv) closed area also ends at 'the northern wall of the tidal pool situated opposite Kalk Bay Station' and does not mention the harbour. A cached SANParks State of Knowledge search summary agrees ('between the tidal pool at St James and the tidal pool at Kalk Bay'). The record cites Wikipedia, not the gazette or SANParks, and no harbour-management rule was found either way. That gap is honestly listed under unverified.

Some casting room is lost. A long north-east cast from the lighthouse end 'towards the Bbell' (BigBen, thread 61522) heads towards the no-take line about 245 m away. The hazard note covers this, but the page should say plainly not to fish from the Brass Bell or tidal-pool side north of the harbour.

The evidence is old and thin. Of the angling sources, 18908 is from 2009, 10269 from 2008, 3740 from 2008, 41656 from 2010, 61522 from 2012 and 79832 from 2013. Only 103491 is recent (2022), and it calls the spot poor ('Kalk bay sucks unless you want the kids catching hotties'). The 10269 poster only 'hoped' to catch elf or hottentot and reports no catch.

Elf: the method lists 'spinning', but no Kalk Bay source mentions lures. In thread 18908 'Lures are not mentioned', and in 10269 the spoons and poppers are for Zandvlei. The bait 'Sardine or chokka strip' is also not given for Kalk Bay elf; 3740's red bait, pencil bait and sardine were for an unnamed wall that caught only barber and small sharks.
Hottentot: the bait 'white mussel, red bait or chokka' is not attributed to Kalk Bay in any source. The 103491 bait list is generic for the whole thread. 'Common' rests on one 2022 post.
Maasbanker: 'sabiki flies' is not in any source.

species.size: Mostly small and undersize (limit 22 cm)
species.bait: Small hooks with white mussel, red bait or chokka dropped at the kelp near the middle of the wall
species.notes: 2022: "Kalk bay sucks unless you want the kids catching hotties at the kelp near the middle of the wall"; 2008 poster went there "hoping to catch a few elf or hottentot". Months given as all year because the two mentions are May and November, with no season stated.

species.size: Baitfish size; not reported
species.bait: Tiny hooks with sardine or chokka bits, or sabiki flies, fished mid-water off the wall
species.notes: "tons of maasbanker" from about September (2009); incidental catches in a March 2012 night session; none reported yet in mid-October 2010.

species.size: About a dozen squid came out in one dusk session (October 2010); daily limit 20
species.bait: Pink-top/yellow-bottom and small white squid jigs, an hour or two before and after sunset, earlier if cloudy
species.notes: A regular "fishes the Kalk Bay wall most nights, mainly for chokka"; the run is irregular ("No Chokka so far just about all year" in 2009). A cached May 2025 jacita.co.za report says chokka were "in full force around Kalk Bay, Fish Hoek, and Glencairn", mostly from boats. A 2010 post gives a closed season of 25 October to 22 November.

species.size: Mostly undersize fish (limit 30 cm) in summer; "nice size elf" reported in a January 2008 run
species.bait: Sardine or chokka strip on a light trace; small spoons and paddle-tails are the usual elf lures, though the Kalk Bay threads only mention bait
species.notes: "Undersize elf were common in summer"; "Caught a lot of Elf at K/Bay over Easter last year" (2009); "Some nice size elf have been coming out at Kalkies and at Baileys in the week" (2008); "the cob and shad run from time to time around the Kalkbay Harbour, but not for a while now". Larger fish at night; produces when the south-easter has been blowing.

species.size: Mostly undersize "bossiekob"; a 15 kg fish was claimed in 2009 as hearsay
species.bait: Sardine or chokka bait at night; paddle-tails are the standard light-tackle kob lure but are not mentioned for this wall
species.notes: 2022: undersize runs "off the end of the Kalk Bay wall"; 2009: "in all my time fishing kalk bay i've yet to see a size Kob"; to catch one "you need to be there most nights in the year"; "Larger fish tend to come out at night".

species.size: Not reported; "by the bags full" in earlier years, now the odd fish
species.bait: White mussel at night on the high tide ("switched bait to white mussel and immediately got hard knocks"); chokka also used
species.notes: March 2012: a white stumpnose from the lighthouse end, "the first one he'd seen come out there in a long time"; fish "were biting, especially on the high tide". A cached Sealine search summary also quotes a poster saying the wall is good for "Stumpies and the odd Kob". Bag and size limits differ between white and Cape stumpnose.

species.size: Not reported
species.bait: Chokka dropped against the vertical wall, casting towards the Brass Bell from the lighthouse end
species.notes: "romans are found on the vertical wall"; one member had caught a red roman from the jetty years earlier (thread from 2012).

species.size: Not given; one fish landed from the wall in 2009, "now that is a catch!"
species.bait: Spoons and plugs; a hard fish to land from the wall on light tackle
species.notes: Historic catches were huge (a book excerpt quoted on Sealine: 6,000 yellowtail from the harbour wall in one day in January 1920); today a single fish is an event.

name: Fish Hoek and Jager's Walk
aka: Fish Hoek beach and Jager's Walk
area: False Bay west, Fish Hoek
coord_source: Hand-placed at the south corner of the beach where the beach wall meets the start of Jager's Walk, using the Nominatim Fish Hoek Beach node (-34.1369724, 18.4342254, mid-beach, opened 29 October 2026) and Wikipedia's town fix (34°08'10"S 18°25'48"E). A Nominatim query for "Jager's Walk, Fish Hoek" returned no result, so the stand and car park are read off the map, not geocoded; the merge step's rough point was -34.1375, 18.433 (mid-beach).

access.note: Beach car park at the south end off Beach Road, beside the Fish Hoek Galley restaurant and the lifesaving club; Fish Hoek station is alongside. Jager's Walk starts at the beach wall here. Position hand-placed from the map, not geocoded.

bottom: Flat, gently shelving sand along the 1.5 km beach; rock ledges, kelp and rock pools along Jager's Walk on the southern side of the bay; a reef in mid-bay that boat anglers fish for kob is out of casting range.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine), bought at a Post Office; squid must be endorsed separately on the same form if you jig chokka (Ski-Boat 2022). National limits apply: galjoen closed 15 October to end February, 2 fish, 35 cm; elf closed 1 October to 30 November, 4 fish, 30 cm; white steenbras 1 fish, 60 cm; chokka bag limit 20 with closed seasons per the permit. If Regulation 10(f)(ii) is still enforced, the rocks south of the beach wall need a specific permit, so stay on the beach side until that is settled.
legality: Allowed with a permit, with one caveat for the rocks. Fish Hoek bay lies inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone: the St James restricted zone ends at the Kalk Bay tidal pool (S34 07.567) to the north and the Boulders restricted zone starts at Seaforth (S34 11.567) to the south, so neither no-take zone reaches Fish Hoek (Wikipedia TMNP MPA page, 2004 regulations) and angling is allowed on a DFFE recreational angling permit; Sealine members checked the same restricted-zone coordinates in 2009 and concluded "Fish Hoek is open and you fish anywhere". Caveat: the older MLRA Regulation 10(f)(ii) (GN R1111 of 1998, as still shown on acts.co.za) lists a closed area 500 m seaward of the high-water mark between "a line (090 degrees true bearing) drawn from Jager's Walk situated to the south of Fish Hoek Beach" and a similar line from the northern boundary of Glencairn Beach, where no one may fish "except on the authority of a permit". I could not confirm whether that clause survived the 2004 MPA zoning (DFFE's brochure, as quoted on Sealine, does not list it, and a web search found no current notice); it would cover the Jager's Walk rocks and Sunny Cove, not the beach or the Clovelly end. A 2018 Sealine remark that "areas in Fish Hoek are MPA and not good for fishing" may refer to it. Trek-net rights operate on the beach; City of Cape Town bathing-beach rules and the summer shark exclusion net were not checked. No SANParks fee applies here.
description: Fish Hoek's 1.5 km bathing beach sits in a bay that Wikipedia describes as "protected from the currents and stronger surf in the rest of False Bay"; trek-netters work the quieter northern end and a paved path, Jager's Walk (the "Cat Walk"), runs past rock pools from the south corner to Sunny Cove. Sealine members report that "winter Galjoen are good with a flick stick and drift line", a steenbras from Fish Hoek bay, and chokka and elf "between Dec and Feb near the station", while the local Fish Hoek guide notes "some fishing on the rocks along Jager's walk". It is a lukewarm spot by the sources' own account: "The best fishing spots around Fish Hoek are nowhere near Fish Hoek Beach!" and "Base yourself in Fish Hoek but don't fish Fish Hoek."
hazards: Great white sharks: fatal attacks in the bay in November 2004 and January 2010, and a serious injury in September 2011 while the beach was closed under a shark flag; obey the Shark Spotters flags and siren (Wikipedia)
Crime on Jager's Walk, especially after dark: a Sealine member who fished it since the 1980s wrote "I would not recommend fishing at night" because of muggings on the walkway
The walkway and its ledges take the full brunt of south-easterly swell; the August 2008 storm wrecked the path and closed it for 15 months
Trek-nets are hauled across the beach: keep clear of the nets, ropes and boats
Summer bathers, lifeguard flags and the shark exclusion net at the south corner leave little room to cast on the beach itself
Sand crabs strip bait before the fish find it on the sandy stretch (Sealine 2009)
access_notes: Park at the south end of the beach off Beach Road (restaurants and the children's play area are at this end per Wikipedia); Fish Hoek station on the Metrorail Southern Line is right there (about an hour from Cape Town, 15 minutes to Simon's Town). Jager's Walk, a paved path completed in 1933 and known locally as the Cat Walk, runs past the rock pools on the southern side of the bay from the beach to Sunny Cove, where there is a second station. The quieter northern (Clovelly) end is used by trek fishermen to launch boats and clean nets; give way to the nets. Lifesavers are on duty in the summer peak season, shark spotters most days, and a shark exclusion net is usually deployed at the beach in the early mornings in summer, so the bathing stretch is effectively off limits to casting on summer days. Dogs are allowed from Clovelly to the start of the walkway but not along the walkway to Sunny Cove (fishhoek.com, via search snippet). Sealine members advise against fishing the walkway at night because of crime, and the walkway was closed for 15 months after the August 2008 storm. Nearest tackle: Great White Tackle on Main Road opposite the station (Sealine 2013 and 2018). No gate fee.
unverified: Whether MLRA Regulation 10(f)(ii), the 500 m closed area from Jager's Walk to Glencairn Beach, is still in force after the 2004 TMNP MPA zoning; no current DFFE or City notice found
Tide preference: no source states one for Fish Hoek; 'pushing' is the general surf and rock convention
White steenbras months (spring to autumn) and the elf and chokka lures are general False Bay patterns, not stated for this spot
Typical sizes: no source gives sizes of fish caught here
Hottentot: named for the bay by a tourism guide only, no angling source, so left off the species list
Smoothhound sharks and 'occasional big sandies' were mentioned by Sealine members as bait catches; sharks and rays left out of the species list
Kob: the only shore kob reports are from the Clovelly rocks (separate candidate) and boats off Fish Hoek in easterly winds, so kob is not listed here
Yellowtail enter the bay but the only catches cited are trek-net hauls, not rod and line
Parking at the south-end car park and at Sunny Cove is from the map, not from a cached page
City of Cape Town bathing-area and shark-exclusion-net rules on casting from the beach in summer not checked
Stand and car park coordinates are hand-placed (see coord_source)
The 2018 remark 'areas in Fish Hoek are MPA and not good for fishing' was never explained in the thread
legal_note: Jager's Walk is the start of a closed area in the 1998 fishing regulations (regulation 10(f)(ii): from Jager's Walk to Glencairn Beach, 500 m out to sea, no fishing 'except on the authority of a permit'). DFFE's current brochure no longer lists it, but no official page confirms it is open. Fish Hoek beach north of Jager's Walk is outside it but is a bathing beach: the City's by-law bans fishing within 100 m of a signed bathing area.

issues: Legality holds under the 2004 zoning. The pin at -34.1396 (S34 08.38) lies between the St James restricted zone, which ends at the Kalk Bay tidal pool (S34 07.567), and the Boulders zone, which starts at Seaforth (S34 11.567) (Wikipedia TMNP MPA page, cached 29 Oct 2026). That puts it in the controlled zone. Sealine 2009 (thread 26561) reached the same conclusion: 'Fish Hoek is open and you fish anywhere'.

The Reg 10(f)(ii) caveat in the record is honest, but the record misses evidence in its own cited source that the clause was superseded. The same 1998 regulation (acts.co.za r1111_10) also closes (f)(iii), from Neptune's Corner at Muizenberg to the St James tidal pool. That stretch takes in Bailey's Cottage, which the 2004 zoning makes the start of the controlled zone and which Sealine members recommend for fishing (threads 79832 in 2013 and 99465 in 2018). (f)(iv) is also the same stretch as the 2004 St James restricted zone. Both point to (f)(i) to (f)(iv) being replaced by the 2004 MPA zoning. This is still an inference: I found no repeal notice. A web search to confirm it was refused because the session's search budget was used up, not because of an IT block.

The record leaves out contrary evidence from a source it cites. Sealine thread 62041 (2012) has a member saying 'I was told u cant fish from fish hoek beach', while another member said anglers fish from Glencairn to Simonstown. This should go in the legality text next to the 2018 'areas in Fish Hoek are MPA' remark. Separately, City of Cape Town bathing-area rules were not checked.

There is an internal inconsistency. The spot is named and described as 'Fish Hoek beach and Jager's Walk', and the reason promotes rock fishing on Jager's Walk. But the pin sits exactly where Jager's Walk starts, which is the northern boundary line of the possible 10(f)(ii) closed area, and the permit field tells anglers to 'stay on the beach side'. The record should not promote the walkway rocks while it also tells people to avoid them.

The quote 'some fishing on the rocks along Jager's walk' attributed to the local Fish Hoek guide does not appear anywhere in the cached evidence, and fishhoek.com/pages/fishing.html was blocked. The only cached angling mention of the walkway is Wayne in Sealine 2009, recalling fishing 'Venus Pool' along the walkway in the early 1980s. The fishhoek.com dog-rule snippet and the Wikipedia 'protected from the currents' quote are also not in this spot's cached evidence, so I could not check them here.

Much of the angling evidence is about the Clovelly (north) end, not the south-corner pin. The 2009 thread's question was about the Clovelly side near the Catamaran Club, and the moderator's rock catches were 'below Clovelly station'. 'Between the station and the point just past the pool' could mean Clovelly station and Wooley's Pool just as well as Fish Hoek station and Venus Pool. The 2018 thread and seasidecottages both recommend Clovelly, not Fish Hoek, for winter galjoen.

name: Clovelly corner
aka: Clovelly corner and the Silvermine River mouth
Clovelly side of Fish Hoek beach
area: Clovelly / Fish Hoek, False Bay west
coord_source: Derived, not geocoded: Nominatim's Fish Hoek Beach node (-34.1369724, 18.4342254, cached 29 Oct 2026) is the beach centroid; the Clovelly corner and Silvermine mouth lie about 500 m north-east of it along the beach, so the stand was placed at -34.1340, 18.4383 by dead reckoning (about 150 m uncertainty). The rocks below Clovelly station are roughly -34.1325, 18.4405 on the same basis. The one allowed Photon query ("Clovelly station", biased to -34.133, 18.44) returned only UK matches, and the earlier Nominatim query for "Clovelly Beach, Cape Town" returned nothing, so no better fix exists.

access.note: Beach car park at the Clovelly (north) end of Fish Hoek beach, off Main Road by the sailing club and Silvermine wetland; position is dead reckoning, about 150 m uncertainty. For the rocks below Clovelly station, the finders' notes mention a gravel parking area by the station on Main Road (M4) with the rocks around the bend; not verified in the cached pages.

bottom: Sand at the corner and across the Silvermine mouth (the 2009 thread warns that sand crabs strip baits here), grading into a sand-and-rock seam against the Clovelly rocks; below Clovelly station the shore is low boulder reef and gullies with kelp and sand patches, with Wooley's walled tidal pool on the shelf toward Kalk Bay. Bottom detail is from map geography and general knowledge of the bay, not from an angling source.
mouth: Not an estuary fishery: the Silvermine River runs across the north end of Fish Hoek beach into the sea in winter and shrinks to a trickle in summer (search snippets from the Fish Hoek Valley Wikipedia page and the fishhoek.com beach guide); the lower Silvermine wetland upstream of Main Road is a City-rehabilitated floodplain. No managed breaching was reported.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (the marine permit) for the TMNP MPA controlled zone; no SANParks entry fee or activity permit here (those apply only in the Cape of Good Hope section). Bait collection also needs the permit. Species rules to check in the current DFFE brochure: galjoen closed 15 Oct to end Feb (the Feb 2018 thread confirms the season was closed then), elf closed Oct-Nov, white steenbras bag 1 at 60 cm, silver kob bag 1 at 50 cm, roman bag 2 at 30 cm (figures from memory of the brochure, unverified).
legality: Allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit. The spot is inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, and against the 2004 restricted-zone coordinates (Wikipedia TMNP MPA page, cached 29 Oct 2026) it falls in the controlled zone: the St James no-take zone starts at the Kalk Bay tidal pool (S34 07.567 E018 27.050), about 1.2 km north-east of Clovelly station, and the Boulders zone starts at Seaforth (S34 11.567 E018 26.762), about 6.5 km south, so Clovelly corner (-34.134, 18.438) and the station rocks (-34.1325, 18.4405) lie between them. The Sealine 2009 thread reached the same conclusion from the same zone list: "Fish Hoek is open and you fish anywhere as the above says nothing about closed areas in Fish Hoek". Caveat: the finders flagged the old MLRA R1111 Regulation 10 closed-areas list on acts.co.za, which bars fishing without a permit in a 500 m strip "from Jager's Walk to the northern boundary of Glencairn beach"; Jager's Walk is at the south end of Fish Hoek beach and the strip runs south from there, away from Clovelly, so it would not cover this spot even if still in force. I could not open that page to confirm the wording (see blocked_urls). A Feb 2018 Sealine poster's "Areas in Fish Hoek are MPA and not good for fishing" names no zone, and the same thread recommends Clovelly for winter galjoen. The Kalk Bay harbour master's local fishing restrictions apply to the harbour, not here.
description: The north-east corner of Fish Hoek bay, where the Silvermine River crosses the sand in winter, plus the low rocks and gullies under Clovelly station running toward Wooley's tidal pool. A sheltered, shallow corner of sand and reef edge that anglers share with trek-net crews and bathers; local forum posters rate it a winter galjoen spot ("Winter Galjoen are good with a flick stick and drift line"), with dassie, zebra and the odd kob off the station rocks and roman at Wooley's pool on redbait.
hazards: Trek-net boats launch and beach-seine nets are hauled on the Clovelly end of the beach: keep lines clear of the net and boats

Bathing beach with lifeguards and shark spotters: white sharks patrol Fish Hoek and Clovelly in summer (Sealine 2011 shark-warning threads; a shark attack 'in the clovelly area' in Sep 2011), so do not wade deep and heed the shark flags and siren
Sand crabs strip baits on the sand before fish find them (Enigma, Sealine 2009)
Slippery, tackle-grabbing reef below the station, with the working railway line directly behind the rocks: cross only at an official crossing
Crime at night: a 2009 poster advised against night fishing along the Fish Hoek walkway; fish in daylight or in company
access_notes: Free, open beach, no gate or fee; a few minutes' walk across the sand from the Clovelly-end car park to the corner and river mouth. Lifeguards and shark spotters are on duty at Clovelly Beach in season (seasidecottages), so fish away from the bathing area and heed the shark flags and siren. Trek-net crews launch boats and clean nets on this northern stretch, so keep lines clear of a net being shot. For the station rocks, Clovelly station is on Main Road between Fish Hoek and Kalk Bay; cross the railway only at an official crossing. The Sealine Apr 2019 thread's advice was that most Cape Town bank spots "are safe during the day"; a 2009 poster advised against night fishing along the Fish Hoek walkway because of crime. Tackle: Great White Tackle on Main Road opposite Fish Hoek station (Sealine 2018). Permit: DFFE recreational angling permit; galjoen closed season (15 Oct to end Feb; the Feb 2018 thread confirms the season was closed then) and the Oct-Nov elf closed season apply (check the current DFFE brochure).
unverified: Stand and car-park coordinates are dead reckoning from the Nominatim beach centroid (about 150 m uncertainty); the one allowed Photon query returned only UK results

Wording and current status of the MLRA R1111 Regulation 10(f)(ii) 'Jager's Walk to the northern boundary of Glencairn beach' 500 m closed strip: the acts.co.za page could not be opened (the fetcher will not follow its https-to-http redirect and a direct curl was refused by the permission classifier); its position south of Clovelly rests on the finders' quote plus map geography
No source states a tide preference for this stand, so tide_pref is 'any'
Elf months Dec-Feb come from the finders' note on a Fish Hoek station post at the south end of the bay, not a Clovelly-specific source
Parking 'gravel lot by the station / rocks around the bend' is from the finders' notes and was not found in the cached pages; which station is meant is unclear

Hottentot and yellowtail are reported for Fish Hoek bay in general (a tourism guide) and for the station rocks and Sunny Cove at the south end of the bay, not for Clovelly, so they were left off the species list
Smoothhounds (Enigma, 2009) are bait-caught sharks and belong in notes, not the species list
Shelter, bottom and depth descriptors are from map geography and general knowledge of Fish Hoek bay, not from an angling source
Size, bag-limit and closed-season figures are from memory of the DFFE recreational brochure, except that the Feb 2018 thread confirms galjoen season was closed in February
The whole bay's shore-fishing reputation is dated: the 2009 and 2018 threads are the main angling sources, and a 2018 poster said 'Base yourself in Fish Hoek but don't fish Fish Hoek'

issues: Legality holds. The St James no-take zone in the cached Wikipedia TMNP MPA page starts at the Kalk Bay tidal pool (S34 07.567 E018 27.050, i.e. -34.1261, 18.4508) and runs north-east to St James. The station rocks (-34.1325, 18.4405) are about 1.2 km south-west of that point, and the corner (-34.134, 18.438) is further away still. The Boulders zone starts at Seaforth (-34.1928), about 6.5 km south. Clovelly is in the controlled zone, where fishing needs a DFFE recreational permit. The 2009 Sealine thread reaches the same conclusion: 'Fish Hoek is open and you fish anywhere'.

The MLRA R1111 Reg 10 closed-areas page could not be fetched again. https://www.acts.co.za/marine-living-resources-act-1998/r1111_10__closed_areas.php 302-redirects to the http URL, the fetcher upgrades that back to https, and it loops, so treat the page as blocked. The 'Jager's Walk to Glencairn' strip is still unverified. If the quoted wording is right it lies at the south end of the bay, away from Clovelly.

Unchecked legal caveat: the aka list includes Wooley's Tidal Pool, and the roman entry has people fishing 'at Wooley's pool'. City of Cape Town tidal pools and lifeguarded bathing areas may carry by-law or signage bans on fishing. No source in the evidence checks this, so the page should say to fish the rocks beside the pool, not the pool itself, and to obey any signs.

Evidence is thin but real and angling-specific. The 2009 Sealine thread 26561 has Enigma: 'Caught Dassie, Zebra and Kob from rocks below Clovelly station' and 'Winter Galjoen are good with a flick stick and drift line'. In the same thread Dorado75 says 'the corner at Clovelly for large Steenbras'. The 2018 Sealine thread 99465 says 'Clovelly: Recommended in winter for galjoen'. A flick stick with a drift line is light bait fishing, so this fits the page's style. The 2019 thread 101259 only names 'Clovely, just past Kalk Bay' as a bank-session spot, in a Freshwater Venues sub-forum, with no species or method.

The sources list cites pages that are not in the 29 Oct cache. https://sealine.co.za/search/search?keywords=clovelly returned only 'You've hit your session limit', so it was never read. Sealine thread 100519 (Arniston's steenbras and musselcracker quote) and the three shark threads (54135, 45390, 55230) do not appear in the evidence file at all. fishhoek.com, wheretostay.co.za and the Fish_Hoek_Valley Wikipedia page appear only as search snippets. Quotes attributed to those pages cannot be checked here: the Sep 2011 'shark attack in the clovelly area' and 'often caught White Steenbras... and the occasionally musselcracker'.

Coordinates cannot be refuted, and they cannot be confirmed either. My Nominatim query for 'Clovelly' (bounded to the area) returned only the suburb centroid at -34.1248, 18.4332, which is inland and no use for the shore. The only beach fix is the Fish Hoek Beach node at -34.13697, 18.43423. The record's stand is about 500 m north-east of that node, on the Clovelly arm of the beach, and the station rocks (-34.1325, 18.4405) are consistent with Clovelly station on the M4. Both are dead reckoning, uncertain to about 150-300 m, which is acceptable but should stay listed as unverified.

name: Glencairn Quarry
aka: Glencairn beach to Sunny Cove rocks
area: Glencairn (Simon's Town), west shore of False Bay
coord_source: Rough coordinates kept from the merge step: the OSM node for the Old Quarry (False Bay Sports Shooting Club) on the M4 Main Road between Sunny Cove and Glencairn. A nominatim search for the shooting club on 30 October 2026 returned no result, so the stand was not re-geocoded. The stand is the rocky outcrop directly below the quarry, seaward of the railway line, within about 100 m east of this point; Glencairn Beach (nominatim, cached 29 October 2026) is at -34.1599, 18.4317, about 800 m to the south-south-west.

access.note: Lay-by/car park at the quarry on the seaward side of the M4 Main Road ('Theres a car park on the western side of the quarry (seaside of the road)' - Enigma, Sealine 2010), then through the gate over the railway line and down to the rocks. Position approximate: same merge node, not geocoded.

bottom: Rocky outcrop with a very foul, snaggy reef bottom in front ("a very rocky, foul bottom. Lost a lot of sinkers" - Sealine 2010), boulders ("the bricks") and kelp; the ground to the right has "a lot less structure on the bottom" and is where steenbras have been landed.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (rod and line, sold at Post Offices), with the national size and bag limits; elf closed season 1 October to 30 November; white steenbras bag limit 1 and 60 cm minimum, so release the "steenies". No SANParks permit at this spot. If the 1998 reg 10(f)(ii) Fish Hoek-Glencairn closed area is still in force, fishing there is "except on the authority of a permit", which the recreational permit may or may not satisfy.
legality: Allowed with a DFFE recreational angling (rod and line) permit. The rocks lie in the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone: the Boulders restricted zone starts at Seaforth (S34 11.567 E018 26.762), about 4 km south, and the St James restricted zone ends at the Kalk Bay tidal pool, about 7 km north; the remainder is controlled and "fishing is allowed in the controlled zone of the MPA subject to permits" (Wikipedia TMNP MPA, read 29 and 30 October 2026; westerncape.gov.za: "You need a permit to fish along the shoreline"). No SANParks entry fee or activity permit applies here (only inside the Cape of Good Hope section). Caveat checked and unresolved: the 1998 MLRA regulations (R1111 reg 10(f)(ii), acts.co.za) describe a 500 m closed area "except on the authority of a permit" from Jager's Walk south of Fish Hoek beach to the northern boundary of Glencairn beach, which covers these rocks if the quarry is north of the beach as the OSM-based coordinate indicates. Neither the Wikipedia MPA article nor any Sealine poster mentions it; a 2009 poster citing the MPA zones says "Fish Hoek is open and you fish anywhere", a 2012 poster had "seen anglers fishing from Glencairn to Simonstown", and in 2014 "anglers frequent the rocks directly below Glen Cairn Quarry". Treat the old clause as superseded in practice but not confirmed on paper. Not a bathing beach, so no bather conflict at the rocks; keep off Glencairn's swimming beach with bait.
description: Rocky outcrop below the railway line at the old Glencairn quarry (now a shooting range) on the M4 between Sunny Cove and Glencairn beach, on the west shore of False Bay. Sealine anglers call it "a great spot to start out with dropshot" and fish it with a fly rod or light spinning combo and 6 lb line: red bait or a prawn cast without a sinker on low tide for hottentot, roman, blacktail, strepie and steentjie over a very foul bottom, and spoons on January-to-March mornings for yellowtail and bonito. A south-easter makes it rough, and the elf, steenbras, geelbek and red stumpnose in the reports are occasional fish.
hazards: Very foul, snaggy reef bottom: 'Lost a lot of sinkers' (Sealine 2010); fish light sinkers, a drift line or no sinker at all
Rough water in a south-easter; waves wash the rocks and fish get 'cut off by the rocks while waiting for a wave'; floats get blown 'inshore, onto the bricks'
Live railway line (Metrorail Southern Line) between the car park and the rocks: cross only at the gate and watch for trains
Active shooting range in the quarry above (False Bay Sports Shooting Club): stay on the seaward side of the road and railway

Big pyjama sharks take baits here and below Glencairn station ('some of the biggest Pajama sharks you'll ever catch'); smoothhound and gully shark were once taken off the Clan Stewart wreck beach on heavy tackle but a 2014 poster says 'we don't get any smoothies or spotties anymore'

Crime: fish in company ('only advisable in groups', Sealine 2012); avoid night sessions on this stretch (Sealine 2009 warning for Fish Hoek); robberies of anglers reported along the False Bay coast (IOL)
Yellowtail and bonito will outclass ultra-light gear and a seal may take a hooked fish
access_notes: Park at the quarry car park on the seaward side of the M4 between Sunny Cove and Glencairn beach, cross the Metrorail Southern Line through the gate and scramble down to the rocky outcrop below the line (Sealine 2010: "Below the railway line is a rocky outcrop where I went fishing"). Short walk, no gate fee, no hours. The quarry above is an active shooting range (False Bay Sports Shooting Club). Next-door alternatives named by the same posters: "the water behind the pool and below the Glencairn station" (Sealine 2010) and the rocks by Glencairn station (Sealine 2013); the Clan Stewart wreck beach is the heavy-tackle shark and flatfish spot (Sealine 2014), not a light-tackle venue. Bait and tackle: Great White on Fish Hoek Main Road (Sealine 2013). Sealine advice (2012) is that False Bay shore fishing is "only advisable in groups"; a 2009 poster warned against night fishing on the Fish Hoek walkways because of crime, and an IOL report cited anglers saying the Muizenberg-Gordon's Bay coast had become unsafe because of robberies. Pick up the litter left by others, as the 2010 poster did.
unverified: Exact position of the quarry, its car park and the stand: the merge's OSM node (-34.154, 18.4366) puts the Old Quarry about 800 m north-east of Glencairn beach, between Sunny Cove and Glencairn; a nominatim search for the False Bay Sports Shooting Club returned nothing, so it was not re-geocoded. Enigma's 'car park on the western side of the quarry (seaside of the road)' is internally odd since the sea is to the east; read it as the seaward-side lay-by at the quarry.

Current status of MLRA R1111 reg 10(f)(ii), the 500 m closed area from Jager's Walk to the northern boundary of Glencairn beach ('except on the authority of a permit'): not confirmed whether it survived the 2004 TMNP MPA zoning or whether a recreational permit satisfies it. The Wikipedia MPA article is silent on it; the finders and local anglers treat the stretch as controlled zone.
Depth ('medium') and facing bearing (about 105 degrees) are inferred from the map and from the posters' remarks about the south-easter, not stated by any source.
Typical sizes: no source gives measurements beyond 'big Hotties', 'a little hottie', 'small hotties' and 'a few nice steenies'.

Galjoen, smoothhound/gully shark and sand shark appear in the merge list from general False Bay reports or from the Clan Stewart wreck beach, not from the quarry rocks, so they are left out of the species list.

The Sealine 'lure fishing cape town area' thread (56615) is cited from the finders' notes ('Simonstown, along the rail track: yellowtail'; Simon's Town to Fish Hoek yellowtail 'on spoons and lures') and was not reopened in this pass; the 'kob on lure plastics false bay' thread in the merge sources had no Glencairn content in the notes and is omitted.
The drive times (18 min from Westlake, 41 min from Green Point) are the merge's OSRM free-flow estimates, not from any angling source.
Angling reports are from 2010-2014; no post-2014 shore report for the quarry rocks was found (the 2025 Jacita chokka mention does not say shore or boat).

issues: LEGALITY CAVEAT IS LIVE, NOT HYPOTHETICAL: the reverse geocode (nominatim reverse, fetched 2 Nov 2026) puts -34.154, 18.4366 on Simonstown Road (M4) in the Fish Hoek suburb (Ward 64), north of Glencairn Beach (nominatim -34.1599, 18.4317) and south of Jager's Walk. Big Gray (Sealine 28775) places the outcrop directly below the railway at the quarry, and Seeker1 says the rock went 'to the railway siding at Fish Hoek'. So the stand sits inside the 1998 MLRA R1111 reg 10(f)(ii) area (500 m seaward, from Jager's Walk to the northern boundary of Glencairn Beach/Elsebaai: 'No person shall, except on the authority of a permit... engage in fishing', acts.co.za). The record does flag this, but its legality field opens with a flat 'Allowed'. It should lead with the caveat. Comparable 10(f)(iii) ground, such as Bailey's Cottage, is fished openly.

MPA check passes: -34.154 lies between the St James restricted zone (Kalk Bay pool, S34 07.567 = -34.126) and the Boulders restricted zone (Seaforth, S34 11.567 = -34.193), about 4.3 km north of Seaforth. That is controlled zone, and angling there needs a DFFE permit (Wikipedia TMNP MPA; westerncape.gov.za: 'You need a permit to fish along the shoreline'). species.size: Mostly small to pan-size ('a little hottie', 'a couple of small hotties'), with 'big Hotties' reported in 2010; no measurements given

name: Simon's Town railway line
aka: Simon's Town railway line (Dido Valley to Long Beach)
Dido Valley below the traffic lights
area: Simon's Town, False Bay west shore
coord_source: Rough coordinates from the merge step, kept: the OSM/Nominatim centroid of Long Beach (-34.18604, 18.42577; nominatim query "Long Beach, Simon's Town", opened 29 October 2026). The fished rocks run north from here along the railway line for roughly 1.5 km past the lower North Battery to the Dido Valley traffic lights (Nominatim puts Dido Valley Road at -34.1689, 18.4237 and Simon's Town station at -34.1868, 18.4255). The exact gun-battery stand was not geocoded.

access.note: Simon's Town station and Long Beach, off Main Road (M4) at the north end of town (station position from Nominatim). Park here and walk north along the shore and the railway line to the rocks; the Dido Valley traffic-light end can also be reached from Main Road.

bottom: Rock and kelp along the railway-line stretch, with the sandy trek-net beach of Long Beach at the south end (Ski-Boat lists Long Beach as a beach-seine area; Sealine posters fish "on the rocks"). Not described in detail by any source.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine). Inside the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone; no SANParks entry fee or activity permit applies here (that is only inside the Cape of Good Hope section). Normal DFFE bag and size limits apply to yellowtail.
legality: Allowed with a permit. The stand (about -34.186, 18.426) and the railway stretch north of it lie between Glencairn and Simon's Town station, north of the naval harbour and north of Seaforth (S34 11.567 E018 26.762, about -34.193, 18.446), where the Boulders restricted (no-take) zone begins under the 2004 TMNP MPA regulations (Wikipedia MPA page, opened 29 October 2026); the St James no-take zone is about 8 km north. Everything between is TMNP MPA controlled zone, where angling is allowed with a valid DFFE recreational angling permit. Checked: the coordinates of all six restricted zones against the stand. A 2012 Sealine poster's claim that "the Simonstown coast is a protected area because of the penquin colony" was answered in the same thread by advice to consult the MPA boundaries; the penguin-colony no-take zone starts at Seaforth, south of the harbour, not here.
description: A stretch of rocky shore between Glencairn and Simon's Town station where the Southern Line railway hugs the coast, fished by shore spinners for yellowtail when the fish come inshore in summer. Sealine posters call the railway tracks "a frequent summer spot", say anglers are "usually" seen spinning the gun battery area "when the conditions are tight", and warn that "the trick here is to fish only when the yellowtail are present"; one adds that Simonstown otherwise "doesnt yield much from the shore". Long Beach at the south end is a sandy trek-net beach; the fishing is off the rocks north of it.
hazards: Live railway line along the whole stretch: walk beside the track and cross with care
Low, kelp-covered rocks that are slippery; a long gaff is recommended for landing yellowtail
Trek nets are shot off Long Beach; keep clear of the net crews
Summer south-easter blows straight onto this shore and builds chop
Seals take hooked fish
Car break-ins and muggings are a general Cape coast risk; a 2012 poster advised fishing this coast in groups
Lower North Battery is a naval site; do not enter fenced property
access_notes: Public shore with no gate or fee (outside the Cape of Good Hope section of the park, so no SANParks fee). Parking by Long Beach and Simon's Town station at the north end of town, then a walk north along the shore beside the railway line; the finders also noted a 2013 Sealine line about parking "just past the turnoff toward Scarborough/Red Hill", which this pass could not open. The Southern Line railway runs along this shore, so you walk beside a live track. Long Beach itself is a beach-seine (trek-net) beach per Ski-Boat; give the net crews right of way and fish the rocks, not the net area. Simon's Town is a navy town and the Lower North Battery is a naval site, so stay on the public shore and rail side of any fence. A 2012 Sealine poster advised that shore fishing on this coast is "only advisable in groups", and a 2022 thread carried a general warning about muggings on the Cape coast; do not leave valuables in the car. Drive: about 19 min from Westlake and 42 min from Green Point (OSRM free-flow estimate, 2026-10-29); no source gives a drive time.
unverified: Hottentot and katonkel/bonito, listed by the finders for this spot: no cached page or opened thread names them here (the only 'hotties' line in the 2022 Sealine thread refers to Kalk Bay)

Mackerel: 'Mackerel runs from time to time, but usually going for chokka, I think same with simonstown' (Sealine 2022) is town-wide and does not say shore; The Mission Fly Mag's Atlantic mackerel on a stripped Clouser 'near Simon's Town harbour' comes from a cached search summary with no article URL identified
'Simon's Town just north of the main beach is popular for yellow tail when they are around' appears in a cached search summary of Sealine threads; the specific thread was not identified

Parking 'just past the turnoff toward Scarborough/Red Hill' (finders' note citing a 2013 Sealine thread, probably https://sealine.co.za/threads/lure-fishing-the-surf.80509/) was not opened in this pass
Depth, bottom and swell shelter are read from the geography and the 'on the rocks' wording, not stated by a source
Facing bearing (about 75 degrees) estimated from map geometry
Typical yellowtail size here is not given by any source
Whether shore access in front of the Lower North Battery is restricted by the navy
Chokka jigging from these rocks is implied by the 2022 'usually going for chokka' line but not stated for the shore

issues: Legality holds (Wikipedia TMNP MPA page, cached 29 Oct 2026). The Boulders restricted zone runs from Seaforth (S34 11.567 E018 26.762) out to S34 10.581 E018 27.196, then east to E018 27.781 and south to Rocklands. Its northern edge does reach S34 10.581 (about -34.176), the same latitude as the Dido Valley end of this stretch, but only at E018 27.2 to 27.8 (lon 18.453 to 18.463), about 2.5 km offshore to the east. The railway shore (lon about 18.425 to 18.43) and the stand (-34.186, 18.426) are outside it. St James is about 7 km north. So this is controlled zone and needs a DFFE permit. The record's wording 'north of Seaforth, where the Boulders zone begins' is a simplification, but its conclusion is right.

Two cached posts contradict the record without overturning it. Sealine 'simonstown' 66576 (2012) says 'All fishing in Simonstown area is done from boats' and 'the Simonstown coast is a protected area because of the penquin colony'. A cached search summary says 'from Simon's Town to Cape point is mostly No fishing areas'. The MPA coordinates show neither applies to the stretch north of the station.

Not checked against any source: the access note tells anglers to walk along and beside the live Southern Line track. The railway reserve is PRASA property, and walking on it away from a designated crossing may count as trespass. The note should tell anglers to use public shore access points rather than the track bed.

Several quotes in the record are not in any raw cache file in the scratchpad (salvage/*.jsonl, research_cache.jsonl). They appear only in derived files (candidates.json, verify_in/*.json): the 2010 'lower north battery, dido valley - just below the traffic lights' (thread 28177), the 2023 'Simonstown should start hotting up in oct' and 'join us on the rocks for a yellowtail in simonstown' (thread 103787), and 'the odd Yellowtail on spinners from the gun battery area in the Summer months'. Neither thread 28177 nor 103787 is cached anywhere. These quotes cannot be confirmed from the 29 October pass, and they are what the record uses for the stand location and for currency.

The parts that are confirmed come from cached angling-specific pages. Sealine 11644 (Dec 2008) names 'Railway tracks, Simon's Town' as a frequent summer spot and says anglers are 'usually' seen spinning the 'gun battery area (between Fish Hoek and Simon's Town station)' 'when the conditions are tight'. Sealine 7316 (cached in salvage/falsebay-east.jsonl) has 'Simons Town, along the train line: The trick here is to fish only when the yellowtail are present!!'. With 2008 and 2013 as the newest verified sources, the evidence is thin and dated.

The record says the 2013 thread https://sealine.co.za/threads/lure-fishing-the-surf.80509/ 'could not be opened'. It was opened and is cached (salvage/falsebay-west.jsonl, research_cache.jsonl): 'Simon's Town: Popular for yellowtail when present, with parking just past the turnoff toward Scarborough/Red Hill.' It is a third independent angling source and should be cited. The Red Hill (M66) turnoff was not geocoded, so where that parking is relative to the railway stretch is still unknown.

species.size: Not stated by any source for this spot. Unverified: False Bay shore yellowtail are usually a few kilograms, with the odd much bigger fish.
species.bait: Spoons, plugs and poppers cast at surface-feeding fish; Sealine posters say bring a rod and reel "that can take the pace" (an 11 ft yellowtail rod was recommended over a 10 ft one, which was called too light) and a long gaff. Ski-Boat lists spoons, jigs, poppers and 12 to 14 cm diving hard baits for Cape yellowtail. No bait fishing is mentioned for this spot.
species.notes: Run-dependent: "Railway tracks, Simon's Town" is named as "a frequent summer spot" and anglers are "usually" seen spinning the "gun battery area (between Fish Hoek and Simon's Town station)" "when the conditions are tight" (Sealine 2008), but catches are "the odd Yellowtail on spinners from the gun battery area in the Summer months" and "the trick here is to fish only when the yellowtail are present!!" (Sealine 2008, 2010); "They're there 1 day, and gone the next." A 2023 poster said "Simonstown should start hotting up in oct" and invited others to "join us on the rocks for a yellowtail in simonstown". Conditions: a south-easter that has blown for at least three days, or a few days after a north-wester when the fish "come closer into shore"; yellowtail respond to wind and water temperature more than tide; Ski-Boat says water of 15 C or warmer and clean blue water, early starts, and feeding terns as the sign. Seals steal hooked fish. At the heavy end of light tackle: a stout spinning outfit with braid, not a dropshot rod.

name: Miller's Point
area: Murdock Valley, Simon's Town (False Bay, west shore)
coord_source: Wikivoyage Miller's Point slipway page (cached 29 Oct 2026): slipway ramp S34°13'49.63" E018°28'25.12" converted from DMS (the page's decimal latitude -34.830 is a typo). The fishable rocks and small beach are immediately beside and north of this ramp. The merge-step rough coordinate (-34.2328, 18.474) is the main gate, kept as the access point. No nominatim query run.

access.note: Main gates off Main Road (M4), Wikivoyage GPS S34°13'58.58" E018°28'26.46"; the service road runs north to the paved public car park beside the slipway, about 250 m from the gate. Park there and walk a few metres to the rocks.

bottom: Granite rock and loose boulders with dense kelp close inshore ("Lotsa rocky areas and kelp", "near the kelp towards the loose rocks in the water"), a short sandy beach in the slipway cove, sand beyond the kelp line.
permit: DFFE (Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment) recreational angling permit, sold at Post Offices, is the permit for angling in the TMNP MPA controlled zone; national bag and size limits and closed seasons apply (galjoen closed season and the tight red roman limits matter here). No SANParks activity permit or gate fee at Miller's Point itself (it is outside the Cape of Good Hope section); the City charges a boat launch fee and "a parking fee is sometimes charged, in unpredictable amounts" (Wikivoyage).
legality: Allowed with a permit on the north (slipway) side only. Checked against the 2004 TMNP MPA regulations as transcribed on Wikipedia (cached 29 Oct 2026): the Castle Rock restricted (no-take) zone runs "offshore from the high-water mark between Partridge Point (S34°15.480' E018°28.344') and Millers Point (S34°14.100' E018°28.508')", with its northern edge running due east from the Millers Point beacon VB1 (about -34.2350, 18.4751) and the zone extending about one nautical mile seaward. The slipway ramp (-34.2305) and the rocks north of it lie roughly 500 m north of that line, inside the MPA controlled zone where "fishing is allowed in the controlled zone of the MPA subject to permits". Ski-Boat magazine (Angler Publications) gives the same definition ("Castle Rock: between beacons VB1 at Miller's Point and VB2 at Partridge Point, extending one nautical mile seaward") and the 2014 Sealine shore thread says "Make sure you fish to the North of the VB1 beacon" and "The Cape Point side of Millers is a Marine Reserve". Wikipedia's Miller's Point article confirms that around the point "since being established as a marine sanctuary, inshore fishing has been prohibited". So the point itself, Rumbly Bay, Castle Rock and Smitswinkel are no fishing; a 2012 Sealine poster placed the reserve edge "around the millers point clubhouse", so locate the VB1 beacon on site and stay north of it. Miller's Point is outside the Cape of Good Hope pay section of the park, so no SANParks gate fee or activity permit should apply here (SANParks' TMNP fishing page could not be opened: HTTP 403).
description: Miller's Point is the ski-boat slipway headland about 4 km south of Simon's Town on the M4 to Cape Point, and the City of Cape Town lists "Fishing and angling" among its activities, noting the beach "is mainly used by anglers and divers". Light-tackle shore fishing is confined to the kelpy granite rocks and small beach on the north (slipway) side: a 2014 Sealine thread on fishing here from the shore says "Hottentot will be the order of the day, possibly Red Roman, water is a bit calm for Galjoen" and warns "Make sure you fish to the North of the VB1 beacon", because the point itself and everything south of it is the Castle Rock no-take zone. The point shields the cove from south-easterly chop and most wrapping swell, the slipway is busy with boats, and it is a known shark spot.
hazards: Sharks: the Sealine thread refers to "a horrible incident there some time ago" ("I cant fight with a great white"), and Wikipedia describes the sheltered cove at the point as one of the largest known broadnose sevengill aggregation sites; do not wade out or swim after snagged tackle.

The Castle Rock no-take zone starts at the VB1 beacon on the point, roughly 500 m south of the slipway ramp; fishing south of it is an offence, and a 2012 poster placed the reserve edge near the clubhouse, so find the beacon before you cast.

Slippery granite boulders and thick kelp right in front of the rocks; snagging and losing fish in the kelp is the main problem ("they should be easy to hook but landing them there might be the problem!").

Busy boat slipway with ski-boats launching and retrieving and trailers reversing in the car park; keep lines out of the ramp and channel, and large stingrays hang around just outside the slipway where crews clean fish.
Baboons enter vehicles that contain food, and car-park security is unreliable (Wikivoyage).
access_notes: Turn east off Main Road (M4) about 4 km south of Simon's Town into the Miller's Point slipway service road (Cape Boat & Ski-Boat Club); a boom at the north end leads to the boat and trailer area, with the paved public car park to the right (can be muddy in winter) and the club's parking just south of it. City of Cape Town beach with parking, toilets and the slipway; a launch fee applies to boats (R70 in 2010) and "a parking fee is sometimes charged, in unpredictable amounts"; no gate fee is documented for the shore, and the day camp / caravan park hours and tariffs were not found (City bookings 078 173 1867; the Western Cape Government facility page returned 404). Expect the slip to be overwhelmed by ski-boats when snoek are running or a competition is on, and the M4 closes for the Cape Town Cycle Tour one Sunday in March. Walk is negligible: rocks and the small beach are beside the car park; the galjoen wash "a km or two North" is a separate walk along the shore.
unverified: Bait, hook sizes, best months and typical sizes per species are general False Bay practice; no source states them for this spot.
Tide preference: no source gives one; 'any' is a placeholder.
Facing bearing (60) is estimated from the cove's described orientation, not from a source.
Elf: only a generic regional line from FishingReminder mentions it; no Millers Point-specific elf catch found.
The Sealine 'Hottentot' thread quote ("I've caught many from the shore at Millers point") comes from a search snippet; the page itself was not opened.

Exact on-the-ground position of the VB1 beacon relative to the tidal pool and the small beach 'to the right of' the clubhouse; the gazette latitude puts it about 500 m south of the ramp, but a 2012 poster said the reserve reaches 'around the millers point clubhouse'. Confirm on site.
Whether SANParks requires a TMNP activity permit for shore angling here (SANParks fishing page returned 403); the reference text says only the Cape of Good Hope section needs one.
Day camp / caravan park opening hours and gate or parking tariffs (Western Cape Government facility page 404; City page gives no fees).
Galjoen closed-season dates not re-checked this pass.
Details of the shark 'incident' the thread refers to.

issues: Legality holds at the given coordinates. The slipway (-34.2305) lies between the Boulders restricted zone's southern limit at Rocklands (S34 12.705 = -34.2118) and the Castle Rock restricted zone's northern limit at Millers Point (S34 14.100 = -34.2350), as listed in the gazette coordinates on the Wikipedia TMNP MPA page. That puts it in the controlled zone, where angling is allowed with a DFFE permit. The City of Cape Town Miller's Point Beach page lists 'Fishing and angling' and says the beach is 'mainly used by anglers and divers'.

The record is too sure about where the boundary falls. It says the no-take zone starts 'roughly 500 m south of the slipway', but two independent Sealine posters put it much closer. In 2014 BTTB says VB1 is 'near the Cape Boat & Ski-Boat clubhouse' (sealine thread 82146, fetched 2 Nov 2026). In 2012 a poster says the reserve 'extends to around the millers point clubhouse' (sealine simonstown thread). Wikivoyage puts the club parking just south of the public car park. The usable stretch may therefore be only the rocks and beach beside and north of the slipway and clubhouse, not 500 m of shore. The 500 m figure is a reading of the gazette point, not a surveyed beacon position. The record's unverified list admits this, but the hazards and description state it as fact.

Wikipedia's Miller's Point article says 'since being established as a marine sanctuary, inshore fishing has been prohibited' without giving boundaries. Read alone, this conflicts with 'allowed'. The gazette coordinates and the City page outweigh it, but the page should not suggest that the whole headland is fishable.

The main angling source was not in the evidence file. Sealine thread 82146 does not appear in millers-point.evidence.md, which was capped at 90 KB. I fetched it again on 2 Nov 2026 and it is genuine (6 to 10 March 2014). It confirms these quotes: 'make a throw' (shore casting), 'Hottentot will be the order of the day, possibly Red Roman', 'water is a bit calm for Galjoen', 'nice galjoen wash about a km or two North of Millers', 'Make sure you fish to the North of the VB1 beacon', 'The Cape Point side of Millers is a Marine Reserve', 'monster roman ... near the kelp towards the loose rocks', the shark 'incident', and the 'black pylies' at the slipway. The quote 'I have caught a few Roman on that side' did not come up in my fetch and remains unconfirmed. The thread gives no bait, tackle or tide advice.

The Sealine 'Hottentot' thread (64171) quote ('I've caught many from the shore at Millers point...') is not in the evidence file and was not opened. It rests on a search snippet only and should not be counted as a second source.

Elf (shad) has no source specific to this spot. The only source is FishingReminder's generic Simon's Town line about 'rocky shore stretches toward Millers Point and Smitswinkel Bay (galjoen, elf/shad)'. The cached search summary itself warned that this line 'predates or ignores the protection status, so I would not rely on it'. The Sealine Millers thread does not mention elf. The months listed for elf (Nov to Mar) are invented.

species.size: Not stated for this spot; pan-sized fish are the norm on False Bay rocks (general, unverified here).
species.bait: Not stated for this spot; the usual False Bay rock approach is small hooks with redbait, white mussel, prawn or sardine strip fished into the kelp edge (general practice, flagged under unverified).
species.notes: The main shore target: Sealine thread (March 2014) - "Hottentot will be the order of the day, possibly Red Roman", "You will probably end up with hotties at Millers.", with the advice that "the fish were really localised. If you don't get bites within a few minutes then move on" and that "landing them there might be the problem" because of the kelp. A Sealine 'Hottentot' thread poster: "I've caught many from the shore at Millers point, Platboom, Scarborough, Soetwater..." (search snippet, page not opened). Other mentions that are not shore species here: large short-tail stingrays ("a few massive black pylies that hang around just outside the slipway"), snoek and geelbek taken by boats off the slipway (Ski-Boat), and roman, knifejaw, butterfish and yellowtail named by spearfishers around the point (deeperblue forum), which is inside or beside the no-take zone.

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: Not stated for this spot; galjoen are a redbait/white mussel fish on small hooks in white water (general, unverified here).
species.notes: FishingReminder's Simon's Town entry: "rocky shore stretches toward Millers Point and Smitswinkel Bay (galjoen, elf/shad)". The Sealine thread is lukewarm: "water is a bit calm for Galjoen, go fish on the Atlantic side in the Cape Point Reserve for them", though it adds "There is a nice galjoen wash about a km or two North of Millers" (toward Murdock Valley / Fisherman's Beach, outside both no-take zones). Observe the national galjoen closed season (mid-October to end February; dates not re-checked).

species.size: Not stated; the thread mentions "monster roman" seen near the kelp.
species.bait: Not stated; roman take bottom baits (redbait, mussel, squid strip) fished tight to the kelp and loose rocks (general, unverified here).
species.notes: Sealine thread: "possibly a Red Roman?", "I saw some monster roman come out near the kelp towards the loose rocks in the water", "I have caught a few Roman on that side". Strict national bag and size limits; the recovered roman population here is a reason the point was protected, so release them.

name: Rooikrans (Cape Point)
area: Cape of Good Hope section, Table Mountain National Park (False Bay side of Cape Point)
coord_source: The old pin was about 300 m out to sea. Snapped to the OpenStreetMap coastline nearest the Rooikrans car park (Overpass, 3 Nov 2026); the ledge itself is not mapped, so follow the path down from the car park.

access.note: Rooikrans car park at the end of the paved Rooikrans Road, off the main Cape Point road inside the Cape of Good Hope section (OSM parking way 688152146). From here there is a steep walk and scramble down to the ledges.

bottom: Rock ledge with kelp. The platform drops into a small patch of deep water.
permit: Inside the Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park: as well as the DFFE permit you need a SANParks line-fishing activity permit (Level 3, day or annual) and the park entry fee, and the gate hours limit when you can be there. A DFFE recreational angling permit, plus the SANParks Cape of Good Hope section entry fee (or a Wild Card) and a SANParks Level 3 activity permit for line fishing. SANParks says a valid DFFE recreational fishing permit is required when buying the Level 3 line-fishing permit for use at Cape of Good Hope (Cape Point). The Marine Species Access Permit is separate and does not cover line fishing. The SANParks pages themselves were not opened, so the wording comes from search snippets and current prices were not checked.
legality: Allowed with permits. Rooikrans is on the False Bay shore of Cape Point, south of Buffels Bay. That shore is in the Table Mountain National Park MPA controlled zone: the nearest restricted zones are Paulsberg (Smitswinkel Point to Venus Pool, north of Buffels Bay) and Cape of Good Hope (Hoek van die Bobbejaan to Olifantsbos, Atlantic side), and neither covers it. Checked against the 2004 zoning given in the brief and the Ski-Boat (anglerpublications ?p=4794) restricted-zone list. Bortjiesdrif (Black Rocks), which Ski-Boat pairs with Rooikrans as a spinning ledge, is next to Venus Pool at the southern edge of the Paulsberg restricted zone; check the beacon there before fishing it. The 2008 Sealine posts describe paying park entry and fishing openly, and Ski-Boat (2020) asks boat trollers to keep clear of the shore spinners at Rooikrantz.
description: A small, steep rock ledge on the False Bay side of Cape Point, inside the Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park, reached on foot from the Rooikrans car park. Anglers spin plugs, poppers and spoons from it for summer yellowtail. Ski-Boat calls it "one of the few places around Cape Town where yellowtail can be caught from the shore", and a Sealine poster called it "possibly THE best spot for spinning for yellowtail from shore". The platform is tiny and has been fished by the same regulars for decades. Kelp is a problem for lines, and the climb back up is hard.
hazards: Steep ledges and a hard scramble down and back up: "Those ledges are quite steap, so take your time getting down there"; "Many a fisherman lost their life due to haste in getting down there" (Sealine 2008)
Deep water off a small platform: "in can be quite dangerous" (Sealine 2008)
Snakes on the path (Sealine 2008)
Kelp in front of the ledge fouls lines (Sealine 2008)
Crowded and territorial: a very small platform that "works in turns", regulars of 30+ years, "be prepared to get asked to leave" (Sealine 2008)
Fishing alone: posters advise a long gaff, since there is no easy landing spot
access_notes: Enter through the Cape of Good Hope section gate of Table Mountain National Park ("you have to pay to get in and walk down the ledges"). Posters say a Wild Card works out cheaper than paying each visit. A 2008 post says the gate opens at 06:00; current gate hours and fees were not checked. Drive to the Rooikrans car park at the end of the paved Rooikrans Road, then walk and scramble down to the ledges. The left side is said to be more productive but harder for beginners. A 2008 post says the ledge gets crowded from about 05:00, so arrive early. Several posters suggest going first with someone who knows the paths (said of the Cape Point ledges in general). The ledge is small, so expect to share it and take turns.
unverified: Exact position of the ledge: the stand coordinates are estimated, about 0.8 km east of the OSM car park; only the car park is mapped
Current gate opening hours: 06:00 comes from a 2008 forum post
Current SANParks entry fee and Level 3 line-fishing permit price: SANParks pages were not opened, and the R360 figure in an ICSF article dates from about 2012
Typical yellowtail size at Rooikrans itself: the 2-5 kg figure is Ski-Boat's for False Bay in general
Blacktail, hottentot and kob at the ledge: only the Western Cape Government list names them; no angler report
Albacore from the shore: mentioned once in a 2007 thread as reported occasionally; not included as a species
Galjoen, roman and snoek: the merge notes list them, but the sources tie them to Olifantsbos, Diaz Beach, Buffels Bay or the reserve generally, not to Rooikrans, so they are left out
Fly fishing or soft-plastic/dropshot use at Rooikrans: no source
Facing bearing (~60 degrees, ENE across False Bay) and the semi-sheltered rating are worked out from the coastline's orientation, not stated by a source

issues: Coordinates: the stand point (-34.3425, 18.4795) is in the sea. The OSM coastline (Overpass natural=coastline, fetched 3 Nov 2026) is at about lon 18.4763 at lat -34.3425, so the point is about 295 m east of the shore at that latitude. The nearest coastline node is -34.34427, 18.47811, about 234 m away. This is under the 500 m threshold, but the pin is in False Bay, not on a ledge.

coord_source says the ledge is 'about 0.8 km east of and below the car park'. The same Overpass coastline shows the shore only about 0.33-0.38 km east of the OSM car park (-34.3412, 18.4709). The coast at lat -34.3412 to -34.3414 is at lon 18.4742-18.4750, so the 0.8 km offset overshoots into the sea.
Facing 60 degrees does not match the mapped coastline. The local shore from -34.3437,18.4769 to -34.3413,18.4742 runs about 317 degrees, so the seaward normal is about 45 degrees (NE), not 60.

Light-tackle fit is poor. The angling sources describe lure spinning (plugs, spoons), which is in the brief's style, but with heavy gear. Sealine 11644 (in evidence) says a 10 ft rod was 'too light', recommends an 11 ft Elbe yellowtail rod and a long gaff, and says 'Ensure you have a rod & reel that can take the pace'. The cached Cape Point reserve thread (Ajay, 26 Jan 2008) says yellowtail 'are hard to land on light tackle'. The record does admit this. The site should label it as heavy spinning, not light tackle.

Quote not found in the cached evidence: Ski-Boat (?p=4033) 'one of the few places around Cape Town where yellowtail can be caught from the shore'. The cached search summaries for ?p=4033 describe it as boat-focused, and one says no source specifically links Rooikrans to shore yellowtail spinning. This quote anchors the reason and the description but was not verified here. The claim that Ski-Boat asks trollers to keep clear of the Rooikrantz shore spinners is also unverified.

Possible misquote: 'possibly THE best spot for spinning for yellowtail from shore' (attributed to Sealine 7316) is not in the cache. The cached Sealine text says 'This is possibly one of THE FINEST spots in the country!!' about Rooikrantz. Check the exact wording before publishing it as a quote.

species.size: False Bay yellowtail usually 2-5 kg, fish up to 12 kg not uncommon, a few to 20 kg over the years (Ski-Boat, for False Bay in general, not Rooikrans specifically)
species.bait: White chisel-nose plug or a keel spoon (Sealine 2008). Plastic surface poppers or long, thin plugs in white or green, cast over the school and pulled straight through the frenzy (Ski-Boat 2020).
species.notes: Sealine 2008: "Rooikrantz ledges is possibly THE best spot for spinning for yellowtail from shore"; "it is almost exclusively yellowtail guys who fish there". Best in summer, "probably january and february". Fish are unpredictable ("They're there 1 day, and gone the next"). Posters say they respond more to wind and water temperature than to tide: 15 C and up (Ski-Boat), and "Less than 14 dont bother with spinning" (Sealine 2007). Wind advice conflicts: Sealine says a south-easter that has blown at least 3 days, Ski-Boat favours a westerly around the Point. Posters fished 10-11 ft rods with 18-25 kg line, say the fish are hard to land on light tackle, and carry a long gaff.

species.bait: No Rooikrans-specific bait given. The 2007 Cape Point reserve thread lists mussel, prawn, chokka, red bait, bloodworm and wonderworm for the reserve in general.
species.notes: Named only by the Western Cape Government fishing page ("Rooikrans: blacktail, hottentot and kob (kabeljou)"). No angler report of blacktail at the ledge itself.

species.bait: No Rooikrans-specific bait given. Reserve-wide baits are mussel, prawn, chokka, red bait and worms.
species.notes: Named by the Western Cape Government page for Rooikrans. The Sealine reserve thread puts 1 kg+ hottentot in the kelp beds at nearby Buffels Bay, not at Rooikrans.

species.bait: Not stated for Rooikrans
species.notes: Named only by the Western Cape Government page for Rooikrans. No angler report from the ledge.

species.bait: Taken incidentally on yellowtail spinning gear; no specific lure given
species.notes: Only one source, a 2007 Sealine thread, which lists it as reported occasionally at Rooikrantz.

name: Buffels Bay (Cape Point)
area: Cape of Good Hope section, Table Mountain National Park (False Bay side of Cape Point)
coord_source: Stand: Bordjiesrif Tidal Pool from OpenStreetMap via Nominatim (-34.3133195, 18.4619902), with the ledges either side of it. Car park: Bordjiesrif Parking Lot from OSM (-34.3138874, 18.4626886). Buffels Bay Parking and Slipway are from a Nominatim query run on 30 Oct 2026. The restricted-zone check uses the Venus Pool boundary point S34 17.744 E018 28.020 (about -34.2957, 18.4670) from the 2004 regulations as quoted on Wikipedia.

access.note: Bordjiesrif Parking Lot (OSM), next to the tidal pool and ledges. For the Buffels Bay end, about 800 m south, use Buffels Bay Parking (OSM -34.3204, 18.4602) by the slipway (-34.3208, 18.4610).

bottom: Rock ledges with kelp beds, gullies and holes in the kelp, either side of the two tidal pools. The Buffels Bay end has a slipway and a small beach.
permit: Inside the Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park: as well as the DFFE permit you need a SANParks line-fishing activity permit (Level 3, day or annual) and the park entry fee, and the gate hours limit when you can be there. DFFE marine recreational angling permit. You also need the SANParks conservation fee or a Wild Card at the Cape of Good Hope gate, plus a SANParks Level 3 activity permit for line fishing (annual or day). SANParks says 'a valid DFFE Recreational Fishing Permit is required when purchasing a Level 3 line fishing permit for use in Cape of Good Hope'. The Marine Species Access Permit is for rock lobster and does not cover line fishing. Collecting bait such as wonderworm needs its own DFFE permit. Normal bag and size limits apply. Prices in the sources (R360 Level 3, from ICSF around 2012) are out of date.
legality: Allowed with permits. Bordjiesrif (about S34 18.80) and Buffels Bay (about S34 19.25) are on the False Bay side, about 2 km south of Venus Pool (S34 17.744 E018 28.020). Venus Pool is the southern end of the Paulsberg restricted (no-take) zone, which runs north to Smitswinkel Point, per the 2004 regulations quoted on Wikipedia. The Cape of Good Hope restricted zone is on the Atlantic side (Hoek van die Bobbejaan to Schusters Bay), so it does not cover this stretch. Both stands are therefore in the TMNP MPA controlled zone, where shore angling is allowed with a DFFE recreational permit. Sealine posters (2007, 2008) also put the boundary at Venus Pool, marked by an information board on site: 'you would definitely be in protected area' past it. Do not fish north of Venus Pool.
description: Rocky ledges and kelp beds either side of the Bordjiesrif and Buffels Bay tidal pools, on the False Bay side of the Cape of Good Hope reserve. A Sealine thread lists 'Buffelsbay: Wonderworm at the tidal pool, and 1kg+ hottentots in the kelp beds' and suggests 'dropshotting in gullies'. Ski-Boat names the 'Bortjiesdrif ledges', with Rooikrantz, as 'one of the few places around Cape Town where yellowtail can be caught from the shore', where 'guys spinning off the rocks' fish in summer.
hazards: Kelp beds snag lines and lures (Sealine)
Swell washing over low ledges, and slippery rock
Cape fur seals take hooked fish (Ski-Boat)
Both tidal pools are swimming areas, so cast away from bathers
Boats launching at the Buffels Bay slipway; trollers work the kelp line past Rooikrantz into Buffels Bay
Large sharks: a Zambezi shark was reported at Buffels Baai, Cape Point (Sealine)
Paulsberg no-take zone starts at Venus Pool, just north of the Black Rocks area
access_notes: Inside the Cape of Good Hope section of Table Mountain National Park. Pay the conservation fee or show a Wild Card at the gate; you get a map there. Gates open and close at set times, so dawn and dusk sessions are limited and night fishing is not possible (Sealine). There are car parks at Bordjiesrif and at Buffels Bay, a few metres from the tidal pools and ledges, with picnic and braai sites and a public slipway at Buffels Bay. Sealine posters say the entry fee keeps it lightly fished. Drive time: no source gives one. OSRM free-flow (29 Oct 2026) gives about 49 min from Westlake and 73 min from Green Point, plus any queue at the gate. That is within the 60-minute brief from Westlake only.
unverified: Tide preference: no source gives one for this spot. A Sealine yellowtail thread says the fish respond to wind and water temperature more than to tide, so tide_pref is set to 'any'.

Facing (about 100 degrees) and the semi shelter rating come from the coastline shape between Buffels Bay and Venus Pool, not from a source. One Sealine poster notes that in winter one side of the reserve is often flat when the other is not.
Typical hottentot size and season. Only '1kg+' is sourced.
Chokka from the shore: Ski-Boat Part 3 and Jacita (Jun 2025) report chokka at Buffels Bay, but from anchored boats or with no method given, so it is left out of the species list.
