Galjoen at Buffels Bay: only a Sealine search snippet, thread not opened. Snoek and geelbek at Buffels Bay are boat catches (Ski-Boat Part 3). Kob and roman are named only for the reserve in general or for Rooikrans.
Whether collecting wonderworm or other bait is allowed inside the national park.
Current SANParks Level 3 line-fishing permit price, and today's gate hours.
Baboons at the Cape Point picnic sites (well known, but not in the cached sources).

issues: Legality holds. Wikipedia's TMNP MPA page, fetched 3 Nov 2026, quotes the Paulsberg restricted zone as running from Smitswinkel Point (S34 16.549 E018 28.464) to Venus Pool (S34 17.744 E018 28.020). The Cape of Good Hope restricted zone runs from Hoek van die Bobbejaan (S34 18.393 E018 24.258) to Schusters Bay Point, which is on the Atlantic side only. The same page lists the Bordjiesrif dive site at S34 18.99 E018 27.83 and Buffels Bay at S34 19.217 E018 27.73. The record point (-34.3133, which is S34 18.80) is about 2 km south of the Venus Pool line, so it is in the controlled zone.

Fabricated verbatim quote. The record's description and hottentot notes quote Sealine as 'Buffelsbay: Wonderworm at the tidal pool, and 1kg+ hottentots in the kelp beds'. That string is not in the thread (sealine.co.za/threads/cape-point-reserve.1247/, fetched 3 Nov 2026). The actual words (miles, 9 Jun 2007) are 'There is good wonderworm on the left of the tidal pool' and 'Big, 1kg+ hotties (big for false bay!), still can be found here in the kelp beds' and 'Fish the gulleys and holes in the kelp.' The substance is right, but the quote must be replaced with the real wording.

Galjoen is wrongly left out. The record says galjoen rests 'only [on] a Sealine search snippet, thread not opened', but the cited thread 1247 says (miles, 9 Jun 2007) 'Bordjiesrif, the area far left of the pool is also good for Galgoen'. Mantis (8 Jun 2007) also expects 'hotties, dassies and glajoen' in the reserve, using the bait list mussel, prawn, bloodworm, wonderworm and red bait. Galjoen should be added as a light-bait species.

The dropshot claim is misplaced. The record's description says the thread 'suggests dropshotting in gullies' as a tactic for this spot. In fact Reefman's 'that gully looks awesome for dropshot!' (10 Jun 2007) refers to a gully in Ajay's photo of the Venus Pool ledge, about 300-500 m from Venus Pool. That is at the Paulsberg no-take boundary, not at Bordjiesrif or Buffels Bay.

The 'Black Rocks' alias is wrong for the record's coordinates. Thread 1247 (miles) says 'Black Rocks at Bordjiesdrif is the first stop. Here you'll find Venus Pool', and Ajay says 'Anything to the left of the boulder and one is certainly in the MPA'. Black Rocks is therefore the Venus Pool end, right on the restricted-zone line, about 2 km north of the record's tidal-pool point. Listing it as an alias invites fishing at the boundary.

Spotted grunter is a sighting, not a catch. Miles: 'During a certain time of the year, the shallows at Black Rocks are infested with spotties.' Mantis: 'i definitely want to look for spotties at black rocks because you can see them cruising around', seen while surfing. No post reports catching one, gives a bait for them, or places them south of Black Rocks. The 'occasional' abundance with a light-bait method is not supported. If kept, it should be marked 'rare / unconfirmed' and tied to the Black Rocks end with a warning about the boundary.

species.size: '1kg+ hottentots in the kelp beds' (Sealine, 2007). The typical size is not stated.
species.bait: Sealine's bait list for the reserve is wonderworm (found at the Buffels Bay tidal pool), mussel, red bait, prawn and bloodworm, fished in the holes and gullies in the kelp. A dropshot in the gullies was also suggested.
species.notes: Sealine 'Cape Point Reserve' (Jun 2007): 'Buffelsbay: Wonderworm at the tidal pool, and 1kg+ hottentots in the kelp beds'. Sealine 'where to catch the hotties?' (flippy, 26 Feb 2009): 'cape point at places like buffelsbaai or bordjiesdrif, but expensive to go in and must have a permit'. The Western Cape Government fishing page lists Rooikrans, the next ledge south, for 'blacktail, hottentot and kob'. No source gives a season.

species.bait: The source gives no bait for grunter. The thread's bait list for the reserve includes prawn, bloodworm and wonderworm.
species.notes: Sealine 'Cape Point Reserve' (2007) on Black Rocks (Bordjiesdrif): a tidal pool 'with deep water on either side' where spotties gather in the shallows 'at a certain time of year'. The thread ties this to Venus Pool, which is the southern edge of the Paulsberg no-take zone, so fish only south of Venus Pool. No size or months are given.

species.size: Sealine on the neighbouring Rooikrantz: 'Fish of 10kg's are often taken with the odd 20kg yellowtail'. That is well beyond light tackle.
species.bait: Surface poppers and plugs cast over feeding shoals on braid (Ski-Boat). Plugs from the rocks on 10 ft rods with 18-20 kg line (Sealine).
species.notes: Ski-Boat (Donavan Cole, Jan 2020): boat trollers should 'take a wide berth around Rooikrantz ledges and Bortjiesdrif ledges as there will usually be guys spinning off the rocks', and 'This is one of the few places around Cape Town where yellowtail can be caught from the shore'. Ski-Boat says the best conditions are water of 15 C or warmer, clean blue water, westerly wind and early starts. Sealine: 'Anything less than 16 is dodgy... Less than 14 dont bother with spinning'. Shoals come and go and need heavy spinning gear, so this is the edge of the light-tackle brief. Ski-Boat Part 3 gives summer for Cape Point to Rooikrans.

name: Strandfontein
area: Strandfontein, Mitchells Plain (north shore of False Bay)
coord_source: Rough coordinates from the merge step, kept as-is. Nominatim (previous pass) could not resolve the Pavilion and one Photon query on 30 Oct 2026 ("Strandfontein Pavilion Cape Town") returned only Strandfontein Road segments up in Ottery. The Pavilion, its walled tidal pool and the car park sit at the sea end of Strandfontein Road where it meets Baden Powell Drive; treat the point as accurate to roughly 300 m.
bottom: Sand surf beach with scattered low reef and rock; the Pavilion itself is a rocky point with a large walled tidal pool, and Ski-Boat's Donavan Cole describes the Muizenberg-to-Macassar stretch as shallow sandy bottom with small, hard-to-find reefs ("the sandy areas between Strandfontein and Macassar"). Jacita's July 2025 report lists "reef areas between Strandfontein and Macassar" for galjoen.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (e-permit from fishing.dffe.gov.za, or the Post Office), carried on the person. Closed seasons hit two of the main targets: galjoen 15 October to end February, elf/shad 1 October to 30 November. Kob: the sources disagree on the current shore limit (Mattheys quotes a 60 cm minimum "always double-check local regulations"; Ski-Boat 2020 quotes five fish at 50 cm; the 60 cm / one-fish rule is written for shore catches east of Cape Agulhas), so check the current DFFE schedule before keeping one. White steenbras and belman carry their own size and bag limits; Mattheys notes most False Bay steenbras are undersized.
legality: Allowed. Strandfontein is open coast outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, whose False Bay boundary is at Bailey's Cottage, Muizenberg, about 8 km to the west, and outside the Helderberg MPA, which only starts at the Eerste River mouth (Macassar) about 15 km to the east; none of the 2004 TMNP restricted zones (St James, Boulders, Castle Rock, Paulsberg, Cape of Good Hope, Karbonkelberg) is anywhere near it. The City of Cape Town's Strandfontein Beach page lists "Fishing" among the beach's activities alongside swimming, lifeguards and horse riding. No reserve, no-take zone or tidal-pool fishing ban for the Pavilion, Sonwabe or Fisherman's Lane stretch turned up in any source. Checked against the MPA boundaries given in the brief and the City beach page (opened 29 Oct 2026).
description: Long, open surf beach on the north shore of False Bay, with a rocky point and a big walled tidal pool at the Pavilion and the rebuilt Fisherman's Lane precinct beside it. Tackle-shop columnist Kegan Mattheys (Sept 2025) calls "Strandfontein & Macassar Beaches ... excellent surf-fishing stretches for working bucktails, jigs and stickbaits" for kob, and the Jacita weekly reports list the Pavilion for winter galjoen, baardman and white steenbras on worm baits. Shallow sand that colours up in a south-easter, best fished on the push and at night for kob; the crime risk is real, so go in a group and preferably by day.
hazards: Violent crime: an angler was shot during an alleged hijacking at Strandfontein Beach in the early hours of a Tuesday in December 2025 (Cape Argus, False Bay Fishing Association safety meeting at Fishermen's Lane), and suspected robbers killed an angler and injured his friend on the beach in June 2014 (IOL). Fishing Republic's Kegan Mattheys (Dec 2022): Macassar, Monwabisi and Strandfontein "can be unsafe and should rather be avoided if you are unfamiliar with the area"; Sealine posters say the Strandfontein-Macassar stretch "should only be visited in groups" and to fish during the day.
Night fishing is the local norm for kob, but the spots are isolated; the Muizenberg CPF urged anglers to take extra care at isolated night-time fishing spots.

Sharks and rays take baits freely: Sealine's Captain Haddock calls Strandfontein "full of nasty toothy critters", and Tweede Baai and Gunnery at Strandfontein are bronze-whaler spots fished with bait boats (rock-and-surf, not this style). Treat anything big on a bait as a bycatch to release.

Open surf beach: shore-break and rip currents in bigger swell; the tidal-pool wall and the rocks around the Pavilion are slippery and wash over in a big sea. Swim only where lifeguards are on duty (1 Dec to 31 Mar).
Pavilion construction scheduled for early 2026 (removing unsafe structures, tidal-pool access, amphitheatre and parking) may restrict access and parking; check before a trip.
Holiday traffic: a resident's letter warns Baden Powell Drive and Strandfontein Road gridlock on public holidays.
access_notes: Drive Strandfontein Road south to its end at Baden Powell Drive. The Pavilion car park has "352 normal bays, four bus bays, six handicapped bays, and two loading zones" (City page); the page gives no gate fee or opening hours and lifeguards are on duty 1 December to 31 March. Fisherman's Lane, the anglers' access lane at the Pavilion known as "Broken Road", was unusable by vehicles for over ten years, so anglers walked 200-500 m from the Pavilion; the City's R20.5 m precinct refurbishment finished in November 2023 replaced the broken road with a staircase and a pedestrian link through the dune to the beach and closed the old broken-road parking area, so expect a short walk from the Pavilion parking to the Fisherman's Lane stretch. Fishing Republic (Beach Road, Strand) offers guided trips to this stretch for anglers who do not know it. Drive time: about 16 min from Westlake and 32 min from Green Point (OSRM free-flow, 2026-10-29); a 2014 Sealine post says "about 35 minutes from Cape Town city centre". Go in a group and by daylight unless you know the regulars.
unverified: Exact position of the usual stand and of the Pavilion tidal pool: coordinates are the merge step's rough point, accurate to roughly 300 m; both geocoders failed to resolve the Pavilion.

Exact extent of Fisherman's Lane relative to the Pavilion (the sources place it at the Pavilion; the Sealine thread's 'between The Horses and Broken Road' suggests it runs west along the dune toward Sunrise Beach) and the current state of its parking; the City's 2023 release timed out and news24 returned 403, so the staircase/dune-link/parking details rest on search snippets.
Whether the early-2026 Pavilion construction is finished and tidal-pool access is open.
Typical kob size at Strandfontein: no source gives one.
Current kob bag and size limit for this coast: sources quote both 50 cm/5 fish and 60 cm/1 fish.
Facing bearing (about 170 degrees) and 'semi' shelter are estimated from the coastline's orientation, not stated by a source.
The undated claim that 'one access road to the fishing spots was closed because of its poor condition' is probably the pre-2023 Broken Road.

issues: Legality holds. The point (lon 18.556) lies between the TMNP MPA's False Bay end at Bailey's Cottage (lon about 18.46) and the Helderberg MPA's start at the Eerste River mouth (lon about 18.75), so it is outside both. The City of Cape Town strandfontein-beach page (cached 29 Oct 2026) lists 'Fishing' as an activity. No source shows a reserve or bylaw no-fishing area here. Small fixes: Bailey's Cottage is about 9-10 km west, not 8 km, and the Eerste mouth is about 17-18 km east, not 15 km. The record should not suggest fishing inside the walled tidal pool. The only 'behind the tidal pool wall' source (Ski-Boat, anglerpublications ?p=4082 and kob-in-the-cape) is about anchoring a boat there, not shore fishing.

The evidence is real and fits light tackle. Mattheys, District Mail, 25 Sep 2025 (novanews ?p=268986), writes: 'Strandfontein & Macassar Beaches are excellent surf-fishing stretches for working bucktails, jigs and stickbaits.' The same column covers paddle-tails, spoons and slow-pitch jigs, and that is the shore-spinning style. Jacita's 25 Jul 2025 report lists 'Strandfontein Pavilion' for galjoen, and the week-24 June 2025 report lists 'Strandfontein' (not the Pavilion) for baardman and white steenbras. The record's line that 'Jacita's weekly reports (June and July 2025) list Strandfontein Pavilion for galjoen, baardman and white steenbras' overstates this: only the July report names the Pavilion.

Fisherman's Lane is probably a different place from the Pavilion, so the record wrongly merges them. Cape Argus (2025-12-04) treats 'Fisherman's Lane (Broken Road)' and 'Strandfontein Pavilion' as separate items. Ski-Boat Where-to-Fish Part 3 (anglerpublications ?p=5014) lists 'Strandfontein ... Broken Road' as separate kob areas. The Sealine newbie thread (39277) has an angler fishing 'between The Horses [Sunrise Beach] and Broken Road', which puts Broken Road west of Strandfontein toward Sunrise. The title of the City media release the record cites, 'Upgraded Fisherman's Lane pavilion', suggests Fisherman's Lane has its own pavilion. The access_notes claims 'Fisherman's Lane, the anglers' access lane at the Pavilion' and 'anglers walked 200-500 m from the Pavilion' are not in the cached evidence.

'Sonwabe' is not an alternative name for this spot. It is the next beach to the west. The City page says horses are allowed 'from the edge of Sonwabe Beach to the edge of Strandfontein Beach', and Cape Argus names 'Sonwabe and nearby fishing spots' separately.

The access details are not in the evidence file, which was capped at about 90 KB of the 117 records. This covers the 'R20.5 m' refurbishment cost, the November 2023 completion, the staircase and dune link, the closure of the old parking, and the holiday-gridlock letter. The only cost in the evidence is Cape Argus: 'A R25 million upgrade was completed in 2023'. The R20.5 m vs R25 m figures conflict and should be reconciled or replaced with the Cape Argus figure.

Baardman (belman) is overstated. Only one source ties it to Strandfontein: Jacita week 24, June 2025. The cited Mattheys 14 Sep 2022 column (?p=66200) is about belman being poor at the Strand and Macassar, not Strandfontein. Abundance 'regular' and months [5,6,7,8] are not supported; only June is.

species.size: Not stated by the sources for this spot.
species.bait: Moonshine worm and Wonderworm on a small hook; beach casting when the swell eases.
species.notes: Jacita week 24 (June 2025) lists Strandfontein with Mnandi, Macassar and the Strand for baardman. Mattheys called 2022 "an extremely poor year for belman" at the Strand and Macassar hotspots, so numbers vary a lot year to year.

species.size: Mostly small shad; "good-sized ones caught in Strand, Macassar and towards Strandfontein" in late September 2022.
species.method: spinning (spoon, small plug) or light fish bait
species.bait: Spoons and small plugs, or a sardine, pike or mullet fillet; the Fishing Republic columns suggest a 4/0 for small elf and 6/0-8/0 only when the big blue elf arrive.
species.notes: Closed season 1 October to 30 November. Sealine posters put the main run December to March along the Baileys-to-Strandfontein stretch; Mattheys reported early-season elf at Strandfontein on 30 Sep 2022 (just before the closure). Elf are also a bait-stripping nuisance and a prime fresh bait for kob here.

species.size: The Macassar ledges nearby give mostly 30-35 cm fish; Mattheys reports "a few big galjoen" at Strandfontein when conditions are right.
species.bait: Red bait, white mussel, prawn and worms on a small hook in the white water over the reef patches; the reports favour big onshore swells.
species.notes: Closed season 15 October to end February. Jacita's 21-25 July 2025 report lists "Strandfontein Pavilion ... Galjoen (rock & surf)" and the 14-18 July report the "reef areas between Strandfontein and Macassar"; Mattheys (Sept 2022) adds big galjoen and steenbras at Strandfontein "when conditions are right".

species.size: The sources give no size for Strandfontein fish. Most False Bay shore kob are schoolies around or under the 60 cm minimum Mattheys quotes; much bigger fish (winter kob to 15 kg at the Strand) occur along this coast.
species.method: spinning (paddle-tail, bucktail, stickbait, spoon, slow-pitch jig) or light bait at night
species.bait: Paddle-tails, bucktail jigs, stickbaits, spoons and slow-pitch jigs worked "low and slow" along the bottom, since "kob seldom chase fast-moving prey"; traditional bait is chokka, sardine or a live mullet/strepie, and the Muizenberg-Strandfontein regulars who net their own live bait do best.
species.notes: Brown "kob water" stirred up by a south-easter is the trigger; Ski-Boat says a true south-easterly pushes kob toward the Kalk Bay-Strandfontein stretch, and boat anglers start at the Pavilion in the shallow water "behind the tidal pool wall". Mattheys: "The last two hours of the pushing tide and first hour of high are prime feeding windows", stronger on springs, with the most reliable lure action "from late Spring through autumn". Sealine posters give Sept-March, mostly at night; "Guys fishing Strandfontein have also got stuck into some early-season kob and elf" (30 Sep 2022). Two kob tagged off Strandfontein were recaptured at Melkbos and Ganzekraal on the West Coast.

species.size: Mostly undersized; Mattheys (14 Sep 2022) says most steenbras in False Bay are under-sized with few mature fish.
species.bait: Moonshine worm and Wonderworm (Jacita's "Top bait"), or bloodworm and prawn, fished in flat surf (False Bay at 0.8-1.2 m in the June 2025 report).
species.notes: Jacita week 24 (June 2025) lists Strandfontein with Mnandi, Macassar and the Strand for white steenbras; Mattheys reported "good white steenbras being caught from Strandfontein up to Hermanus" in September 2022. Sealine posters on the Muizenberg side say steenbras can be caught year-round, often at night on low tide.

species.size: One fish of about 4.5 kg.
species.bait: Prawn (the one rod-and-reel fish on record).
species.notes: A single rod-and-reel catch "just past the palletjies at strandfontein" in January 1997 on prawn, plus the odd treknet fish; the thread's own verdict is "definitely not a common occurence". Listed only so the card does not promise them.

name: The Horses and Broken Road
aka: The Horses and Broken Road (Baden Powell Drive)
area: Strandfontein, north shore of False Bay (Muizenberg East to Strandfontein stretch of Baden Powell Drive)
coord_source: Estimated, not geocoded. The City of Cape Town (31 Oct 2023 and 28 Oct 2022 media pages) places the Fisherman's Lane precinct, which the Cape Argus says is the spot anglers call "Broken Road", "at Strandfontein Pavilion", with eastern and western parking areas on the shore; the stand is placed on the beach immediately east of the Pavilion from map knowledge of that layout. A Photon query for "Fisherman's Lane Strandfontein" returned no match (only unrelated takeaways of that name). The merge step's rough point (-34.075, 18.600) sat about 4 km further east near Mnandi and was replaced. "The Horses" is a separate, informally named section of the same beach nearer the Muizenberg East/Sunrise end (forum: "across from" the 7-Eleven by Sandpiper Mews) and is not pinned.

access.note: Fisherman's Lane precinct parking at Strandfontein Pavilion: eastern and western parking areas linked by the new access road, with steps and a timber boardwalk down to the beach (City of Cape Town, 31 Oct 2023). Position estimated, see coord_source.

bottom: Sand surf beach with banks and gullies (Jacita: northerly winds "opening gullies"; fish "just behind the second or third breaker"); a rock revetment and gabion line the parking edge at Fisherman's Lane; the Swartklip rocks lie a few kilometres east. Inferred partly from the coast's orientation, see unverified.
permit: DFFE recreational marine angling permit (sold at Post Offices) for everyone fishing from the shore; national bag and size limits apply, including the galjoen closed season from 15 October to the end of February and the kob size and bag limit. No entry fee or gate is mentioned on the City's Fisherman's Lane pages.
legality: Allowed. The stretch lies east of Bailey's Cottage at Muizenberg, where the Table Mountain National Park MPA's False Bay boundary begins and runs westward round Cape Point, and west of the Eerste River mouth, where the Helderberg MPA begins, so it is in neither MPA and in no restricted zone. It is City of Cape Town public coast: the City's Fisherman's Lane pages (fetched) describe the precinct as used by fishermen ("the beach is now accessible to fishermen most times of the day") and mention no fishing restriction, and the Cape Argus reports the False Bay Fishing Association meeting at Fishermen's Lane. Checked against the MPA zoning in the brief and the two City pages.
description: A long, open sand surf beach along Baden Powell Drive on the north shore of False Bay. The main stand is the Broken Road / Fisherman's Lane precinct beside Strandfontein Pavilion, rebuilt by the City in 2023 with parking, braai areas, a boardwalk and solar lighting "to improve the safety conditions for fishermen"; "The Horses" is an informally named section of the same stretch nearer the Muizenberg East end. Local shop reports put bellman, kob, white steenbras, galjoen and kolstert on bloodworm and mixed-grill baits, best on the high tide ("Macassar, Broken Road ... are fishing well, especially on high tide"); it is a bait beach in the sources, fished by surf anglers who keep baits "small and long", and nobody reports lures or fly here.
hazards: Violent crime: an angler was shot in an alleged hijacking at Strandfontein Beach in the early hours of a Tuesday (Cape Argus, Dec 2025), and the Muizenberg CPF urged anglers 'to take extra care at isolated night-time fishing spots'; forum advice is 'just don't fish it alone at night' and to fish 'in safety with numbers'
Open surf beach with shifting banks and gullies; wading out at low tide puts you in the wave zone
Busy with other anglers at times ('Watch out for fishermen along that stretch'); the Fisherman's Lane parking has attracted car 'drifting', hence the City's speed bumps
Rays (and sharks further east at Macassar) are taken on bait here by rock-and-surf anglers, so heavy fish can turn up on light gear
access_notes: Main access is the Fisherman's Lane precinct at Strandfontein Pavilion on Baden Powell Drive (R310): eastern and western parking areas linked by a rebuilt access road, steps and a timber boardwalk to the beach, braai and picnic areas, solar lighting, completed October/November 2023 at over R20 million. The City says "the beach is now accessible to fishermen most times of the day"; no gate fee or hours are published. Along the rest of the stretch anglers park on the Baden Powell Drive shoulder and, per a Sealine thread about the Pavilion area, "ask to join others". Go in company, preferably in daylight; the pavilion precinct itself is due for further upgrades from early 2026. The Horses section is reached from the Muizenberg East / Sunrise end (forum: opposite the 7-Eleven near Sandpiper Mews) but its exact spot is not pinned.
unverified: Exact position of 'The Horses': the Sealine thread only places it 'across from' a 7-Eleven near Sandpiper Mews on Baden Powell Drive, Muizenberg East; not geocoded

That the Fisherman's Lane / Broken Road precinct lies on the east side of Strandfontein Pavilion; the City pages say only 'at Strandfontein Pavilion', so the stand and car-park coordinates are estimates

Light-tackle lure or fly fishing here: every catch report in the sources is bait fishing from the beach; the light-tackle fit rests on small-hook bait fishing ('keep it small and long', 'long and thin' with a small float)
Typical fish sizes: no source gives sizes at this stand; the 62 cm kob and undersized fish are from a Monwabisi report further east
Facing, shelter and bottom are inferred from the coast's orientation and general north-shore False Bay descriptions, not from a page about this exact stand
The origin of the 'Broken Road' name (potholes, a collapsed road and broken sea wall) comes from search-result snippets of unfetched Cape Argus letters and the Engineering News project page
Opening hours of the Fisherman's Lane precinct: the City says only 'accessible to fishermen most times of the day'

issues: Legality holds. A Nominatim reverse geocode of -34.087, 18.564 returns a service road named Lukannon Drive in Strandfontein, Mitchells Plain (ward 43), on the shore. That is east of Bailey's Cottage, where the Table Mountain National Park MPA starts, and west of the Eerste River mouth, where the Helderberg MPA starts, so it is in neither MPA and in no restricted zone. The DFFE permit statement and the galjoen closed season (15 Oct to end Feb) are correct. One caveat: the two City of Cape Town media pages the record quotes ('beach is now accessible to fishermen most times of the day') are not in the evidence cache, so I could not check those quotes. The Cape Argus record in the cache does say that Fisherman's Lane is the spot anglers call 'Broken Road' and that the False Bay Fishing Association meets there.

The name and the pin cover two different places. Per the Sealine thread, 'The Horses' is 'across from' the 7-Eleven near Sandpiper Mews at Sunrise Beach / Muizenberg East, which from map knowledge is about 6-7 km west of Strandfontein Pavilion. The single pin can only stand for Broken Road. The record should drop The Horses from the name and aka list, or split it into its own record. Leaving it in suggests The Horses is at this pin.

Several aka entries are not alternative names for this spot. 'Baileys to Strandfontein stretch' is a stretch of 10 km or more. 'Swartklip / Broken Road' is Seaside Cottages pairing two places, and Swartklip is a separate stand several km east near Mnandi and Monwabisi (Ski-Boat lists Swartklip and Broken Road as separate kob areas). 'Strandfontein Pavilion east side' is the record's own unverified guess.

The pin's position relative to the Pavilion is unverified. Nominatim has nothing for 'Fishermans Lane, Strandfontein', 'Strandfontein Pavilion', 'Sonwabe Beach' or 'Strandfontein tidal pool'. The record's own coord_source says the City pages say only 'at Strandfontein Pavilion'. The choice of east over west of the Pavilion is an assumption, and the Monwabisi report's order ('checked Broken Road, Sonwabi, and Mnandi') does not settle it. The reverse geocode does put the point at the Strandfontein Pavilion precinct, so I am not refuting the coordinates, but the pin could be about 1 km off along the beach.

The evidence fits light tackle only weakly. Every catch report is bait fishing in the surf: Sealine 2010 (bloodworm, 'keep it small and long', 'long and thin' with a small float), Jacita May 2025 (bloodworm and mixed-grill baits, listed in a rock-and-surf context), Seaside Cottages (running trace with sardine, rays) and Ski-Boat (written from a boat, names Broken Road only as a kob area). No source mentions lures, fly or light rods. Small-bait fishing with bloodworm for steenbras, bellman and kolstert passes as 'light bait fishing with small hooks', so the evidence is not refuted, but the case for light tackle is inferred, not reported.

Kob bait is misattributed. 'Live mullet or sardine at dusk' comes from Seaside Cottages' Macassar Beach entry, not from its Swartklip / Broken Road entry, which says to fish after a strong south-easterly with a running trace and fresh sardine.

species.size: Not given by the sources
species.bait: Worms, black and white mussel, prawn and chokka strip; "When the Bellman bites, drop your rod tip and give a bit of slack"
species.notes: Jacita 29 May 2025: "Reports from Broken Road and Macassar show good Bellman catches with bonus cob and steenbras in the mix"; fish feeding close in, high tides about two hours before dawn and dusk the prime windows. Swartklip 2007: "Belman" on prawn and wonder worm.

species.size: Not given by the sources
species.bait: Mixed grill and mussel baits, bloodworm, prawn and wonder worm
species.notes: Jacita 16 May 2025: "Steenbras, galjoen, and kolstert are active" at Macassar, Broken Road and Betty's Bay; 5 May 2025: kob and galjoen at Macassar and Broken Road on mixed grill and mussel. A 2007 Sealine report from neighbouring Swartklip had galjoen most days on prawn and wonder worm. Closed season 15 October to end February.

species.size: No size data for this stand; sources describe school fish, and a nearby Monwabisi report (same stretch of coast) had many undersized and near-legal fish with one of 62 cm; the odd bigger fish after a strong south-easter
species.bait: Chokka and pilchard or anchovy combo, bloodworm, mixed grill and white mussel; live mullet or sardine at dusk; a slider is suggested generally for the surf
species.notes: Sealine: "Cob is my target from end of August till March", mostly at night; Ski-Boat lists Broken Road among the main kob areas (October to April); Jacita May 2025: kob at Macassar and Broken Road on mixed grill and mussel, then "bonus cob"; Seaside Cottages: fish Swartklip / Broken Road after a strong south-easterly.

species.size: No sizes given for this stand; the surf stretch produces mostly small to medium fish
species.bait: Fresh bloodworm first, then prawn or a chokka/sardine combo, on small, long baits with a small float; wade out and cast at low tide
species.notes: Sealine: "Steenbras: throughout the year"; AF "caught steenbras here on fresh worm" at The Horses; alanlloyd: "dont be afraid of fishing low tide, just wade as far as you can and cast out a bloodworm". Jacita May 2025: steenbras active at Broken Road, "bonus ... steenbras".

species.size: Not given by the sources; usually a small pan-size fish
species.bait: Bloodworm and mixed grill baits
species.notes: Only mention is Jacita 16 May 2025: "Steenbras, galjoen, and kolstert are active" at Macassar, Broken Road and Betty's Bay, "especially on high tide".

species.size: Not given by the sources
species.bait: Fish baits (sardine, pike, mullet); no source reports spoons or plugs here
species.notes: Sealine, for the Muizenberg to Strandfontein stretch: "Elf: Dec till March. Bait mostly fish. Sardine, pike or mullet." Swartklip 2007: "Elf on Fish Bait". Jacita notes a slider can tempt elf in the surf generally.

species.size: One fish over 5 kg reported, called the first seen there
species.bait: Not stated (bloodworm and prawn are the stretch's baits)
species.notes: Single Sealine report from the Sunrise end of the stretch in August 2010, described as unusual for the area.

name: Mnandi Beach
area: Rocklands, Mitchells Plain (False Bay north shore, between Strandfontein Pavilion and the Wolfgat cliffs)
coord_source: Stand: the beach placemark embedded in Wanderlog's Mnandi Beach map/Google Maps links (-34.075607, 18.61151), on the sand about 600 m west of the resort. Car park: OSM/Nominatim "Mnandi Swimming Pool, Weltevreden Road, Rocklands" (-34.0743862, 18.6183903), the resort complex the merge step used. Neither is a confirmed angler stand; the beach runs about 5 km and anglers spread along it, so treat both as approximate. Nominatim found no "Mnandi Beach" feature and a photon query returned unrelated KwaZulu-Natal streets.

access.note: Mnandi resort and swimming-pool car park at the southern end of Weltevreden Road, Rocklands (OSM). City page: 222 parking bays plus six disabled bays; Wanderlog: public parking near the beach entrance is monitored by SAPS, the access road suits all cars, and the walk from the parking to the waves is 'a bit rough'.

bottom: Sand surf beach with gutters and banks; limestone cliffs and ledges of the Wolfgat Nature Reserve start east of the resort (Jacita groups it with the beaches; the lekkeslaap/tourism descriptions seen in the cached search mention the Wolfgat limestone cliffs).
permit: DFFE (Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment) recreational angling permit, sold at Post Offices, for every angler. Standard national bag and size limits apply; white steenbras is a restricted species (bag limit 1, minimum size 60 cm in the recreational regulations as I know them; verify against the current permit conditions). No local permit, SANParks fee or CapeNature licence; a resort or pool entrance tariff may apply at the gate but is not stated on the City page.
legality: Allowed, with a DFFE recreational angling permit. Mnandi sits on the False Bay north shore at about lon 18.61, east of Bailey's Cottage at Muizenberg where the Table Mountain National Park MPA ends and well west of the Eerste River mouth at Macassar where the Helderberg MPA begins, so it falls in no MPA controlled or restricted zone (checked against the 2004 TMNP MPA zoning and the Helderberg MPA limits in the brief). The City of Cape Town's own Mnandi Beach page lists "Fishing" among the resort's activities alongside safe swimming, water sports and picnics (page gives no restrictions on where or when). No SANParks entry fee or CapeNature licence applies. The beach east of the resort runs along the City's Wolfgat Nature Reserve; whether angling is permitted along the reserve frontage was not checked.
description: Mnandi is the City of Cape Town's resort beach at the bottom of Mitchells Plain, a long sandy surf beach on the north shore of False Bay with the limestone cliffs of Wolfgat Nature Reserve to the east and Strandfontein Pavilion to the west. Anglers fish it as part of the Strandfontein-to-Macassar surf strip: Jacita's weekly report lists "Strandfontein, Mnandi, Macassar and the Strand area" as "prime time for targeting Baardman and White Steenbras" in winter on moonshine and wonderworm, worm baits fished on small hooks in flat surf of 0.8 to 1.2 m. The resort has a 222-bay car park and summer lifeguards, but Wanderlog's listing warns of armed robberies targeting fishermen, so go in a group and in daylight.
hazards: Armed robberies targeting fishermen and visitors (Wanderlog listing: 'The area is known for armed robberies targeting both fishermen and visitors'; reviewers: fish 'in numbers', daylight only, 'please be careful not to visit at night and always be in groups').

Surf beach with lifeguards only during peak summer periods (City); wading and bait-walking in the gutters carries the usual rip risk on this False Bay strip (rips not sourced for Mnandi specifically).
Walk from the car park to the water described as 'a bit rough' (Wanderlog review).
Wind: Jacita's general False Bay advice is that 'Wind can be nasty', the south-easter blows onto this shore.
access_notes: City of Cape Town resort beach (Blue Flag since 2004) at the end of Weltevreden Road, Rocklands, Mitchells Plain, on the seaward side of Baden Powell Drive. 222 parking bays plus six disabled bays at the resort; parking monitored by SAPS, who per Wanderlog "mostly remain in their patrol vehicles". Short walk over the dune to the sand, described by one reviewer as "a bit rough". Lifeguards only "during peak periods in summer" (City). Opening hours and any resort or pool entrance tariff are not stated on the City page; the beach itself is open public shore. Safety: Wanderlog's listing says "the area is known for armed robberies targeting both fishermen and visitors"; reviewers advise fishing "in numbers", visiting in daylight ("relatively safe during the day") and never at night. Drive: about 22 min from Westlake and 33 min from Green Point (OSRM free-flow estimate, 2026-10-29).
unverified: Light tackle: no cached page uses the words 'light tackle' for Mnandi; the light-bait method is inferred from the target species (baardman, white steenbras) and the worm baits named for flat surf.

The Kegan Mattheys (Apr 2026) quote in the merge notes about belman on 'light to medium tackle with scaled-down hooks and leaders' could not be confirmed: the novanews column it was attributed to was fetched on 30 Oct 2026 and does not mention Mnandi (it names galjoen at Strandfontein and Macassar and tuna off Strand).
Tide preference 'pushing' is Jacita's general False Bay rock-and-surf advice ('Fish with confidence on the push or turn of the tide'), not a Mnandi-specific statement.
Kob: no kob landed at Mnandi itself in the cache; inferred from the Sealine report of the same stretch.
Typical fish sizes at Mnandi are not given by any source.
Facing bearing (173) is estimated from the coastline orientation between Strandfontein and Monwabisi, not stated by any source.
Rip currents on this beach are not sourced for Mnandi specifically.
Resort opening hours and any entrance/pool tariff are not stated on the City page.
Whether angling is permitted along the Wolfgat Nature Reserve frontage east of the resort beach was not checked.
White steenbras bag and size limits are quoted from memory of the DFFE recreational regulations, not from a cached page.
Road directions (Baden Powell Drive / Weltevreden Road junction) are from general knowledge.

issues: Legality holds. At lon 18.61 the spot is on the False Bay north shore, east of Bailey's Cottage at Muizenberg (where the TMNP MPA ends) and well west of the Eerste River mouth at Macassar (where the Helderberg MPA starts). It is in no restricted or controlled zone. The City of Cape Town's Mnandi Beach page lists 'Fishing' among the resort's activities (cached 29 Oct 2026). Two things were not checked, and neither makes the record wrong: whether the City's coastal by-law bars angling inside the lifeguarded bathing area (Wanderlog says 'swimming is allowed within designated areas'), and the Wolfgat Nature Reserve frontage east of the resort. The record's stand point is about 600 m west of the resort, away from Wolfgat.

Coordinates land on the place, but coord_source describes them wrongly. A Nominatim reverse geocode of -34.0756, 18.6115 (fetched 2 Nov 2026) resolves to an OSM car park (amenity=parking, Lukannon Drive, Mitchells Plain, Ward 43) at -34.07538, 18.61077, not 'on the sand'. Wanderlog's embedded Google placemark (-34.075607, 18.61151) is confirmed, so the point is Google's 'Mnandi Beach' pin. It is within 500 m of the beach, so the coordinates are not refuted. But the angler stand should be moved a short way seaward onto the sand once checked on a map, and coord_source should say the pin falls on a beach car park.

The Wanderlog quotes the record relies on are all confirmed by a fresh fetch (2 Nov 2026). They were not in the 29 Oct cache except as a search summary: 'popular fishing spot', 'This is also a great spot for fishing', 'armed robberies targeting both fishermen and visitors', 'fishing in numbers', SAPS 'mostly remain in their patrol vehicles', 'a bit rough from the parking to the waves', 'relatively safe during the day', 'please be careful not to visit at night and always be in groups', and the road to the parking 'perfect for all cars'. The record leaves out a more recent review (Grant M., Nov 2025): 'Great beach for fishing... I went with a group of fisherman and we were not bothered by anyone.' This is a newer angling data point and slightly softens the safety warning.

The angling evidence is thin but real. The only angling-specific page naming Mnandi with species is Jacita's week-24 report (8 to 16 June 2025), one sentence grouping 'Strandfontein, Mnandi, Macassar and the Strand area' for baardman and white steenbras, with a general top bait of moonshine and wonderworm. The Sealine report only says the reporter checked Mnandi and that it 'had few anglers'. That is enough to show shore bait fishing happens here, so the evidence is not refuted.

Light-tackle fit is inferred and partly contradicted. Jacita's companion rock-and-surf article (Aug 2025) says this north-shore strip needs heavier gear: Macassar needs 'good casting distance and strong tackle to hold ground', 'side pull and deep water gutters are common' with 170 to 225 g sinkers, and in False Bay 'go heavier on the sinkers'. Worm baits for baardman in flat surf fit light bait fishing, but the light-tackle method holds only on calm days. The record should say so instead of presenting it as the norm.

Months look invented. Baardman and white steenbras are given months [5,6,7,8], but the only source is a single report for 8 to 16 June 2025, so only June is sourced and May, July and August are extrapolation. Kob months [9,10] come from one Sept 2010 report about Monwabisi, not Mnandi.

species.size: Not stated by the sources for this spot.
species.bait: Moonshine and wonderworm ('Top bait: Moonshine and Wonderworm' in the week-24 report), fished on small hooks in flat surf of 0.8 to 1.2 m.
species.notes: Jacita, week 24 (8 to 16 June 2025): 'Strandfontein, Mnandi, Macassar and the Strand area' are 'prime time for targeting Baardman and White Steenbras'; 'Flat surf is the name of the game this week'. Winter, seasonal.

species.size: Not stated by the sources for this spot. Restricted species: bag limit 1 and 60 cm minimum size in the recreational regulations as I know them, so most fish are released; verify current limits.
species.bait: Moonshine and wonderworm (the report's top baits for the week), small hooks, flat surf.
species.notes: Same Jacita week-24 sentence as baardman: Mnandi named with Strandfontein, Macassar and the Strand as 'prime time for targeting Baardman and White Steenbras'. Winter, seasonal.

name: Monwabisi
area: False Bay north shore, Khayelitsha (off Baden Powell Drive)
coord_source: OSM "Monwabisi Tidal Pool" node (water=tidal_channel) via photon.komoot.io on 2026-10-30, taken as the stand at the dolosse breakwater ("the Blokke") beside the resort car park (the 2010 report fishes "the parking-lot hoop and the first set of Blokke"). The merge step's nominatim "Monwabisi, Khayelitsha" place node at -34.0725, 18.6936 sits about 600 m ENE and is a suburb point, not the beach. Car park not separately geocoded.
bottom: Sand surf with low reef ledges and rock towards the cliffs to the west ("reefs at Monwabisi", "monwabisi ledge"), plus the concrete dolosse breakwater ("the Blokke") that forms the tidal pool.
permit: DFFE recreational angling (marine) permit, bought at the Post Office; no MPA or SANParks permit needed. Resort day-visitor tariff on the City page: R14 adult, R7 child (date of tariff unknown, verify). Species rules from the cached sources: galjoen closed season 15 October to end February; elf bag four per person, 30 cm minimum; kob five per person, 50 cm minimum; geelbek two per person.
legality: Allowed. Monwabisi is on the north shore of False Bay east of Muizenberg, so it is outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA (which runs from Bailey's Cottage at Muizenberg west and south round Cape Point), and it is west of the Eerste River mouth, so outside the Helderberg MPA; no restricted zone applies. It is a City of Cape Town resort whose page acknowledges anglers ("in winter it is generally only used by anglers"); fishing is not on the resort's activities list but nothing found prohibits it. Checked against the MPA boundaries given for this project, the City resort and beach pages (cached 29 Oct 2026) and the Sealine angling threads.
description: A City of Cape Town resort beach on the north shore of False Bay between the Swartklip cliffs and Macassar, where a dolosse breakwater ("the Blokke") encloses a tidal pool, with sand beach either side and low reef ledges towards the cliffs to the west. Anglers fish the breakwater, the ledges and the open surf for kob, with elf and geelbek in summer: a 2011 Sealine lure thread lists "monwabisi ledge" among the "deeper surf spots for cob geelbek and elf" on dropshot/artlure and advises that by the cliffs "a decent cast with braid an u could be into a fat cob", while a 2010 report had "loads of Kob" caught at the parking-lot hoop and the first set of Blokke on moonshine and bloodworm. The City's own page says that in winter the resort "is generally only used by anglers".
hazards: Personal safety: the Strand tackle-shop columnist says Macassar, Monwabisi and Strandfontein "can be unsafe and should rather be avoided if you are unfamiliar with the area and surrounds"; regulars on this stretch advise fishing in a group and leaving before sunset

White sharks: the northern shores of False Bay from Macassar to Muizenberg have the highest inshore white shark activity in the bay, and shark spotters at Monwabisi saw three white sharks on their first day (2012); keep wading shallow
Rip currents: the breakwater was built because of drownings in the strong False Bay currents here; the open surf beyond the pool is exposed to the south-westerly swell and onshore south-easters
Seals take hooked kob and belman
Dolosse breakwater (the Blokke) is slippery concrete with swell washing over it at high water
Crowded with bait anglers when the kob are running
access_notes: Monwabisi Resort, off Baden Powell Drive, Khayelitsha. City resort with parking for 400 vehicles, picnic and braai sites, lifeguards and shark spotters in the bathing season; opening hours are not published on the City pages. Day-visitor fee R14 adult / R7 child per the City page. The breakwater and pool are right by the car park ("the parking-lot hoop"); the ledges and cliffs are a walk west along the beach. Safety: the Strand tackle-shop columnist says Macassar, Monwabisi and Strandfontein "can be unsafe and should rather be avoided if you are unfamiliar with the area and surrounds" and that Fishing Republic (Strand) runs guided trips there; Sealine regulars fishing this stretch advise going in a group and not fishing after sunset. Busy with anglers when the kob are on.
unverified: White steenbras (listed by the merge step): only sourced for the neighbouring Mnandi, Strandfontein and Macassar beaches (Jacita, June 2025), not for Monwabisi itself, so left off the species list
Tide preference: no Monwabisi-specific source; 'pushing' follows the regional Jacita advice to fish the push or turn of the tide in False Bay
Day-visitor tariff (R14/R7) is from the City resort page of unknown date; whether it is charged to anglers in winter or at the gate is not stated
Opening or gate hours: not published on the City pages
Exact car park position: implied to be beside the breakwater ("parking-lot hoop") but not geocoded
Whether the City Coastal By-law restricts casting inside the demarcated bathing area while lifeguards are on duty in season
Current condition of the dolosse breakwater and pool: the angling reports date from 2007-2013
Facing bearing of 180 is read off the coastline orientation (Mnandi to Macassar runs roughly east-west), not from a source

issues: Legality holds. At lon 18.687 the spot is well east of Bailey's Cottage, Muizenberg (about 18.46 E), where the TMNP MPA ends, and west of the Eerste River mouth at Macassar, where the Helderberg MPA starts. It is not in any listed restricted zone. The City resort page (cached 29 Oct 2026) says 'in winter it is generally only used by anglers' and prohibits nothing. The City beach page has no fishing rules. Nothing in the evidence shows a by-law ban on fishing. The permit, galjoen closed season, elf 4/30 cm and kob 5/50 cm limits match the cached sources.

Evidence holds, but the record overstates the lure detail. I re-fetched the 2011 Sealine 'lure fishing cape town area' thread, which is not in the cached evidence file. Post #4 (Dorain du preez, 4 Nov 2011) says 'also Monwabizi by the clifs... a decent cast with braid an u could be into a fat cob'. Post #6 (subaruseun, 4 Nov 2011) lists 'monwabisi ledge to tweede baai surf' under 'deeper surf spots for cob geelbek and elf'. The page names dropshot and artlure only as general methods, not for these spots, and never mentions paddle-tails. So the record's 'on dropshot/artlure' and its kob method 'dropshot or paddle-tail' are inferred from the thread's topic, not quoted.

The 2010 'Monwabisi Kobbies' report (cached) was bait fishing only ('old moonshine and bloodworm'), and the record reports that correctly. The record reads 'parking-lot hoop' and 'first set of Blokke' as the dolosse breakwater, but the cached summary calls the Blokke 'rocks'. Treat the breakwater reading as an inference.

Galjoen: the evidence file only supports the 2013 thread's plan to fish 'reefs at Monwabisi' for galjoen (Sealine search snippets for Soetwater and Misty Cliffs). The quote 'Been to monwa reefs and misty recently. Awesome spots' is not in the cached evidence, and I did not re-fetch that thread, so it is unverified. The adjoining Swart Klip cliffs had galjoen 'most days' in the 2007 macassar/strand thread, which supports the species locally but not at the spot itself.
Elf abundance 'regular' is overstated. The only Monwabisi-specific support is its place in post #6's general list of deeper surf spots for cob, geelbek and elf, so it should be 'occasional'.

Harders abundance 'regular' is invented. The source only says 'Harders were also in the water' (2010). The tidal-pool float method is also unsourced, and nothing checked confirms that fishing inside the City tidal pool is allowed. Neither the City pages nor any by-law were checked on this.

species.size: Mostly undersized to just-legal school fish (50 cm minimum); a 62 cm fish was reported in Sept 2010 and the lure thread talks of the odd fat cob on a long cast
species.method: spinning (dropshot or paddle-tail on braid, long cast) or light bait
species.bait: Dropshot/artlure (paddle-tails) on braid with a long cast from the ledge or cliffs; bait anglers at the Blokke used moonshine and bloodworm, and the regional columns list chokka, sardine and live mullet

Season from the general False Bay sources (Sept/Oct to March/April, best at night and in brown kob water after a south-easter). Seals steal hooked fish here.

species.bait: Bread or dough on small hooks under a float (standard harder method; no Monwabisi-specific bait given)

name: Swartklip
aka: Monwabisi bays (the resort stretch, which a 2011 poster says used to be called Swartklip)
area: Mitchells Plain / Khayelitsha coast, north shore of False Bay
coord_source: Approximate, low confidence. Nominatim (bounded query, 30 Oct 2026) returned no coastal feature named Swartklip, only the Swartklip Refuse Transfer Station (-34.0494, 18.6488, inland) and Swartklip Road, whose seaward segment in Endlovini (-34.0678, 18.6612) meets Baden Powell Drive. The merge-step coordinate (-34.064, 18.63) sits inland near Wolfgat. The stand is placed on the sandy bays just west of the Monwabisi tidal pool, following the Sealine 2011 directions ("walk down to the beach area about 3/4 bays to choose from", "2nd bay" behind the day camping site), with the Monwabisi resort position taken from general knowledge rather than a geocoder result. Treat as within about 1 km.

access.note: Monwabisi resort car park inside the security gate (R8 then R10 in Feb 2011; current fee unverified). Sealine 2011: park 'next to main building' by the dirt bins on the right-hand side, or 'at the toilets side quite far in'; Metro police beach patrol is based there; two posters reported vehicle break-ins, one 'inside the paid area'. From the car park walk down to the beach: three or four bays west of the tidal pool, the pool and its breakwater. Position approximate.

bottom: Sand bays between low cliffs and rocky points, with reef and gullies off the points and the Monwabisi pool breakwater ("right side cliff at the bottom where the rocks begin", "the points usually give deeper water", Sealine 2011); foul ground offshore that snags lures from boats (Ski-Boat 2020). Kob "feed over sand and on the edge of reefs and gullies" (Ski-Boat 2022).
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine, from the Post Office) for every angler; the Monwabisi resort charges a gate fee instead of a fishing permit (R10 in 2011). National species rules apply: galjoen closed season 15 October to end February (merge notes; national regulation, not re-checked this pass); silver kob minimum 50 cm and bag limit of five (Ski-Boat, April 2020); geelbek two per angler (Ski-Boat, 2022).
legality: Allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit. Sea spot on the north shore of False Bay between the Wolfgat/Mnandi cliffs and Macassar: it is outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA (whose controlled zone ends at Bailey's Cottage, Muizenberg, well to the west) and outside the Helderberg MPA (which begins at the Eerste River mouth at Macassar, about 6 km east), and it is in none of the 2004 restricted zones. The City of Cape Town's own Wolfgat Nature Reserve page (fetched 30 Oct 2026) says the reserve "is the perfect destination for picnicking, fishing and paragliding", with no fishing prohibition or extra permit stated. Sealine posters fish the Monwabisi resort bays, pool and breakwater openly after paying the gate fee (2011) and the beach off Baden Powell (2007). No local by-law against angling was found.
description: Swartklip is the stretch of sandy bays and low dark cliffs on the north shore of False Bay between the Wolfgat Nature Reserve cliffs and the Monwabisi tidal pool, reached off Baden Powell Drive and, for the bays, through the Monwabisi resort gate; a 2011 Sealine poster notes the resort area "used to be called Swartklip". Shore anglers report galjoen, belman and elf "biting on Prawn and Wonder Worm... Elf on Fish Bait" (May 2007) and "Cob, Elf, Steenbra, Bellman, Galjoen, W/stump" from the bays, the points and the pool breakwater (Feb 2011), while a False Bay shore-spot guide calls Swartklip/Broken Road a "legendary stretch for surf anglers" for kob and steenbras after a strong south-easter. It is an exposed, shallow surf beach over sand with rock at the points, and every source says to fish in a group and leave before dark.
hazards: Crime: every angling source warns against fishing alone or after dark. 'DEFINITELY not alone there after sunset its dangerous' (Sealine 2007); 'its not safe to fish alone and especially at night so fish in numbers' (Sealine 2011); 'Had 2 instances of break-ins to my vehicle there... Once inside the paid area' (Sealine 2011); the City's Wolfgat page requires all activities to be done in groups.
Slippery rocks on the pool breakwater: 'the breakwater rocks are slippery, so exercise caution and watch the tides' (Sealine 2011).
Cliffs: 'dont fish of the cliff i say, just a tip use the beach' (Sealine 2011).
Exposed surf beach open to the full south-westerly swell entering False Bay; wading to cast ('wade and get that bait out deep', Sealine 2007) puts you in the surf.
access_notes: Reached off Baden Powell Drive (R310). Sealine 2007 directions: "if you go down baden Powell from the N2 towards strandfontein, the first long bend to the right goes down hill... then the first turn off left is swart klip... after the first speed bump is a road to the left, go down there". Sealine 2011: pay at the security gate (R8, "now R10.00" in Feb 2011), walk down to the beach, "about 3/4 bays to choose from"; favourites are "the back of the day camping site, 2nd bay", the "right side cliff at the bottom where the rocks begin", and "off the pool, breakwater and in the bay itself"; "the points usually give deeper water, bigger fish". The adjoining City of Cape Town Wolfgat Nature Reserve (Baden Powell Drive, Mitchells Plain) is free, open Monday to Friday 07:30 to 16:00 (weekend hours not listed), lists fishing among its activities and states "For safety reasons, all activities must take place in groups" (tel 021 392 5134/5, wolfgat.naturereserve@capetown.gov.za). Resort gate hours not found. Safety from every angling source: "DEFINITELY not alone there after sunset its dangerous" (2007); "not fishing once the sun starts setting, and DONT go alone.. groups is usually best" (2007); "its not safe to fish alone and especially at night so fish in numbers" (2011); "Had 2 instances of break-ins to my vehicle there" (2011). Drive: OSRM free-flow 26 min from Westlake and 32 min from Green Point (merge step, 29 Oct 2026) to the rough merge coordinate; allow about 5 min more to the Monwabisi gate, which is roughly 6 km further east.
unverified: Exact stand and car-park coordinates: no geocoder feature exists for the spot; the stand was placed from the Sealine 2011 directions and general knowledge of where the Monwabisi resort is.

That Swartklip and the Monwabisi resort bays are the same place rests on one 2011 poster ('It used to be called Swartklip... under correction'); the 2007 'gravel pitch / 1ste and 2de baai' nickname may have been meant for Sunrise Circle rather than Swartklip.
Current Monwabisi gate fee and gate hours (R8 to R10 in Feb 2011); whether the gate is open at first light.

Galjoen closed season and sizes, and the elf closed season (1 Sept to 30 Nov), are quoted from the national recreational regulations as generally known, not re-checked against the current DFFE brochure this pass.
Monwabisi beach's reputation for rip currents and drownings is general knowledge, not in the sources opened.
A search snippet said a Sealine poster called Swartklip 'an excellent spot for kob' in the 1970s; that page was not opened.
Baden Powell Drive is sometimes closed by windblown sand or for safety along this stretch; not checked.
Months for kob and elf are partly the general False Bay seasons from Ski-Boat rather than spot-specific.

Geelbek 'Swartklip to Macassar' (Ski-Boat 2022) and the 'Kapteins Klip/Manadi and Swartklip' kob run (Ski-Boat 2020) are boat-fishing references and are not counted as shore species. Rays (Seaside Cottages) and barbel (Sealine 2011) are bait-caught by-catch and are left out of the species list.

issues: Legality holds. The stand (-34.0795, 18.6935) is on the Monwabisi shore. That is far east of Bailey's Cottage at Muizenberg, where the TMNP MPA controlled zone ends, and west of the Eerste River mouth at Macassar, where the Helderberg MPA no-fishing strip starts. None of the 2004 restricted zones covers it. One point is unchecked: the Wolfgat page the legality text leans on (City of Cape Town, 'fetched 30 Oct 2026') is not in the cached evidence file and was not re-fetched. It is also an adjoining reserve, not the stand. Whether a City coastal by-law limits angling off the Monwabisi tidal pool, which the record suggests fishing ('off the pool, breakwater'), was not found either way.

Angling evidence holds. I re-fetched https://sealine.co.za/threads/monwabisi.46601/ (thread started 2 Feb 2011 by litemaster). It is a real shore-angling thread covering the beach, bays, rocks, the pool and the breakwater. Species: RINEX lists 'Cob,Elf,Steenbra,Bellman,Galjoen ,W/stump & barbel'; BigBen lists 'Das,Belman,Wildeperd,Bras,Kob,Elf' and 'caught a beenbek behind the pool... on white mussel during March fishi'n for galjoen'. Those are light-bait species, so the light-tackle fit is genuine.

The Swartklip name rests on one poster: RINEX, 2 Feb 2011, 'It used to be called Swartklip.' Every other source places 'Swartklip' only loosely between Mnandi/Kapteinsklip and Macassar (the Ski-Boat boat articles and the Seaside Cottages list). The Nominatim features named Swartklip (Swartklip Road meets Baden Powell at about -34.0678, 18.6612) sit about 3 km west of the stand. If 'Swartklip' means the Swartklip Road / cliffs stretch rather than the Monwabisi resort bays, the record mixes two places. The directions, safety notes and most species actually describe Monwabisi.

Coordinates are consistent with what the record describes, the Monwabisi bays. Nominatim (fetched 2 Nov 2026) puts the Monwabisi suburb node at -34.0725, 18.6936. The stand is about 780 m due south of that, on the shoreline, and the access point (-34.0785, 18.698) is beside it. A second Monwabisi suburb node sits at -34.0680, 18.7080. The resort and tidal pool themselves were not geocoded, so the exact stand is still within about 1 km, as the record says.

Quotes I could not confirm. These are attributed to Sealine 2011 but did not appear in my re-fetch, which may have trimmed them: 'the back of the day camping site, 2nd bay', 'the points usually give deeper water, bigger fish', and 'Metro police beach patrol is based there'. The record says 'Dassie' heads a poster's list, but the actual text is 'Das'. The beenbek size 'about 3 kg' did not appear: Strepie asks 'What size was it?' and no answer was returned.

The thread itself identifies the beenbek. Strepie replies 'Beenbek = Cracker!', meaning a musselcracker, so the record's 'identity unverified' label is too cautious. Rename the entry to musselcracker (beenbek). It is still a single fish caught 'a few yrs back' before 2011, so 'rare' is right.

name: Macassar Beach
aka: Macassar Beach (west of the Eerste River mouth)
area: Macassar, north-east False Bay (between Monwabisi and Strand)
coord_source: Nominatim result for "Macassar Beach Resort", cached 29 Oct 2026: Macassar Pavilion, Strand Road, Sandvlei (-34.0750870, 18.7488049). This is the City resort and car park on the beachfront, and anglers fish the surf directly in front of it. No OSM point was found for the Eerste River mouth, which is the eastern legal limit; Photon on 30 Oct 2026 returned only upstream Eerste River segments near Stellenbosch.

access.note: Macassar Pavilion / Macassar Beach Resort car parks off Beach Road, reached from Macassar Road (City of Cape Town page). You walk from the car park onto the sand, and no vehicles are allowed on the beach.

bottom: Sand beach with deep gutters and rocky ledges ("Macassar ledges", District Mail 2022; "side pull and deep water gutters", "watch the rocks", Jacita 2025)
mouth: The Eerste River mouth is the eastern limit of legal fishing. The Helderberg MPA's western boundary is a line running 180 degrees true from the mouth, and Sealine anglers say the "Mond side of the fence is a no go zone". No source says whether the mouth is currently open or closed, or who manages it. A search summary only notes that the mouth opens and closes.
permit: You need a DFFE marine recreational angling permit (e-permits at fishing.dffe.gov.za). Normal bag limits, size limits and closed seasons apply. Kob have a 60 cm minimum size, which Kegan Mattheys says to "always double-check". Jacita (Oct 2025) says galjoen and elf were "out of season" in late October. You cannot fish or collect bait east of the Eerste River mouth (Helderberg MPA). No vehicles are allowed on the beach, and people were fined for this in 2017. The beach resort is a City of Cape Town facility whose fees are set in the Recreation and Parks Tariffs Booklet. I could not confirm whether a day-entry fee applies to anglers.
legality: Fishing is allowed with a permit on the beach WEST of the Eerste River mouth. Macassar lies outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, whose controlled zone runs from Bailey's Cottage in Muizenberg round to Mouille Point. From the Eerste River mouth east to the Lourens River mouth in Strand, out to 500 m seaward of the high-water mark, is the Helderberg MPA. That whole stretch is a no-take zone with no fishing and no bait collection (Wikipedia: "The whole MPA is a no-take reserve"). The City manages it under the Marine Living Resources Act, and in August 2025 it asked visitors via the District Mail to "refrain from any form of fishing in this area". A 2017 Sealine thread reports that anglers "fishing at the fence" by Somchem were fined, with "Mond side of the fence is a no go zone". I checked the Wikipedia Helderberg MPA boundaries, the District Mail article of 6 Aug 2025, the 2017 Sealine fines thread and the City's Macassar Beach page, which promotes the beach for anglers.
description: Macassar Beach is a long, exposed False Bay surf beach in front of the City's Macassar Pavilion resort. The sand is broken by deep gutters and rocky ledges. Anglers spin for kob here with paddle-tails, spoons, bucktails and stickbaits worked "low and slow". They fish the ledges and gutters with worm, prawn and mussel baits for galjoen, bellman, blacktail and white steenbras. Fishing stops at the Eerste River mouth, because the beach east of it is the Helderberg MPA no-take zone.
hazards: Crime and robbery. Sealine posters call Macassar "a security risk not really worth it" (2016) and say the stretch from Strandfontein to Macassar Beach "should only be visited in groups" (2014). The District Mail (Dec 2022) says Macassar, Monwabisi and Strandfontein "can be unsafe and should rather be avoided if you are unfamiliar with the area".
Fish in daylight and in groups: "fish during the day - safety reasons" (Sealine 2020), "There is safety in numbers at Macs" (Sealine 2019).
Exposed coastline with "powerful waves and currents" (City of Cape Town).
Strong side pull and deep gutters. Jacita suggests 170-225 g sinkers for bait anglers, so light bait rigs will not hold in big surf.
Rocky ledges: "Watch the rocks and be ready to reposition quickly as the swell shifts" (Jacita).
MPA boundary: anglers have been fined for fishing at the Somchem fence by the Eerste River mouth (Sealine 2017).
A licensed trek-netting operation works this beach (City of Cape Town).
Strong winds draw kitesurfers to the beach (City of Cape Town).
access_notes: This is the City of Cape Town's Macassar Beach resort on Beach Road, reached from Macassar Road. It has several car parks, toilets, picnic and braai areas, a camping area, a slipway and lifeguards in peak periods (City page). The City page gives no opening hours. Bookings: 021 444 7493, macassar.resort@capetown.gov.za. No 4x4 is needed: "dont need 4x4 I used Corsa bakkie and is close to Strand" (Sealine 2020). Driving on the beach is banned and fined. For safety, fish in daylight and with other anglers. A 2019 poster found it "relatively safe as there is always a lot of guys there". Keep west of the Eerste River mouth and the Somchem fence.
unverified: Facing of 200 degrees is my own estimate from the coastline's WNW-ESE trend between Monwabisi, the Macassar Pavilion and the Eerste mouth. No source gives a bearing.
Exact position of the Eerste River mouth and the Somchem fence. The merge step's -34.0812, 18.7648 is unsourced, and I found no OSM point for the mouth.
Whether the Eerste River mouth is currently open or closed, and who manages it.
Exact closed-season dates for galjoen and elf. Sources only say both are 'out of season' in late October.
Whether the City resort charges anglers an entry fee, and its gate hours.
Typical kob size at Macassar specifically.
Elf on lures at Macassar. No source names a lure for elf here.
Geelbek from the shore. The only Macassar geelbek source (Angler Publications 2022) is about anchored boats from Swartklip to Macassar, so I left it out of the species list.
Hottentot and red steenbras appear only in a boat-fishing article covering the Strandfontein-Macassar sand, so I left both out.

Whether light tackle is practical on rough days. Jacita says bait anglers need 170-225 g sinkers in the side pull. The light-tackle fit rests on the lure fishing in calmer surf described by the District Mail and Sealine.
Sharks are caught here (Sealine 2020 lists 'shark' among Macassar species), but only as bait catches by rock-and-surf anglers. I left them out of the species list.

issues: Legality holds. Wikipedia (Helderberg MPA, cached 29 Oct 2026) puts the MPA's western boundary on a line at 180 degrees true from the Eerste River mouth. The District Mail of 6 Aug 2025 (novanews ?p=267430) confirms the MPA runs from the Lourens mouth in the east to the Eerste mouth in the west. Macassar is also outside the TMNP MPA, which ends at Bailey's Cottage. The pin at 18.7488 E is about 1 to 1.5 km west of where the mouth should be: Wikipedia puts the MPA's centre at 18.783 E with about 4 km of shoreline, and the merge step's unsourced mouth point is 18.7648 E. So the pin is outside the no-take zone. I still could not confirm the mouth's exact position, because an Overpass query for the Eerste River geometry failed (HTTP 000, corporate proxy).

The aka list includes 'Eersterivier mond (east boundary)'. That is the MPA boundary, not a name for the legal spot. If someone searches 'Eerste mouth' or 'Mond' and lands on this record, it points them at the edge of the no-take zone, where anglers 'fishing at the fence' were fined (Sealine 2017, view_topic.php?id=105835). It should come out of aka.

Several quotes in the record are not in the cached evidence, because the file is capped at about 90 KB and a fresh fetch failed (sealine.co.za returned HTTP 000 through the proxy). I could not verify any of the following: the Sealine 2016 paddle-tail quotes ('a few very good spots at macassar to catch kob on paddle tails', 'caught kob on paddletail and spoon'), from thread 93538; 'a security risk not really worth it' (2016); 'dont need 4x4 I used Corsa bakkie' and the kolstert/shark species list (2020), from thread 102094. Thread 102094 appears in the evidence only as a search-result link.

Light-tackle fit is supported, but only just. The District Mail of 25 Sep 2025 (?p=268986) says 'Strandfontein & Macassar Beaches are excellent surf-fishing stretches for working bucktails, jigs and stickbaits', and lists paddle tails and spoons as kob lures in general. That is an angling-specific source describing lure fishing from the shore here. On the other side, Jacita (12 Aug 2025) says Macassar needs 'good casting distance and strong tackle to hold ground' with 170-225 g sinkers, and an older Sealine thread recommends a 14 ft rod for kob. Bait fishing at this spot is mostly heavy surf tackle, not light bait rigs with small hooks.

The kob size field mixes in '90-100 cm False Bay reef kob (2022)'. In District Mail ?p=65894 that figure refers to unnamed False Bay reefs, fished with 14-36 kg tackle, not to the shore at Macassar. It should not sit in this spot's size field.

The permit text gives one 60 cm minimum for 'kob (silver/dusky)'. The District Mail figure is for Argyrosomus japonicus (dusky kob). A search summary in the evidence ties the 60 cm / one-per-day rule to 'east of Cape Agulhas', and Macassar is west of Agulhas. DFFE sets separate limits for silver and dusky kob, so the page should say to check the current DFFE limits for each species rather than state one figure.
