species.notes: "Reports from Broken Road and Macassar show good Bellman catches with bonus cob and steenbras in the mix" (Jacita, 30 May 2025). Jacita (June 2025) lists Macassar for baardman on flat surf. The District Mail (Sep 2022) calls Macassar Beach a "belman hot spot" but says that year was very poor for belman.

species.size: "Good-sized ones" (District Mail, Sep 2022). No measurements given.
species.bait: Fish baits. No Macassar-specific lure or bait is named.
species.notes: "Macs has been very good to me lately with kob and elf" (Sealine, Sep 2019). The District Mail (30 Sep 2022) reports elf "with some good-sized ones caught in Strand, Macassar and towards Strandfontein". Sealine anglers give December to March as the season. A closed season applies, and Jacita (Oct 2025) says elf is "out of season" in late October.

species.size: Mostly 30-35 cm (District Mail, Sep 2022)
species.bait: Red bait, white mussel, worms, prawn
species.notes: "Macassar ledges have consistently produced galjoen throughout the season", with bigger seas helping (Kegan Mattheys, 14 Sep 2022). "Macassar looks promising for galjoen anglers" (Jacita, June 2025). Jacita (July 2025) also names the reef areas between Strandfontein and Macassar. The closed season covers late spring and summer, and Jacita (Oct 2025) says galjoen is "out of season" then.

species.size: No typical size is given for Macassar. The legal minimum is 60 cm (District Mail 2025), and False Bay reef kob of 90-100 cm were reported in 2022.
species.bait: Lures: paddle-tails and spoons (Sealine 2016), plus bucktails, jigs, stickbaits and slow-pitch jigs, all worked "low and slow" near the bottom (District Mail 2025). Bait: fresh chokka strips, sardine fillets, live mullet (Jacita Oct 2025).
species.notes: "There are a few very good spots at macassar to catch kob on paddle tails" and "I have caught kob on paddletail and spoon caught off the beach at macassar" (Sealine, Mar 2016). "Strandfontein & Macassar Beaches are excellent surf-fishing stretches for working bucktails, jigs and stickbaits". The best window is "the last two hours of the pushing tide and first hour of high", and lure action is most reliable "from late Spring through autumn" (Kegan Mattheys, Sep 2025). South-easterly onshore wind and coloured water bring "perfect Kob conditions" (Jacita Oct 2025). Sealine anglers give Sept to March as the season, mostly at night. "Macs has been very good to me lately with kob and elf" (Sealine 2019).

species.size: Not stated for Macassar. The District Mail (2022) says most False Bay steenbras are under-sized.
species.bait: Bloodworm, moonshine and wonderworm, mixed-grill baits
species.notes: The City lists white steenbras among the anglers' targets. Jacita (May and June 2025) reports steenbras active at Macassar on high tide, with "Bloodworm and mixed grill baits" working best. Sealine (2007) has steenbras around "all week, but on bloodworm only".

species.size: Not stated
species.bait: Worms and mixed-grill baits
species.notes: The City lists blacktail among Macassar anglers' targets. Jacita (16 May 2025) says "steenbras, galjoen, and kolstert are active" at Macassar, especially on high tide. Sealine (2020) lists "kolstert" among Macassar species.

name: Strand beachfront
aka: Strand beachfront (east of the Lourens River)
area: Strand, north-eastern False Bay (Helderberg)
coord_source: The pin does not land on the named place. An OSM reverse geocode puts it in Helderzicht, Somerset West, with the nearest feature (Beach Road at -34.1001, 18.8151) about 400 m east, and it is about 550 m west of waterinfo's mouth estimate. So it sits at or inside the no-take Helderberg MPA, and a pag
bottom: A sandy beach broken by rocky reefs and gullies (the 'Strand reefs', with foul ground that snags lures). It runs from Melkbaai towards Harmony Park.
mouth: This is a sea spot, not an estuary. The Lourens River lagoon next to it sits behind a beach bar, and waterinfo.co.za says "Occasionally, during the dry summer season, the lagoon is closed or has only a small outflow to the sea". Nobody manages the mouth artificially according to the sources. The mouth matters as the Helderberg MPA boundary, not as a fishing feature.
permit: Strand closed area (Lourens River to Gordon's Bay): shore angling is the only fishing allowed, no bait collecting or cast nets. No fishing within 100 m of a signed bathing area; a 2009 local report says daytime fishing is not allowed on the main beach in season, so check the signs. The Lourens River lagoon behind the bar is closed to fishing (tidal lagoon rule), and west of the mouth is the Helderberg MPA. You need a DFFE recreational angling permit (marine). The stretch from the Lourens mouth to Gordon's Bay is for shore angling only, so no boat fishing and probably no other gear. Collecting bait off the Strand reefs was called a "big NO NO" on Sealine; only washed-up redbait may be picked up. Galjoen are closed from 15 Oct to the end of Feb (District Mail Dec 2022), and elf were out of season in October (Jacita, Oct 2025). The kob minimum is given as 60 cm in a Sep 2025 column and "around 50 cm" in a Feb 2026 column, so check the current DFFE limits.
legality: Fishing is allowed from the shore. The Helderberg MPA is wholly no-take ("no fishing, harvesting of invertebrates or seaweeds, or bait collection of any kind") and runs from the Eerste River mouth east to "a line at 180° true from the mouth of the Lourens River", 500 m seaward (Wikipedia; District Mail Aug 2025 p=267430). The Strand beachfront south-east of the Lourens mouth is outside it. From the Lourens mouth to the eastern breakwater of Gordon's Bay harbour, "Only shore angling (and no other type of fishing) is allowed" (the Marine Recreational Activity brochure, quoted on Sealine 2012 and on waterinfo.co.za). The City of Cape Town's Strand Beach page lists "Fishing" as an activity. Checked: Wikipedia's Helderberg MPA page, waterinfo.co.za, the City beach page, District Mail p=267430 and the Sealine winter thread.
description: This is a sandy False Bay beach broken by shallow reefs along Beach Road, Strand. Local columnist Kegan Mattheys (Fishing Republic, Strand) calls it "your most productive but also more difficult" kob area and writes that "In areas like Strand we tend to fish very light" for garrick: a 7 ft rod, 4000 reel and 20 lb braid, with plugs, spoons and paddle-tails. Sean Mills' fly blog lists leerfish, elf, kob, mullet, maasbanker and white steenbras for the Strand and Gordon's Bay beaches, "Best fished in a south easter, the gullies in the rocks can be fished at low tide and the beach at high tide". Rock-and-surf anglers also take bronze whalers, raggies, spotted gully sharks, hound sharks, and blue and eagle rays here on heavy bait tackle (District Mail, Dec 2022).
hazards: The Helderberg MPA (no-take) starts at the Lourens River mouth, immediately west; do not fish or collect bait west of the mouth
Wading the reefs alone, especially on a neap tide; Sealine advises 'safety first' and staying on the shore when alone
Surge on the reefs; fish feed harder 'once standing on the reefs becomes uncomfortable' (District Mail 2025)
Foul reef ground snags lures, so weedless paddle-tails are advised
Swimmers, surfers and lifeguard bathing areas in summer; the Mosterd's Bay section was closed 15 Dec to 15 Jan in 2025/26
Bait collecting off the Strand reefs is reportedly not allowed
access_notes: The beach is along Beach Road, Strand. The City of Cape Town says there is parking for about 1,000 vehicles, plus a boat launch and slipway. No car-park coordinates were confirmed. The beach is on Beach Road, Strand, with large City parking (about 1,000 bays), lifeguards, a tidal pool and a slipway. The Mosterd's Bay section was "temporarily closed from 15 December 2025 - 15 January 2026" (City of Cape Town). Sealine posters call the Strand "quite productive in the right conditions, and fairly safe" and "Strand and Melkbos probably your safest spots at night" (2020). A 2022 District Mail column says "it's safe to say its a better bet to fish in Strand than it would be at Macassar, Monwabisi or Strandfontein". The Fishing Republic tackle shop is at 73 Beach Road. Melkbaai can get crowded. The estimated drive (OSRM free-flow, 29 Oct 2026) is about 43 min from Westlake and 38 min from Green Point. The Mission fly magazine puts the eastern False Bay reefs "about a 25 minute drive from the Cape Metropol". Stay south-east of the Lourens River mouth: west of it is the no-take Helderberg MPA.
unverified: Where exactly the stand and the Lourens River mouth are: the pin (-34.0994, 18.8108) may sit on or just west of the Helderberg MPA's eastern boundary line
A 2009 blog says 'fishing is not allowed during the day' on Strand Beach. It may be an old bathing-area bylaw; the City page lists Fishing with no hours. Check signs at the beach.

Quotes the finders attributed to Sealine threads 93538 and 56615 ('Try Melkbaai in the Strand for leeries', 'if the Garrick/Elf are around in Strand/Gordons bay then a spoon works like a bomb') were not found in the cache
Yellowtail from the Strand shore: only a tourism page (capetourism) and a general shore-target mention; no Strand shore catch report
Whether the Strand pier itself may be fished: no angling page mentions it
Exact closed-season dates for elf (only 'out of season' in October is sourced) and the current kob minimum size (60 cm vs about 50 cm in different columns)
The Mission's '25 minute drive' covers the eastern False Bay reefs in general, not Strand specifically

issues: COORDINATES (the main problem): an OSM Nominatim reverse geocode of the pin (-34.0994, 18.8108), fetched 2 Nov 2026, snaps to 'Beach Road, Helderzicht, ... Somerset West' at -34.1001, 18.8151. That is about 400 m east of the pin, and the pin is in Somerset West, not Strand. waterinfo.co.za's coarse fix for the Lourens mouth (about 18.817) is also about 550 m east of the pin. So the pin sits at or west of the Lourens River mouth, which is on or inside the no-take Helderberg MPA (Eerste mouth to the 180-degree line from the Lourens mouth). Published as it is, the pin would mark a no-take zone as a legal fishing spot. It must be moved at least 1 km south-east along the Strand beachfront before publishing.

LEGALITY at the named place holds, but the record leaves out the actual regulation. acts.co.za (MLRA reg 10(f)(v), cached) lists the 500 m strip from 'the security fence next to the Lourens River, Strand' (northern limit at 225 degrees true) to the Gordon's Bay eastern breakwater light as a closed area 'except on the authority of a permit'. The Marine Recreational Activity brochure (quoted in Sealine thread 65296 and in the cached search summary) says 'Only shore angling (and no other type of fishing) is allowed' there. So shore angling with a DFFE recreational permit is correct, and the legality text should cite reg 10(f)(v). Note that this line is drawn at 225 degrees from a security fence, not at 180 degrees from the mouth like the MPA line, so stay well clear of the mouth.

The Lourens River lagoon itself: the cached acts.co.za summary shows reg 10(a), 'engage in fishing or collecting any fish in a tidal river or lagoon', as a closed-area clause. Treat the lagoon behind the bar as off-limits; the record only covers it as an MPA boundary.

Daytime restriction not resolved: helderbergbasin (2009) says 'fishing is not allowed during the day' along Strand Beach. The record lists this as unverified, but an hour-by-hour rater needs it settled. It may be a City bathing-area or lifeguard-hours rule. Until it is confirmed, the page should warn against daytime fishing in the lifeguarded bathing areas in season.

Light-tackle evidence is real but mostly about garrick. District Mail p=83436 (Oct 2023): 'In areas like Strand we tend to fish very light' (7 ft rod, 4000 reel, 20 lb braid) is about garrick. Sealine 65296 has leerie spinning from the cement block at Blakes. For kob, the same column advises an 11 ft rod and 30-50 lb braid on rocks, and Angler 2020 says paddle-tails are used by 'rock and surf guys' off the Strand reefs. Kob spinning here is medium-to-heavy rather than light, and the record should say so.

Several cited sources are not in the cached evidence file, which was capped at 90 KB: the capeflyfishing blog (Sean Mills), District Mail p=54504, p=89064, p=63697, the full text of p=65894, the City Strand beach page, waterinfo.co.za, Wikipedia's Helderberg MPA page and Jacita July 2025. Claims that rest only on them are unverified here, not refuted. These are maasbanker, mullet as a target, fly methods for elf and garrick, shore geelbek, the City's 'Fishing' activity listing, the 1,000 parking bays and the Mosterd's Bay closure.

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: Moonshine worm and Wonderworm (Jacita, June and July 2025).
species.notes: Jacita (July 2025): belman may show in the Strand area on a calmer day with lighter wind and a smaller swell. Kegan Mattheys (Sep 2022) calls the Strand a 'belman hot spot', although 2022 was 'an extremely poor year'.

species.size: 'Plentiful and fat' (Sealine, June 2012).
species.bait: Redbait (stinkmossel), white mussel and prawn. Only use bait you bought or that washed up, because collecting off the reefs is not allowed.
species.notes: Reef fish are fished 'left of the swimming pool' at Blakes and around Melkbaai by day.

species.size: Mostly small elf on 4/0 hooks, with 'bigger blue elf' some seasons.
species.bait: Chokka, sardine and strepie fillet. A 4/0 hook suits smaller elf, and 6/0-8/0 when the 'bigger blue elf' are around (District Mail columns). Spoons and plugs are used when spinning, and flies too.
species.notes: 'In season Shad (Elf) during the evenings' (helderbergbasin 2009). 'A few of the kob bakkies in Strand have caught kob and elf in the evening' (Sep 2022). Jacita (Oct 2025) notes elf are out of season in October; the closed season covers Oct-Nov.

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: Small flies or ultra-light bait. They are also netted or caught as live bait for kob.
species.notes: Listed for the Strand and Gordon's Bay beaches by Sean Mills. Kegan Mattheys describes mullet as the baitfish garrick and kob feed on.

species.size: Mostly school fish off the reefs. 'Beautiful size winter kob of up to 15 kg' were reported at Strand in Sep 2022. Legal minimum 60 cm (Sep 2025 column) or about 50 cm (Feb 2026 column); check DFFE.
species.bait: Lures: paddle-tails, spoons, bucktails, stickbaits and slow-pitch jigs fished 'low and slow' near the bottom (Kegan Mattheys, Sep 2025). Rock-and-surf anglers use paddle-tails 'quite successfully' off the Strand reefs (Angler, 2020). Bait: chokka, sardine, mullet or fresh fish on a 6/0-10/0 hook with flotation and a red running float, or 4/0-6/0 hooks with high-density foam or a dingle dangle rig.
species.notes: The Sep 2025 column calls Strand 'your most productive but also more difficult' kob area because of rugged reefs. It says 'The last two hours of the pushing tide and first hour of high are prime feeding windows', and to work the reefs on low tide. Jacita (Oct 2025): with south-easterly onshore winds, 'Try your luck along Macassar Beach or the Strand reefs - both are known to fire'. Catches rose after 'a lot of colour and a strong easterly wind' (2022). Kob are often caught in the evening or at night (helderbergbasin 2009; Kobtober column 2022).

species.size: Not stated for Strand.
species.bait: White chisel-nose and needle-nose plugs, spoons, paddle-tail and fluke soft plastics, bucktails, topwater lures (Rapala pencil 107, Skitter V, Skitter Walk) and 20-30 g slow-pitch jigs. At Strand: a 7 ft medium-heavy spinning rod, 4000 reel and 20 lb braid. Leeries are spun 'from the cement block at Blakes' (Sealine 2012). Streamer flies are used for leerfish on the Strand beaches (Sean Mills).
species.notes: Kegan Mattheys (Oct 2023): 'In areas like Strand we tend to fish very light for these fish', because long casts are not needed. The spinning season starts as the south-easter returns towards summer. The Sealine Blakes mention is from a June thread.

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: Small baits or flies at night.
species.notes: Sean Mills: night fishing at the Pavilion targets maasbanker.

species.size: Mostly undersized in False Bay ('few mature fish', District Mail 2022). Minimum size is 60 cm.
species.bait: Worms (Moonshine worm, Wonderworm) and prawn.
species.notes: Named for the Strand beach by Sean Mills and helderbergbasin (evenings). Jacita (June 2025) reports white steenbras in the Strand area in flat surf of 0.8-1.2 m.

species.size: 'Small and scarce' at Strand (Sealine 2012).
species.bait: Redbait, white mussel, prawn and worms (galjoen baits in general, District Mail 2022).
species.notes: Closed season runs from 15 Oct to the end of Feb (District Mail Dec 2022).

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: Fish baits (sardine, maasbanker, mackerel) and chokka. Flies on the eastern False Bay reefs (The Mission).
species.notes: Named as an edible species caught at Strand (District Mail Dec 2022). Months come from a boat-fishing article. The Mission says the eastern False Bay reefs are 'traditionally known' for Cape salmon but does not name Strand.

species.size: Not stated.
species.bait: Not stated.
species.notes: Listed among the species anglers target at night along the Strand beach (helderbergbasin 2009).

name: Harmony Park reefs (Strand)
area: Strand / Gordon's Bay (north-east False Bay)
coord_source: Nominatim (OpenStreetMap) query run 30 Oct 2026. The stand is the "Harmony Park Tidal Pool" node (-34.1396321, 18.8457002, Dolphin Street, Southfork), on the reef edge in front of the resort. The access point is the "Harmony Park Resort" node (-34.1415523, 18.8487406), which matches the merge coordinates. No source gives the exact point on the reef where anglers wade out.

access.note: Harmony Park Resort (City of Cape Town), corner of Jan Bruin and Gordon's Bay roads on the R44 between Strand and Gordon's Bay. Day visits are capped at 250 visitors. Nominatim resort node.

bottom: Shallow, rough rocky reef shelves that anglers wade out onto, next to the Strand sand beaches. Snags are heavy ("the reefs are nasty", Sealine).
permit: Strand closed area (Lourens River to Gordon's Bay): shore angling is the only fishing allowed, no bait collecting or cast nets. You need a DFFE marine recreational angling permit. This stretch is shore angling only: no boat fishing, spearfishing or other fishing within 500 m of shore between the Lourens River mouth and the Gordon's Bay eastern breakwater. Galjoen are closed from 15 October to the end of February. Dusky kob have a 60 cm minimum size and a strict daily bag (Mattheys 2025). If you go in through the resort, City of Cape Town resort entry rules and tariffs also apply.
legality: Fishing is allowed from the shore only. Harmony Park is east of the Lourens River mouth, so it is outside the Helderberg MPA no-take zone, which runs from the Eerste River mouth to the Lourens River mouth (City of Cape Town and Wikipedia via cached search results; the task's own legality reference agrees). Between the Lourens River mouth and the eastern breakwater of Gordon's Bay harbour, "only shore angling (and no other type of fishing) is allowed ... extending 500 m seawards". This is the MLRA closed-areas rule (R1111), quoted in the DFFE recreational fishing brochure and on Sealine. The City's Harmony Park Resort page lists "Fishing" as an activity. I did not re-open the R1111 text itself; it comes from cached search summaries and the 2012 Sealine quote.
description: Shallow rocky reefs in front of the City's Harmony Park Resort and tidal pool, between Strand and Gordon's Bay. A Sealine angler says you "can wade the reefs at harmony park which is very productive" but warns to "be kitted correctly and get someone experienced to show you the ropes or it can be very dangerous on the reefs". On the wider Strand reef stretch, anglers spin light for elf and kob ("In areas like Strand we tend to fish very light", Kegan Mattheys) and use small-hook reef baits for blacktail and galjoen.
hazards: Wading out onto the reefs: 'it can be very dangerous on the reefs' (Sealine, 2007). Anglers wade deep on low water and 'let pushing tide push you back to shore' (Sealine, 2012), so the rising tide can cut you off
Surge and swell break over the reef shelves (Mattheys: fish feed harder once standing on the reefs becomes uncomfortable in the surge)
Heavy tackle loss on the reefs: 'take plenty of tackle ... the reefs are nasty'
Fishing alone or at night: 'safety first so if you fishing alone rather from the shore only' (Sealine, 2012)
Galjoen closed season, 15 Oct to end Feb, and kob size and bag limits
Do not fish west of the Lourens River mouth: from there to the Eerste River is the Helderberg MPA no-take zone
access_notes: The City of Cape Town page gives the resort address as 'Cnr Jan Bruin and Gordon's Bay roads, Gordon's Bay'. It lists 'Fishing' and a 'Tidal pool' among activities, has seasonal opening periods, and caps day visitors at 250. The page states no hours, fees or parking details. You can also reach the tidal pool from Dolphin Street, Southfork (OSM). A local tackle shop in Gordon's Bay harbour is mentioned on Sealine. Bait: you may pick up red bait that has washed out (Sealine, 2012); collecting live bait off these reefs is probably not allowed in this shore-angling-only zone. The OSRM free-flow estimate is about 46 to 52 min from Green Point or Westlake.
unverified: Only one angling page names Harmony Park, a 2007 Sealine post. The species list is built from sources on the Strand reefs generally, not Harmony Park by name
The merge note's 'slippery pool-side jetty' and 'productive for galjoen and kob' at Harmony Park itself: not found in any page that was opened
Exact stand position on the reef; the tidal pool node is used as a proxy
Typical sizes for elf, blacktail and galjoen at this spot
Resort day-visit fee, gate hours and parking, and whether the reefs can be reached from public land outside resort hours
Whether collecting bait off these reefs is prohibited under the shore-angling-only rule; only the 2012 forum post says washed-out red bait may be picked up
The R1111 closed-area wording was not re-read from the regulation itself; it comes from cached search summaries of the DFFE brochure and a 2012 Sealine quote
Facing bearing (about 230 degrees) and 'semi' shelter are estimates from the coastline's orientation, not from a source
City of Cape Town Resort Brochure PDF was unreachable on 29 Oct 2026 (ECONNREFUSED), not checked

issues: Legality holds. The Helderberg MPA no-take zone runs from the Eerste mouth (Wikipedia: -34.0812, 18.7648) to the Lourens mouth at Strand. Harmony Park (-34.1396, 18.8457) is about 3.7 km south-east of Strand (Wikipedia: -34.1167, 18.8167), so it is east of the Lourens mouth and outside the MPA. Two cached search summaries (estuary.jsonl n=2 and n=31) quote the 2024 DFFE permit brochure and the 2014/15 SANParks brochure: 'only shore angling (and no other type of fishing) is allowed between the mouth of the Lourens River, and the eastern breakwater of the harbour at Gordon's Bay, extending 500 m seawards'. The R1111 regulation text itself was not opened, by the record's author or by me.

The City of Cape Town Harmony Park Resort page, re-fetched 2 Nov 2026, confirms 'Fishing' among its activities, a 'Tidal pool' among its facilities, and the address 'Cnr Jan Bruin and Gordon's Bay roads, Gordon's Bay'. It has no rules on fishing or bait and no fees or hours. The '250 day visitors ... at 50% maximum capacity' line reads like a leftover COVID-era cap and may be stale, so it should not be stated as a current rule.

Only one angling source names Harmony Park: Sealine thread 2243, a post by Mantis on 25 Sep 2007. I re-fetched it. It is 19-year-old, second-hand advice in a thread about the Harbour Island pier and wall: 'if you go to the right you can wade the reefs at harmony park which is very productive' and 'a few shad get taken on spoon in that area'. It fits light tackle (spoons), so evidence is not refuted, but it is thin.

In the same post, galjoen are placed on the OTHER side: 'if you go to the left you need to fish for gallies on a rough sea', with Harmony Park 'to the right'. The record's galjoen notes cite thread 2243 as covering 'the Strand reefs and the Gordon's Bay wall area'. In fact the thread puts galjoen at the Harbour Island wall and to the left, not at Harmony Park.

Blacktail rests only on Sealine thread 65296 ('winter fishing strand', 2012). That thread is not in the cached evidence, which suggests it never mentions Harmony Park, and the record admits it covers the Strand reefs generally. The quotes 'plentiful and fat', 'let pushing tide push you back to shore' and 'if you fishing alone rather from the shore only' could not be checked against the evidence.

Elf: abundance 'regular' overstates the only Harmony-Park source, which says 'a few shad get taken on spoon in that area'. 'Your quota of shad in a few minutes when conditions are right' is about 'the strand reefs' in general and depends on conditions ('the strand works best in howling south east winds'). 'occasional' fits better. The size note ('good-sized ones caught in Strand', late Sep 2022) cites novanews p=65894, which is not in the evidence and was not checked. The Sep to Apr months come from a kayak-fishing guide snippet (cached search summary), not a shore source.

species.size: No size given for Harmony Park. Mattheys reported 'good-sized ones caught in Strand' in late September 2022
species.bait: Spoons; also plugs and soft-plastic paddle tails on light spinning gear
species.notes: In the Harmony Park post, Mantis says 'a few shad get taken on spoon in that area' and 'spinning off the strand reefs will see your quota of shad in a few minutes when conditions are right'. The season (Sep to Apr) comes from a cached kayak-fishing guide snippet for the Strand area.

species.size: Many reef fish are undersize. The legal minimum is 60 cm. Bigger fish turn up in winter on bait
species.bait: Lures: stickbaits, paddle tails, bucktails and spoons fished 'low and slow' near the bottom. Bait: live mullet or maasbanker, or chokka and sardine, on circle hooks
species.notes: Mattheys calls the Strand reefs 'your most productive but also more difficult' area for kob. Fish are around all year, with the best lure action 'from late Spring through autumn'. He suggests a 7 ft medium-heavy rod, a 4000 reel and 20 lb braid for Strand. 'The last two hours of the pushing tide and first hour of high are prime feeding windows.' These sources describe the Strand reefs generally, not Harmony Park by name.

name: Gordon's Bay harbour
aka: Bikini Beach (adjacent, south of the wall)
area: Gordon's Bay, north-east False Bay (Helderberg)
coord_source: Nominatim 'Gordon's Bay Harbour' (leisure=marina, Beach Road), -34.1641251, 18.8590065, run 30 Oct 2026. This point is in the harbour basin, not on a measured breakwater stand, so the wall stand is assumed to be within about 200 m. Fishbrain's 'Gordon's Bay' water point (-34.1588, 18.8648) lies offshore of Main Beach. The merge step's rough point was -34.164, 18.86, which agrees.

access.note: Harbour area off Beach Road. The City lists parking at Bikini Beach, which is next to the harbour, but no separate car park coordinate was found, so this repeats the Nominatim harbour point.

bottom: A rock breakwater over sand, with reef and weed patches in the area (inferred). Angler Publications says kob here feed 'over sand and on the edge of reefs and gullies' and chokka over weed bottoms. Neither statement is specific to the wall.
permit: The harbour belongs to the Department of Public Works and Infrastructure; no official statement on angling from the walls was found, although anglers have fished them for decades. Follow the harbour master's signs and keep clear of working boats. The end of the eastern breakwater is the southern limit of the Strand closed area, where shore angling is the only fishing allowed. DFFE recreational angling permit (sold at Post Offices). Chokka (squid) needs its own permit, on the same form as the angling permit (Angler Publications). Bag and size limits apply: silver kob 1 per angler per day, minimum about 50 cm (District Mail, 2026); geelbek 2 per day. In the Strand to Gordon's Bay 500 m zone only shore angling is allowed, so no fishing from boats or kayaks there.
legality: Fishing is allowed with a permit. The Helderberg MPA (no-take) runs only from the Eerste River mouth to the Lourens River mouth in Strand, so Gordon's Bay harbour lies outside it, about 5 km south-east. MLRA Regulation 10 (Acts Online, closed areas, item (f)(v)) sets a 500 m zone from Strand to Gordon's Bay whose limit is "the eastern breakwater of the fishing harbour at Gordon's Bay". The Marine Recreational Activity Information Brochure, as quoted on Sealine in June 2012, says: "Only shore angling (and no other type of fishing) is allowed between the mouth of the Lourens River ... and the eastern breakwater of the harbour at Gordon's Bay, extending 500 m seawards." Shore angling from the wall is therefore permitted under the zoning. I found no harbour-master, Navy or City rule that bans fishing from the wall, but I did not confirm that none exists.
description: The old harbour at Gordon's Bay in the north-east corner of False Bay. Local sources say fishing "from the rocks and the old Harbour Wall is a popular pastime" (sahistory). A Sealine angler calls it "mostly casual style fishing but can get everything from kob/stumpnose/hottie/blacktail" on light baits such as redbait and prawn. Bikini Beach, a Blue Flag swimming beach, lies just south of the harbour wall, and no source describes fishing from the beach itself.
hazards: Swell reaches the outside of the wall: the City's Bikini Beach page says surfers ride a left-hander 'off the harbour wall', so the wall can be wave-washed and slippery in a big south-westerly swell
Boat traffic and launching in a working harbour (yacht club, local fishing fleet, NSRI Station 9 sea rescue)
Swimmers and surfers right next to the wall at Bikini Beach (Blue Flag, lifeguards December to March), with summer crowds
SA Navy officer training facility next to the old harbour; keep out of naval areas
Personal safety: a Sealine poster advises 'safety first' and shore-only fishing when alone
access_notes: The harbour is on Beach Road, Gordon's Bay, and the City lists parking at the adjacent Bikini Beach. The wall is a short walk from there, with no gate fee known. The harbour houses the Gordon's Bay Yacht Club, a local fishing fleet, an SA Navy officer training facility and NSRI Station 9, so keep clear of the slipway, moored boats and naval areas. Bikini Beach has lifeguards during the Blue Flag season (December to March) and is busy in summer. The old GB Tackle shop in the harbour 'closed down a while ago' (Sealine, 2012), so bring your own bait. I found no posted hours or harbour-master rules for fishing.
unverified: Whether the harbour authority (proclaimed fishing harbour) or the SA Navy restricts fishing from any part of the wall or breakwater. No rule was found either way.

Whether City beach by-laws stop fishing at Bikini Beach during bathing hours or season. A 2009 Helderberg blog says fishing is not allowed in daytime on Strand Beach, but nothing says the same for Bikini Beach.
Whether the 2012 brochure wording (shore angling only, Lourens River to the Gordon's Bay eastern breakwater) is still the current regulation text.
Facing bearing of 260 degrees, estimated from the coast's geometry rather than measured.
Depth (medium) and bottom at the wall.
Tide preference: no source gives one for the harbour, so 'any' is a placeholder.
Light-lure fishing (paddle-tails, dropshot, spoons) and squid jigging from the wall. No source mentions either at this spot. Chokka are reported for Gordon's Bay only from boats.
Exact stand coordinates on the breakwater. The Nominatim point is the harbour or marina.
Typical sizes for hottentot, blacktail and stumpnose here.
Bikini Beach as a fishing stand. No angling source describes fishing from the beach, so it is listed only as an adjacent landmark.

Galjoen, musselcracker and Roman or santer seabream. A promotional guide mentions galjoen and cracker for Gordon's Bay rocks, and Fishbrain lists Roman and santer area-wide, likely from boats. They are left out of the species list.

issues: Legality holds. The harbour is outside the Helderberg MPA, which ends at the Lourens River mouth (City of Cape Town search summary; Wikipedia Helderberg MPA in the cached search). The record's quotes from Acts Online Regulation 10(f)(v) are accurate: the closed 500 m strip runs from the security fence at the Lourens River to a 320-degree true line from the navigation light at the end of the eastern breakwater of the Gordon's Bay fishing harbour. That regulation's lead-in reads 'No person shall, except on the authority of a permit'. The only text saying shore angling is allowed in that strip is the 2012 brochure as quoted in the Sealine thread, a forum quote 14 years old. A later search summary repeats the same wording from a 2014/2015 SANParks marine brochure (sanparks.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/04/marine_rec_brochure.pdf), which slightly strengthens it. Neither is a current DFFE text.

The claim that the harbour is 'about 5 km south-east' of the Lourens River mouth has no source in the evidence. Strand's beachfront alone covers most of that stretch, and my own estimate (not sourced) puts the mouth about 7 to 8 km from the harbour. It should be reworded rather than stated as a measurement.

The kob bag limit may be wrong. The record gives '1 per angler per day, about 50 cm' from the District Mail (Feb 2026), which itself hedges with 'about one fish' and 'around 50 cm'. A cached search summary (sealine/Cape Town shore-spots query) gives 1 per day and 60 cm as the rule for shore and estuary catches EAST of Cape Agulhas. That implies a different limit west of Agulhas, where Gordon's Bay is. Check the current DFFE brochure before publishing a figure.

The species name 'Silver kob (Japanese meagre)' mixes up two species. Japanese meagre is Argyrosomus japonicus, the dusky kob, not silver kob (A. inodorus). Fishbrain's area list says 'Japanese meagre'. Angler Publications (a boat article) says silver kob. The only shore source, Sealine's flippy, says just 'kob'.

Steentjie does not appear anywhere in the cached evidence. Grep finds no 'steentjie', and no Fishbrain catch list for the Gordon's Bay water (rttJK-BA) was fetched. The detail '10 in (about 25 cm), 6 oz' cannot be checked and looks invented or carried over from elsewhere.

Several hazard and access facts do not appear in the cached evidence: the City's Bikini Beach page quote about a left-hander 'off the harbour wall', parking at Bikini Beach, lifeguards from December to March, and the Fishbrain water point -34.1588, 18.8648. The City page and the Fishbrain page show up only as search-result links. These may have come from the writer's own fetches, but they cannot be confirmed from the cache. Blue Flag status, the yacht club, the fishing fleet, the SA Navy training facility and NSRI Station 9 are all supported by the search summaries.
