name: Milnerton beach
aka: Sunset Beach wreck (the wreck behind the Milnerton golf course)
area: Milnerton
coord_source: Nominatim "Milnerton Lighthouse" fetched 2026-10-30: -33.8817080, 18.4877808, class man_made, type lighthouse, "Loxton Road, Woodbridge Island, Milnerton". Matches the merge-step coordinates and the mondo.surf Milnerton surf-spot coordinates (-33.881217, 18.485983) seen in a cached search result. The stand is the beach immediately seaward of the lighthouse; the wreck stand is further north behind the golf course (not separately geocoded).

access.note: Milnerton Beach car park area at Lagoon Beach Drive (City of Cape Town facility page: 'ample' parking, toilets; Nominatim 'Lagoon Beach' -33.8927919, 18.4823750). The lighthouse stand is about 1.3 km north along the sand, or by road to Loxton Road on Woodbridge Island where the lighthouse stands; parking at the lighthouse end is not confirmed by any source.

bottom: Sand surf beach with low reef patches near the lighthouse ("the reef at Milnerton", sealine 2017) and a wreck off the golf course to the north.
mouth: Not an estuary stand, but the Diep River / Milnerton Lagoon mouth lies just south of Woodbridge Island and is managed by the City of Cape Town: a sealine poster says "the City closed the mouth and the water was stagnant for about 3 to 5 months", and a flytalk post says the mouth "is and has been open for a few years"; no current statement found. Effluent from the lagoon (Potsdam wastewater works) affects the beach water near the mouth.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine, sold at Post Offices) for rod-and-line fishing; the same permit system covers bait collection (sand prawn pumping, white mussel), and the lagoon has posted bait-collecting times and permit boards (sealine 2007). National MLRA species rules apply: galjoen closed 15 October to end February (a sealine poster notes "the galjoen season would be closed in December"), bag 2, min 35 cm; elf closed 1 October to 30 November, bag 4, min 30 cm; white steenbras bag 1, min 60 cm; kob bag 1, min 60 cm. The species limits are standard national regulations from general knowledge, not from the spot pages.
legality: Fishing allowed. The stand (lat -33.8817, lon 18.4878) is on the Table Bay coast north-east of Table Bay harbour, outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, whose northern limit is Mouille Point (2004 regulations as summarised in the task brief), and outside the Robben Island MPA, which surrounds the island only (merge note: the island MPA's eastern limit is about E18 24.06', the mainland here is at about E18 29'). No restricted (no-take) zone applies. It is a City of Cape Town public beach whose facility page states no fishing restriction. The adjacent Milnerton Lagoon falls under the City's Table Bay Nature Reserve with posted bait-collecting regulations (sealine 2007), but the sea beach itself is not in the reserve's fishing-restricted waters as far as the sources show. A DFFE (Marine Living Resources Act) recreational angling permit is required for shore angling and for collecting bait.
description: Open Table Bay surf beach on the Milnerton and Woodbridge Island stretch, with the lighthouse and a wreck behind the golf course as the landmarks anglers name. Sealine posters recommend "the areas near the Milnerton Lighthouse" for galjoen, kob, hottentot and "sometimes steenbras" on white mussel, worm, pilchard, mullet or freshly pumped sand prawn, one reported a single galjoen "at the wreck found behind the Milnerton golf course" on a bad-weather day, and a fishing aggregator says the beaches from Milnerton to Bloubergstrand produce kob, elf and winter galjoen. The sources describe surf rods and bait rather than lures, so treat it as a light-bait beach with elf and kob as the lure possibilities, and expect discoloured water near the lagoon mouth after sewage spills.
hazards: Water quality: sewage and poorly treated effluent from the Diep River and Milnerton Lagoon (Potsdam WWTW), with fish kills reported in December 2019 and March 2022 and E. coli warnings; posters describe the lagoon water as 'uninviting and possibly polluted' and anglers reject lagoon harders because they 'come from dirty water'.
Personal safety: 'I wouldn't venture to secluded spots after dark' (sealine 2014); the stretch north towards Melkbos 'is not always the safest spot' (sealine 2016).
Open Atlantic surf and cold Benguela water; lifeguards only in designated areas (City of Cape Town).
Kitesurfers and surfers use the river mouth and the wreck (kitekahunas listing for Milnerton River Mouth; mondo.surf lists Milnerton as a surf spot).
Dogs run off lead on the beach (City of Cape Town), a nuisance for bait left on the sand.
Shy sharks and gully sharks take baits here (sealine 2014); a 2014 poster worried about a 50 kg-plus shark on a light rod.
access_notes: City of Cape Town lists Milnerton Beach at Lagoon Beach Drive, Milnerton, with "ample" parking, toilets, "lifeguards on duty within designated areas" (no hours or season given), dogs "allowed to run freely", "generally safe for swimming", no fees or opening hours stated and no fishing rule mentioned. The lighthouse is on Loxton Road, Woodbridge Island (Nominatim). The wreck behind the Milnerton golf course is fished from Sunset Beach further north (sealine, 2016). Bait: locals pump sand prawn in the adjacent Milnerton Lagoon, "the main bait source for the area", and cast-net harders there, but the lagoon has boards "with all the regulations for bait collecting, and times and permits" and its water is often dirty (sealine 2007, 2014, 2018). Safety: "I wouldn't venture to secluded spots after dark" (sealine, 2014); the stretch north towards Melkbos "is not always the safest spot" (sealine, 2016). Drive: no source gives a time; OSRM free-flow from the merge step (2026-10-29) puts it at about 13 min from Green Point and 29 min from Westlake.
unverified: Light-tackle (lure or fly) fishing at Milnerton beach: no source documents it; the sealine advice is an 11 ft scratch rod for reef fish and a 14 ft medium rod for kob and steenbras, all with bait. The 2018 sealine thread 'Light tackle spots in blouberg?' and the 2017 'Yellowtail in Milnerton/Blouberg' thread (fetched 2026-10-30) do not mention Milnerton catches at all; the yellowtail sighting was off Dolphin Beach Hotel, unconfirmed, with no shore catches.
Tide preference: no source states a best tide stage for this beach, so tide_pref is left unset.
Best months for kob, elf, hottentot and white steenbras here: not stated; only galjoen is tied to a season ('winter galjoen', fishingreminder).
Typical sizes: not stated by any source for this spot.
Parking at the lighthouse end (Loxton Road, Woodbridge Island): not confirmed; the City lists ample parking at Lagoon Beach Drive.
Lifeguard hours and season, beach opening hours and fees: not stated on the City page.
Whether the Milnerton Lagoon mouth is currently open: posters from 2014 and 2015 say the City closed it once and that it has since been open for years; no current statement found.

The reef and wreck as bottom features come from a 2013 boat-oriented post ('the reef at Milnerton', within 1 nm) and a 2016 shore report; their exact positions relative to the lighthouse are not sourced.
The fishingreminder blurb covers the Milnerton to Bloubergstrand beaches as a stretch, not Milnerton beach specifically, and the site is an aggregator.

Leervis, stumpnose, harders and sand shark are reported only for the adjacent Milnerton Lagoon and Woodbridge Island estuary side (sealine 2007, 2010, 2014; flytalk), mostly as 1960s to 1980s memories, so they are kept out of the beach species list.
Facing bearing (280) and shelter (semi) are derived from the coastline orientation and Table Bay's partial protection from south-west swell, not from an angling source.

issues: Legality holds. The stand is on the Table Bay mainland coast, north-east of Mouille Point (the TMNP MPA's northern limit) and well east of the Robben Island MPA, so no restricted (no-take) zone applies. Wikipedia's Table Bay Nature Reserve page (fetched 2026-11-02) names its parts as Rietvlei Wetland Reserve, Diep River Fynbos Corridor, Zoarvlei Wetlands, Milnerton Racecourse Nature Reserve and Milnerton Lagoon. It does not name Woodbridge Island, the Milnerton beach or the lighthouse. The lagoon side of the Woodbridge Island strip is reserve water, though, and the legality text should say to fish the seaward beach, not the lagoon edge. No official City page in the cache states a fishing rule either way. The City facility-page details the record quotes (ample parking, toilets, dogs off lead) are not in the cached evidence and were not checked.

Evidence for the spot is thin, and none of it is light tackle. The only angling source in the cache that names the beach is one sentence from kaspaas (sealine, 16 May 2014): 'You can try the areas near the Milnerton Lighthouse'. That is a suggestion, not a catch report. The tackle he gives is an 11 ft scratch rod and SL30 for galjoen and hottentot, which counts as light bait fishing, and a 14 ft medium surf rod with a Daiwa 40 or Shimano 30 for kob and steenbras, which is ordinary surf gear. No source documents lure or fly fishing at Milnerton beach.

The M@rius 2016 quotes ('only ever caught 1 galjoen on that stretch myself', 'the wreck found behind the Milnerton golf course', a 'steenie' at the wreck) and the 'not always the safest spot' line from sealine thread 93741 are not in the cached evidence. The cache holds only a search snippet for that thread (asks which baits to use and where the tackle shops are). These quotes come from an uncached merge-step fetch and could not be verified here.

The fishingreminder blurb is an aggregator, and the cached summaries disagree on its scope. Two say 'beaches from Milnerton to Bloubergstrand produce kob, elf/shad and winter galjoen'. A third says the blurb 'describes Bloubergstrand, not Milnerton'. It is weak support for kob, elf and galjoen at this exact spot.

Bottom field: 'low reef patches near the lighthouse ("the reef at Milnerton", sealine 2017)' is not supported. The cached snippet is a 2013 post, quoted in a 2017 thread about spots within 1 nm in Table Bay, a boat context. Jacita (May 2025) names 'Milnerton Banks' only as a boat fishing ground. Kaspaas places his reefs 'from Blouberg all the way to Big Bay', not at Milnerton. No source puts reef that can be reached from shore near the lighthouse.

Elf: method 'spinning' is invented. No source gives any method for elf at Milnerton. The beach claim rests only on the aggregator stretch blurb. The other elf mentions are lagoon memories (1960s to 1980s) or second-hand ('heard that elf were caught there in the past').

species.size: Not stated by any source for this spot.
species.bait: Method not stated by the sources for Milnerton; spoons and small plugs are the standard elf lures on this coast, and bait anglers use pilchard strip (general practice, not from the spot pages).
species.notes: fishingreminder: Milnerton to Bloubergstrand beaches produce 'elf/shad'. matouf (sealine, 2007) recalls 'baitfish and odd leerie or elf' at Woodbridge Island after the island was developed. alwyn (sealine, 2010) says 'elf, steenbras, stumpnose and leeries were the main species targetted' in the Milnerton lagoon in the 1960s and 70s, and a 2014 poster heard elf were caught there in the past. Closed season 1 October to 30 November.

species.size: Not stated by any source for this spot.
species.bait: White mussel, worms and freshly pumped sand prawn on small hooks; a sealine regular says red bait 'isn't used in this area' and frozen pink prawns don't work.
species.notes: kaspaas (sealine, 2014): 'You can try the areas near the Milnerton Lighthouse', edibles galjoen, kob, hottentot and sometimes steenbras, with an 11 ft scratch rod for the reef fish. M@rius (sealine, 2016): 'only ever caught 1 galjoen on that stretch myself' in about ten attempts, 'at the wreck found behind the Milnerton golf course', on a bad-weather day. zzzz (sealine, 2007): 'a few galjoen' caught 'very nearby' the lagoon. fishingreminder: 'winter galjoen' on the Milnerton to Bloubergstrand beaches. Closed season 15 October to end February.

species.size: Not stated by any source for this spot.
species.bait: White mussel, worm, sand prawn or pilchard on small hooks, scratching over the reef patches.
species.notes: kaspaas (sealine, 2014): hottentot among the edibles near the Milnerton Lighthouse; 'An 11ft scratch rod with an SL30 reel for reef fish like blacktail, hottentot and galjoen'. Only one source names it for this spot; it needs the reefy patches rather than open sand.

species.size: Not stated by any source for this spot.
species.bait: Pilchard, mullet (haarder) strip, freshly pumped sand prawn or white mussel (kaspaas's West Coast bait list). Paddle-tails are the usual light-tackle approach for kob but no source documents lures at Milnerton.
species.notes: kaspaas (sealine, 2014) lists kob among the edibles near the Milnerton Lighthouse and advises a 14 ft medium rod for kob and steenbras. fishingreminder: the beaches from Milnerton to Bloubergstrand 'produce quality kob'. No month, tide or lure detail for Milnerton itself.

species.size: Not stated by any source for this spot.
species.bait: Freshly pumped sand prawn (the area's preferred bait), white mussel or worm.
species.notes: kaspaas (sealine, 2014): 'sometimes steenbras' near the Milnerton Lighthouse. M@rius (sealine, 2016) saw a 'steenie' come out at the wreck behind the golf course once, on a bad-weather day. Posters recall many juvenile steenbras in the adjacent lagoon in the past (sealine 2014). Bag 1, min 60 cm.

name: Milnerton Lagoon
aka: Table Bay Nature Reserve, Milnerton Lagoon section
area: Milnerton / Woodbridge Island
coord_source: Nominatim/OSM place node for Woodbridge Island, cached 29 October 2026 (-33.8842651, 18.4872183), used as the island's lagoon bank; the fly guide calls "the Woodbridge Island area" the best spot. The named stands (old wooden bridge by the golf course, old pump station) could not be geocoded: Nominatim returned no result for "Wooden Bridge Milnerton" on 30 October 2026, so treat the point as within a few hundred metres of the bridge.

access.note: Lagoon Beach public car park at the mouth (OSM, from the merge step). The wooden bridge and the island's lagoon bank are reached from the Woodbridge Island / Otto du Plessis Drive side.

bottom: Sand and mud with prawn beds; algae, weed and debris foul lines and lures ("the line collects algae and debris")
mouth: Managed by the City of Cape Town: "the water level is controlled at the lagoon mouth" at Lagoon Beach. The City closed it around 1999 and the water stood stagnant for three to five months; it was open and "wide and quite deep at times" from late 2013 and had "been open for a few years" by 2015. In September 2026 the City launched a "Milnerton Beach Wells" pilot to raise salinity and improve flushing.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine, sold at the Post Office) for estuarine fish, and its bait-collection section for prawn pumping and cast-netting, with national bag and size limits; local bait boards on the bank set collecting times. If you fish the gated Rietvlei section instead, the City's day fishing permit (R42 adult, max 2 rods with 2 hooks per rod, 2016/17 tariff, from the gate) and a CapeNature freshwater licence apply there. Leervis is release-only nationally.
legality: Allowed, with a permit, as far as the sources show. Not in any MPA: Milnerton is north of Mouille Point, outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, and the Robben Island MPA covers only the island. The lagoon is the Milnerton Lagoon section of the City of Cape Town's Table Bay Nature Reserve: the City's page lists that section and says "For more information about fishing permits and watercraft tariffs, please consult the nature conservation tariffs", and the reserve tariff sheet lists "Day Fishing Permits" (R42 adult, 2 rods with 2 hooks) for the gated Rietvlei section; nothing published states a separate rule, or a ban, for the lagoon banks. Sealine posters (2007) found "there are no signs saying u cannot fish in the lagoon", with posted boards regulating bait collecting "and times and permits". A 2014 thread describes illegal gill nets but no angling ban. The City has temporarily prohibited all recreational use during sewage events (2013). A City flyer that may hold the section rules could not be fetched.
description: The Diep River's tidal lagoon behind Woodbridge Island, inside the City's Table Bay Nature Reserve, is fished with fly and light spinning gear from the island's lagoon bank, the old wooden bridge and the mouth at Lagoon Beach. A 2013 Cape fly-fishing guide lists "elf, leerfish, mullet, some kob", says "The Woodbridge Island area is the best spot" and that "Fishing close to anglers pumping prawns can produce excellent results", but Sealine anglers report thin, variable results: "loads and loads of harders and prawn", one "small leerie" on paddle-tails, and steenbras that are juvenile or historic. Chronic sewage pollution from the Potsdam works is the defining problem, so check the City's water-quality advisories before fishing.
hazards: Chronic sewage pollution from the Potsdam wastewater works: repeated spills, E. coli up to 750 000 per 100 ml in effluent, fish kills (Dec 2019, Mar 2022), recurring City health advisories; after the 2013 spill 'All recreational activities in the affected areas are now prohibited'. Avoid contact with the water and do not eat fish from it while advisories stand
Illegal night gill-netting reported by anglers
Strong current at the mouth when it is open; a drowning at Milnerton Lagoon Beach was reported in December 2023
Very shallow with soft mud and prawn beds; algae and debris foul lines and lures
Wind: the river mouth is a kitesurfing spot in the summer south-easter
Litter and personal safety: anglers asked whether it is safe to fish alone before dark
access_notes: Lagoon Beach car park at the mouth (-33.8928, 18.4824) is the clearest public access; the old wooden bridge is a pedestrian heritage bridge by the golf course at the northern end of Woodbridge Island. The gated, fee-paying part of the Table Bay Nature Reserve is the Rietvlei section (main entrance southern end of Grey Avenue / 10 Sandpiper Crescent, Table View; open daily 07:30 to 16:00, exit by 17:00; R20 adult entry for 2026/27; day fishing permit R42 adult, max 2 rods with 2 hooks per rod at the 2016/17 tariff). No source applies those hours or fees to the lagoon banks. Bait-collecting boards on the lagoon banks post times and permit rules. No drive-time statement in any source.
unverified: Whether the City requires its own fishing permit on the lagoon banks outside the gated Rietvlei section; the City flyer with section rules could not be fetched (connection refused, 30 October 2026)
Free public access and parking on the lagoon banks apart from the Lagoon Beach car park, and whether the reserve's 07:30 to 16:00 hours apply to the lagoon banks at all
Exact coordinates of the old wooden bridge and the old pump station; the record uses the Woodbridge Island OSM node
Best months: no source gives a season for any species here; Cape leervis and elf are generally summer fish
White steenbras 60 cm minimum size and bag limit of 1, and leervis release-only status, come from the national recreational regulations, not from a page opened for this spot

The 2013 'All recreational activities in the affected areas are now prohibited' notice and the 2013 rumours of new no-prawn-pumping signs come from the finders' notes; the source page is not in the cached evidence
The 2007 remark 'You go in through the gates where all the boats launch from and they will tell you where to fish' appears to describe the Rietvlei launch gates, not the lagoon
The flytalk thread (blocked) reportedly describes a leervis bite mark on a mullet and the mouth being open 'for a few years' in 2015, seen only in a search snippet
Whether the 'Black River (Milnerton)' named for harders on Sealine is the same water as the lagoon
legal_note: no official statement on angling was found. The City closed the lagoon, the estuary mouth and Lagoon Beach for swimming and recreation in December 2022 because of sewage pollution; its facility page no longer shows the closure, but no notice lifting it was found. If it is open, a DFFE permit applies because it is an estuary.

issues: Budget note: the evidence file is capped at about 90 KB ('stopped: 78 records matched'). It does not contain the record's two strongest light-tackle sources: the capeflyfishing.blogspot.com 2013 fly guide (the 'elf, leerfish, mullet, some kob', 'Woodbridge Island area is the best spot' and 'close to anglers pumping prawns' quotes) and sealine thread 80519 (the 'loads and loads of harders and prawn', 'small leerie' on paddle-tails and kob 'rumours' quotes). I could not verify either one, and I had no budget left to fetch them.

The reason field says 'Sealine threads document paddle-tail, fly and light-bait fishing from the lagoon bank and the old wooden bridge'. The Sealine threads in the evidence (85348, 2294, 41688, 5715, 99273) document only bait fishing, cast-netting and milk-crate catching of harders and mullet, pumped prawn for steenbras, and leervis 'years ago'. None mentions a paddle-tail or a fly. Light-bait shore fishing from the wooden bridge is supported, but only for the 1980s and around 2011.

Every angling report in the evidence is from 2007 to 2018, and most describe decline: 2007 'an expanse of water dead, no fish, no bait' (sealine 2294); a 2014 thread titled 'Angling potential? Not likely!!' (sealine 85348); a 2018 poster ruled Milnerton out for harders because 'they need to be a decent size and not come from dirty water' (sealine 99273). The newest sign of fish is a 2026 Southern Mullet sighting far up the Diep River (vernonchalmers 2026/10), which is not an angling report.

Kob: the lagoon sources in the evidence argue against it. sealine 41688 (alwyn, 1960s-70s) 'couldn't recall kob'; the 85348 summary says 'No kob or flounder are mentioned'. In the search results, kob is mentioned only for the open surf beaches from Milnerton to Bloubergstrand, not for the lagoon. The fly guide's 'some kob' is not in the cached evidence. The kob bait 'Paddle-tails or flies' is invented.

Leervis: the record cites themissionflymag.com/open-secrets-zandvlei-leervis for 'the estuary used to produce good leeries'. That article is about Zandvlei, the page is not in the evidence, and the quote probably refers to Zandvlei, not Milnerton. Drop the citation unless the page names Milnerton.

Harders: 'Mostly small, 15 to 30 cm' and months [1..12] appear in no source. The record itself admits 'no source gives a season for any species here'. The 'common' abundance rests on the unverified thread 80519; the cached threads support harders (springers on outgoing spring tides, harders off the wooden bridge, 'some big harders' in the 1960s-70s) but give no current abundance.

species.size: Mostly small, 15 to 30 cm; 'springers (large harders)' run on outgoing spring tides
species.bait: Small flies on fly gear (the fly guide lists mullet); small hooks and light bait from the wooden bridge (no specific bait named); cast nets are used to take them for livebait or the braai, which needs the DFFE permit
species.notes: Dec 2013: 'there are loads and loads of harders and prawn in the lagoon'. 1980s: 'harders off the wooden bridge'; mullet off the wooden bridge again around 2011. 'Outgoing spring tides produced springers (large harders) and mullet'. A 2018 poster rejected Milnerton harders because 'they need to be a decent size and not come from dirty water'. 2026: a southern mullet was sighted far up the Diep River as an early recovery sign.

species.size: Mostly small or juvenile today ('a small leerie', 'a few juvenile leerie' near the wooden bridge); 'sizer leeries' were taken near the old pump station in the 1980s
species.bait: Paddle-tails (the one documented recent catch), flies, or a small live mullet fished 'as light as possible'
species.notes: Jan 2014: 'one day I picked up a small leerie there' while throwing paddletails. 2008: 'We used to catch at Milnerton lagoon as well years ago'. 2007: 'odd leerie or elf'. The Mission: the estuary 'used to produce good leeries and other species of fish'. Fly guide lists leerfish. No source gives a season. Leervis must be released by law in SA recreational regulations (catch-and-release species).

species.size: Juveniles: 'small steenies' in the 1980s, a 6 cm fish netted around 2011; 'sizeable steenies' last reported around 1999. Below the 60 cm legal minimum, so release fish here
species.bait: Pumped sand or mud prawn from the lagoon's own beds
species.notes: Caught 'juvenile steenbras on pumped prawn' as a child (1980s); 'many steenbras' in the past, with illegal night gill nets blamed for the decline. The same 2007 recollection ('from stumpnose to steenbras to harder') also lists sand shark, and galjoen were reported 'very nearby' in the surf, not in the lagoon.

species.size: Not stated; recent mentions are hearsay
species.bait: Spoons, plugs or flies; no lagoon-specific lure named
species.notes: Fly guide lists elf. 2007: 'baitfish and odd leerie or elf'. 2014: a poster 'heard that elf were caught there in the past'. In the 1960s to 70s 'elf, steenbras, stumpnose and leeries were the main species targetted there'.

species.size: Not stated; historic
species.bait: Prawn
species.notes: 2007 recollection of catches 'from stumpnose to steenbras to harder'; a main target in the 1960s to 70s. No recent report.

name: Blouberg
area: Bloubergstrand / Table View
coord_source: Merge-step Nominatim result for Big Bay / Eden on the Bay (-33.7928, 18.4588), rechecked on photon.komoot.io on 30 October 2026, which returned Eden on the Bay at -33.79236, 18.45777 and no feature for Little Bay, Kleinbaai or the Blouberg rocks. This point is the car park at the north end of the stretch, not a single stand: the rock-and-kelp reef runs about 3 km south from the Big Bay point along Sir David Baird Drive and Marine Drive, and anglers fish anywhere along it.

access.note: Big Bay public car park beside the Eden on the Bay centre; the rocks begin at the point on the south side of the bay. Further south, street parking on Sir David Baird Drive at Bloubergstrand village (Little Bay rocks) and along Marine Drive in Table View (the Doodles to Blue Peter reef below the promenade).

bottom: Shallow rock reef and kelp beds broken by sand gullies along the Table View to Bloubergstrand front and around the Big Bay point; open sand with sandbanks on the Big Bay and Dolphin Beach stretches. Gullies on this coast sand up between big seas.
permit: DFFE recreational marine angling permit (sold at Post Office branches) for rod-and-line fishing; separate permits are needed to cast-net harders or to collect mussels and other bait. National bag and size limits and closed seasons apply: galjoen closed 15 October to end February, elf/shad closed 1 October to 30 November, white steenbras one fish of 60 cm or more. Rock lobster and abalone may not be taken here according to Wikipedia; check the current DFFE recreational rock-lobster rules before diving for crayfish.
legality: Allowed with a permit. Open coast outside every MPA: the Table Mountain National Park MPA ends at Mouille Point and the Robben Island MPA surrounds the island only (its restricted zone lies between E18 12.12' and E18 21.72'; this shore is at about E18 27'). Wikipedia's Blaauwberg article says the Bloubergstrand area "falls within a marine nature reserve" where "the extraction of species such as Cape rock lobster and abalone is prohibited", and in the same section that "a licence is required in order to catch previously well-known local varieties of galjoen and Hottentot", so angling is licensed, not banned. Sealine anglers report fishing these rocks and beaches openly from 2012 to 2025. Not checked: the City of Cape Town Coastal By-law rule on fishing inside the lifeguarded bathing area at Big Bay in summer.
description: A roughly 3 km front of shallow rock reef, kelp and sand gullies running from the Table View beachfront (Doodles to the Blue Peter) through Bloubergstrand village and Little Bay to the rocky point at Big Bay, facing west-south-west over Table Bay towards Robben Island. Sealine anglers fish it "off the rocks and in-between the kelp" with a 10 to 12 ft, 2 to 4 oz rod for "small hotties and the occasion galjoen", and report three bronze bream, "plenty of rockfish" and a small shark from "the blouberg beach and rocks"; kaspaas lists galjoen, kob, hottentot and sometimes steenbras for "the reefs from Blouberg all the way to Big Bay just past Table View", with shy and gully sharks as the bait-rod bycatch. Catches are patchy: several posters record blanks, one found "no fish around the Blouberg Area" bar shy sharks, and 12 degree upwelled water in April 2024 gave "not even a tug".
hazards: Exposed Atlantic shore: constant trade winds bring 1 to 3 m surf for most of the year and Big Bay takes the full swell.
Cold Benguela water; upwelling to 12 degrees kills the bite ('Not even a tug', April 2024).
Slippery kelp-covered rock, and gullies that sand up between big seas.
Busy water: kitesurfers and windsurfers off Big Bay and Dolphin Beach in the summer south-easter, swimmers at Big Bay; keep casts clear of the bathing area.

Security: the spots are busy by day but 'empty quickly at sundown'; do not fish alone after dark (Sealine, 2016), and 'I wouldn't venture to secluded spots after dark' (Sealine, 2014). The bait-rod bycatch is shy and gully sharks.
access_notes: Big Bay: large public car park beside the Eden on the Bay centre (shops, ablutions); the rocks begin at the point on the south side of the bay. Bloubergstrand village: street parking on Sir David Baird Drive near Ons Huisie and the Blue Peter, with a short walk over the rocks into Little Bay. Table View: roadside parking along Marine Drive from Doodles to Dolphin Beach, with the kelpy beachfront reef below the promenade. No gate or fees and no closing time, but anglers advise fishing by day or in company. Nearest tackle shops named on Sealine: Big Catch (Paarden Eiland) and Sea Port Supply. Bait for this coast is white mussel, worms, pilchard, harder and freshly pumped sand prawn; frozen pink prawns 'don't work' and redbait is little used here (Sealine, 2014). Expect 'forget about getting to the beach, casting in and leaving within an hour or so' fishing.
unverified: 'Large kabeljou are still in Blouberg for anglers who know where to cast' (2017) is quoted in the merge notes but does not appear in the cached evidence (the evidence file was capped at about 90 KB).
Tide preference: no source gives a tide stage for this stretch; the only tide reference on this coast is a morning high tide for steenbras at Derdesteen (2011).

Parking details (Big Bay car park at Eden on the Bay, Sir David Baird Drive, Marine Drive), Big Bay's lifeguard season and the City Coastal By-law rule on fishing in bathing areas come from general knowledge, not from a cached or fetched page; Sealine threads say access and parking are not discussed.

The compass bearing (245 degrees) and the reef-and-sand bottom description are read from the map and from the posts' wording ('rocks and in-between the kelp', 'reefs', 'sandbanks'), not from a page that states them.
Elf and yellowtail have no shore catch report for this stretch: elf rests on the fishingreminder listing, yellowtail on a 2017 sighting.

Legal sizes and closed seasons quoted (galjoen 15 Oct to end Feb, elf 1 Oct to 30 Nov, white steenbras one fish at 60 cm) are from the national MLRA regulations as remembered, not from a page fetched in this pass.

No spinning or fly report for Blouberg itself was found: a 2018 Sealine question about artificial lures on this coast went unanswered, and the only dropshot mention is from a kayak at Melkbos. The light-tackle fit rests on one angler's 2024 reports with a 2 to 4 oz rod and on the small-hook hottentot and harder fishing.

issues: Legality holds. The shore at about E18 27.5' sits between the end of the TMNP MPA at Mouille Point and the Robben Island MPA, which surrounds the island only. Wikipedia's Blaauwberg page (fetched 2 Nov 2026) has both quotes word for word: 'The Bloubergstrand area falls within a marine nature reserve' (lobster and abalone) and 'A licence is required in order to catch ... galjoen and Hottentot'. So angling is licensed, not banned. One gap: the Robben Island restricted-zone longitudes the record gives (E18 12.12' to E18 21.72') appear in no cached or fetched page, so they are unsourced. The conclusion does not depend on them.

The anchor point is the Big Bay car park (Eden on the Bay). That puts it next to the Big Bay bathing and kitesurf beach, the one part of the stretch where the unchecked City Coastal By-law bathing-area rule is most likely to apply. Big Bay itself is open sand. The rocks-and-kelp evidence points to Bloubergstrand village and Little Bay instead: Just Billy's 'blouberg beach and rocks' and his 'Doodles to Blue Peter' question, plus Sealine's Kleinbaai harders. Photon puts Ons Huisie, on Little Bay, at -33.79952, 18.45899, about 750 m south of the record point. The point is still on the named stretch, so it is not refuted, but the Little Bay rocks make a better anchor.

drive_hint misattributes a quote. In the cached 2014 thread (cape-town-fishing-advise-urgently-needed.83487), kaspaas says 'well within your 40 km area' about Derdesteen, Haakgat, Bontkop and Melkbosstrand beach, not about the Blouberg to Big Bay reefs.

The light-tackle fit is weaker than the record says for kob and white steenbras. kaspaas (2014) gives an 11 ft scratch rod for hottentot and galjoen but a 14 ft medium rod with a Daiwa 40 or Shimano 30 reel for kob and steenbras. In the 'Light tackle spots in blouberg?' thread (2018), the poster says conditions 'looked like medium-to-heavy tackle', and nobody named a light-tackle spot in reply. Labelling kob and steenbras 'light bait' (or 'dropshot' for kob) goes against the record's own sources. Only the hottentot, galjoen, klipvis and harder fishing fits light tackle.

Much of the cited material covers Derdesteen, Haakgat, Kreeftebaai, Bontkop and Melkbos, several km north of Big Bay, not the Table View to Big Bay front. Examples: Blouberg & Melkbos thread posts #11 to #16, the galjoen-fishing-west-coast thread (Bontkop, Kreeftebaai, Melkbos kayak), and cape-town-fishing-spot.102094 (Melkbos slip, Derdesteen). gotaway's 'cob and steenbras currently around in numbers' (2016) names no spot. These do not show those species on this stretch.

The novanews.co.za/districtmailhelderberg/?p=268986 source cited for kob is not in this spot's cached evidence. The outlet covers the Helderberg (Strand and Somerset West), so it cannot support kob at Blouberg.

species.size: Pan-sized braai fish.
species.bait: Bread, dough or a sliver of pilchard on a tiny hook under a float; the thread does not say how, and most locals net them (cast net needs its own permit).
species.notes: Kleinbaai (Small Bay / Little Bay) at Bloubergstrand is named with Black River and Melkbos as the best Cape Town harder spots (Sealine, 2018). Licensed trek-net fishermen still row their nets out in Small Bay.

species.size: Mostly small fish off these rocks ('small hotties'); the 2 kg-plus fish are boat catches on the Milnerton Banks and around Robben Island.
species.bait: White mussel, prawn, pilchard strip or redbait on a #1 to 2/0 long-shank hook with a light trace, fished right against the kelp; long thin baits are easier for them to swallow.
species.notes: Just Billy (Apr 2024): 'Loving it off the rocks and in-between the kelp... I catch small hotties and the occasion galjoen' on a 10 to 12 ft 2 to 4 oz rod. kaspaas (2014) lists hottentot for the reefs from Blouberg to Big Bay. stinkmossel (2012) suggested a Blouberg spot for hotties: white mussel, or redbait when the water looks like galjoen water. In cold water they sit near the surface among the kelp fronds; a green tinge makes them active, ice-cold blue upwelled water shuts them down.

species.size: Small; bycatch.
species.bait: Any scrap of mussel or prawn on a small hook dropped into the kelp gullies.
species.notes: 'Plenty of rockfish' along the Blouberg beach and rocks (Just Billy, Feb 2024).

species.size: Not reported for this stretch; 'the occasion galjoen' off the rocks (2024). The legal season runs 1 March to 14 October.
species.bait: White mussel first (kaspaas says redbait is little used on this coast); redbait when the water is rough and foamy 'gally water'.
species.notes: fishingreminder: Bloubergstrand's beaches produce 'winter galjoen on clean water'. jacques9 (Jan 2017) on the Blouberg to Melkbos stretch: galjoen are plentiful in winter and not worth fishing for in summer. kaspaas (2014) lists galjoen for the reefs from Blouberg to Big Bay.

species.size: Not reported.
species.bait: The one catch report names no bait; redbait, mussel or prawn on a small hook in the kelp gullies is the standard bream bait.
species.notes: Just Billy (Feb 2024) fished 'along the blouberg beach and rocks' and caught 'only three bronze bream, plenty of rockfish and a small shark'. Single February report, so the months are a guess from it.

species.size: Not reported.
species.bait: Spoons, small plugs or paddle-tails on a light spinning rod; no local report names a lure for this stretch.
species.notes: Listed for Bloubergstrand by fishingreminder ('quality kob, elf/shad, and winter galjoen'); a 2018 Sealine question about elf and leervis on this side went unanswered. Closed season 1 October to 30 November.

species.size: Not reported for this stretch; most Blouberg shore reports are blanks.
species.bait: Fresh pilchard, harder (mullet) strip or freshly pumped sand prawn on bait; soft plastics fished low and slow in the evening are the lure option, but the only dropshot report for this coast is from a kayak at Melkbos.
species.notes: kaspaas (2014) lists kob for the reefs from Blouberg to Big Bay; fishingreminder says these beaches 'produce quality kob'; gotaway (Apr 2016) said cob and steenbras were 'currently around in numbers' and advised flat water; kob and steenbras are the species most mentioned for this side (2018). Catches are actually reported from neighbouring Melkbos (cob, elf and white stumpnose at the slip, Feb 2025), not Blouberg itself. Lure anglers elsewhere fish kob low and slow from late spring to autumn.

species.size: Not reported; bag limit one fish of 60 cm or more.
species.bait: Freshly pumped sand prawn or white mussel on a light surf rig; prawn is the steenbras bait used at nearby Derdesteen.
species.notes: kaspaas (2014): the Blouberg to Big Bay reefs hold 'sometimes steenbras'; gotaway (Apr 2016): cob and steenbras around in numbers; Dr halibut hoffman (2024): in very cold water steenbras are the likely catch. A 2012 question whether Blouberg to Melkbos is best for winter steenbras went unanswered.

name: Haakgat
area: Blaauwberg Nature Reserve coast, between Big Bay and Melkbosstrand (Bloubergstrand north)
coord_source: Nominatim natural=bay node "Haakgat, Melkbosstrand, Western Cape" (-33.7519444, 18.4408333), queried 2026-10-30; it matches the merge-step node. No car-park node exists in OSM, so the stand is the bay itself; the signposted Haakgat parking area sits just inland of it off Otto du Plessis Drive.
bottom: Rocky reef with kelp and red-bait beds, broken by sand gullies ("holes" or "gaps") that fill with sand in calm spells and scour open after storms.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine, sold at Post Offices). Galjoen closed 15 Oct to end Feb; bag and size limits for galjoen, kob and white steenbras apply. The City's Blaauwberg Nature Reserve has its own permit tariffs for some activities but lists none for shore angling; confirm with reserve management on 021 444 0454.
legality: Allowed with a DFFE recreational angling permit. Haakgat is on the West Coast north of Big Bay, far outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA (whose Atlantic boundary ends at Mouille Point) and outside the Robben Island MPA (the island only); no other MPA covers this coast. The shore is the coastal section of the City of Cape Town's Blaauwberg Nature Reserve (open sunrise to sunset, seven days): the City's reserve page lists no fishing prohibition, and the City's 2016 reserve flyer, as summarised in search results, advises anglers to fish while in possession of a valid permit. Sealine posters describe fishing it alongside 5-6 other anglers with no suggestion it is restricted. National rules apply, including the galjoen closed season (15 October to end of February) and bag and size limits.
description: Haakgat is a small rocky bay with kelp, red-bait beds and sand-filled gullies on the open West Coast between Big Bay and Melkbosstrand, inside the coastal section of the City of Cape Town's Blaauwberg Nature Reserve. Sealine anglers fish it from the rocks with bait for galjoen in winter and hope for kob and white steenbras, but it is slow: one poster "tried 3 weekends in a row at Haakgat without any success", another reports "No luck", and a local explains the gullies only open after storms ("Wait for another few storms and the gallies will start feeding"). The local advice is to fish the early push ("Best time is 2h after low") in a NW wind once the swell has dropped, with white mussel, prawn or wonder worm.
hazards: Big Atlantic swell washes the rocks: "if the swell are to big you don't get anything" and "Die swell kan baie groot raak" - the local advice is to stay home when the swell is up
Slippery kelp-covered reef and red-bait beds; the gullies sand up for weeks after calm spells
Cold water (11-16 C) and strong summer SE winds; Haakgat is a popular kitesurf launch, so expect kites off the beach on windy afternoons

Secluded after sundown: "I wouldn't venture to secluded spots after dark"; spots on this stretch empty quickly at sunset, and posters asked whether cars are safe at the neighbouring Bontkop pull-off, suggesting parking at Haakgat instead
Reserve coastal section closes at sunset
access_notes: Turn off Otto du Plessis Drive (the Big Bay to Melkbosstrand coast road) at the signposted Haakgat coastal parking area, one of the Blaauwberg Nature Reserve's coastal lots alongside Derdesteen, Kreeftebaai and Holbaai. Coastal section hours are sunrise to sunset, seven days a week. A Western Cape Government holiday notice (seen only in a search summary) said entry to these coastal parking areas is free; the reserve's main gates charge R20 per adult and R20 per vehicle, cashless only, so confirm with reserve management on 021 444 0454. It is a short walk from the car park to the rocks; anglers also park here and walk round to Bontkop. Nearest bait and tackle: Big Catch (Paarden Eiland) and Sea Port Supply; mud prawn is pumped at Milnerton lagoon. Posters say the spots are busy by day in hot weather.
unverified: No source describes lure, fly or explicitly light-tackle fishing at Haakgat itself; the "Light tackle spots in Blouberg" thread only records "No luck" there, and all Haakgat reports are bait sessions of unstated tackle weight
The merge's "kob (dropshot)" comes from a lure thread naming Bontkop, Koeberg, Derdesteen and Ganzekraal and a search snippet about Bontkop, not Haakgat; that lure thread was not re-read in this pass

Free entry to the Haakgat coastal parking area and the 2016 flyer's permit wording were seen only in search-result summaries; the Western Cape Government notice (westerncape.gov.za/gc-news/33/5837) returned 404 on fetch and the flyer PDF was not fetched
Whether the coastal lots sit outside the reserve's R20 fee gates is not stated on the City page

The facing bearing (about 255 degrees) is read from the run of the coast on the map, and the shallow reef-and-gully character from the posters' talk of holes, kelp and sanding up; no source gives these numerically
No typical sizes are reported for any species here
Months for kob and white steenbras rest on a single April 2016 mention for the stretch
Drive times are OSRM estimates from the merge step; no source states one

issues: Legality holds on position. At about -33.752, 18.441, Haakgat is well north of Mouille Point, so it is outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA. It is also about 8 km from Robben Island, outside that MPA. No restricted zone in the reference list covers this coast. But the Blaauwberg Nature Reserve claims are not in the cached evidence. The City reserve page, the 2016 flyer and the 'free coastal parking' notice do not appear in haakgat.evidence.md, so 'the flyer tells anglers only to carry a valid permit' rests on a search summary that was never fetched. Treat the reserve rules as unverified, not confirmed.

The angling evidence is real but weak, and none of it is explicitly light tackle. sealine.co.za/threads/haakgat-blaauwberg-strand.82788 (Apr 2014) is all blank bait sessions. One regular, Mengs, says he 'has seen only one galjoen caught there'. sealine.co.za/threads/light-tackle-spots-in-blouberg.100585 lists Haakgat only with 'No luck', calls the area 'tough', and says Derdesteen looked like medium-to-heavy tackle water. The only tackle guidance for this coast (cape-town-fishing-advise-urgently-needed.83487) is an 11 ft scratch rod with an SL30 for galjoen and a 14 ft medium rod with a Daiwa 40 for kob and steenbras. Galjoen bait-scratching in the gullies is the only part that fits the light bait-fishing scope.

I re-fetched west-coast-derdesteen-to-melkbos.93896 (page 1 of 2) on 2026-11-02. It confirms these quotes: 'tried 3 weekends in a row at Haakgat without any success', 'Got some nice open holes and the gallies are on the bite', 'Best time is 2h after low', 'Nw is jou beste wind' and 'Die swell kan baie groot raak'. But the 'on the bite' report covers Kreeftebaai to Melkbos with no named spot. The friend's galjoen is at an unnamed spot. The NW wind and swell advice (posts #17-18) answered a question about Bontkop, not Haakgat. The '2h after low' advice is confirmed for the whole stretch (#10). No catch at Haakgat itself appears anywhere in the thread.

The hazard line misreads the thread. In #14, Chuck2103 asked whether his car was safe at Bontkop or whether he should park at Haakgat or Vlei and walk round. jacques9 answered in #15 that his car is safe at Bontkop. Nobody 'suggested parking at Haakgat instead'.

Kob is not reported at Haakgat in any source. The only kob in the Derdesteen-to-Melkbos thread is at Ganzekraal (#11, 'meestal net kabeljou'). Elsewhere kob appears only as a stretch-wide forum target ('Kob and steenbras come up most on the forum') or an area-wide note ('cob and steenbras currently around in numbers', Apr 2016, Blouberg/Big Bay/Melkbos). The one tackle setup the sources give for kob on this coast is a 14 ft rod, which is heavy rock-and-surf and outside the light-tackle scope.

White steenbras is not reported at Haakgat either. It appears only as the same stretch-wide or area-wide target, plus one sighting at the Milnerton golf-course wreck. The record admits no steenbras catch at Haakgat is reported, and the tackle point is the same as for kob.

species.size: Not reported for this spot.
species.method: light bait (small hooks, in the gullies on the push)
species.bait: White mussel, mud/sand prawn (pumped at Milnerton lagoon, called "the best bait for that area"), wonder worm, chokka, pilchard. Red bait is debated: "It doesn't work in this area" versus "Redbait works very well, depends on the spot".
species.notes: The one fish anglers actually report here. A 2014 regular had seen only one galjoen caught at Haakgat; in 2016 a local said "Wait for another few storms and the gallies will start feeding", then "Got some nice open holes and the gallies are on the bite" on the Kreeftebaai-Melkbos stretch, and his friend landed one. Best tide "2h after low" for this stretch; NW is the best wind; fish before a storm or once the swell drops. Closed season 15 Oct to end Feb.

name: Bontkop (Melkbosstrand south)
area: Melkbosstrand south / Blaauwberg coast
coord_source: Approximate. No geocoder has a feature for the angling spot itself. Nominatim and Photon return only Bontkop B&B (Livingsea Close, Melkbosstrand, -33.7326, 18.4363), and its listing says the house sits on the beach at 43 First Avenue, at the south end of Melkbos, with a nature reserve along its southern border. The stand is put about 200 m west of the B&B, on the estimated shoreline. The merge step's rough point (-33.701, 18.431) lies about 3.5 km further north towards Koeberg. It does not match the forum's suggestion to park at Haakgat and walk, so it was not used.

access.note: Seaward end of First Avenue (Eerstelaan), Melkbosstrand, using the Bontkop B&B geocode. The listing's directions: go to the Melkbos beachfront, turn left, keep south until First Ave at the T, then turn right towards the sea. Sealine anglers also asked about parking at Haakgat or 'Vlei' and walking north.

bottom: Rock and reef with gullies and "holes" between patches of sand. The forum talks about the holes opening after storms on the Haakgat–Melkbos stretch.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit, bought online or at the Post Office. Galjoen rules apply: closed season from 15 October to the end of February, a bag of 2 per day and a 35 cm minimum size. These are the standard DFFE figures and were not fetched this pass; a 2014 Sealine post only confirms the December closure. Because the closed season runs until the end of February, galjoen cannot be kept at the time of writing (late October). No gate fee or reserve permit is reported for the Melkbos end.
legality: Fishing is allowed with a permit. Bontkop is on the Atlantic coast north of Table Bay. It is outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, which ends at Mouille Point, and outside the Robben Island MPA, which covers the island only. The Helderberg MPA is in False Bay, far away. The coast just south of it is Blaauwberg Nature Reserve (City of Cape Town). A Western Cape Government page lists fishing "(permit)" among the reserve's activities. The Cape Town coastal map says a DFFE recreational permit is needed for any fishing or other extractive activity along the coastline. I found no rule closing this stretch.
description: A rocky stretch with gullies at the south end of Melkbosstrand, where the town meets the Blaauwberg Nature Reserve coast. Local Sealine anglers fish it in winter for galjoen, baiting with worm, white mussel and prawn. One calls it "a great area" that "produces more than a few species". The forum's advice is to fish on small swell before a front comes in or as the swell drops after it, starting about two hours after low tide.
hazards: Open Atlantic swell running over low rocks and gullies; big swell also kills the bite
Slippery reef and cold Benguela water
Personal safety: the 2014 thread advises not going to secluded spots after dark
Galjoen closed season 15 Oct to end Feb
access_notes: Park at the seaward end of First Avenue in south Melkbosstrand, or at Haakgat further south and walk north along the shore. jacques9 (2016) says he has "never had car trouble" parking at Bontkop. No gate fee or opening hours are reported for this end. The Blaauwberg Nature Reserve coastal section to the south is run by the City, and its own access rules were not checked. The forum's conditions advice: fish before a storm while the swell is still small and again as it drops; spring tides with flat water were described as good; about 2 hours after low tide is best on this stretch. No lifeguards at the rocks.
unverified: The exact position of the Bontkop stand. It is placed from the Bontkop B&B geocode and that listing's description, not from an angling source.
The '(Koeberg side)' label in the merged name. The evidence puts Bontkop at the south end of Melkbos, towards Haakgat, not north towards Koeberg.

Kob and white steenbras at Bontkop. The merge listed them, but no source names them for this spot: the 2014 thread lists kob, hottentot and steenbras for the Milnerton Lighthouse and Blouberg–Big Bay reefs, and the Melkbos kob were caught on dropshot from a kayak.
Whether lures work here. Tool_Fan (2018) asked about artificial lures in this area and nobody answered.
The typical galjoen size at Bontkop.
Whether Bontkop is inside the Blaauwberg Nature Reserve boundary or just north of it, and whether that reserve has any extra rule for anglers.
The galjoen closed season dates, bag limit and minimum size. They come from standard DFFE regulations that were not fetched in this pass.

issues: Legality holds. The point (-33.7335, 18.434) is on the Atlantic coast north of Table Bay. That is outside the TMNP MPA (which ends at Mouille Point), outside the Robben Island MPA (island only) and far from the Helderberg MPA. None of the cached or fetched pages mention a reserve or bylaw closure (the derdesteen-to-melkbos thread fetched 2 Nov 2026 mentions no restriction). The Koeberg restricted area is several km north at Duynefontein. The reserve and tourism pages the record cites (westerncape.gov.za/gc-news/33/5837, the capetown.travel coastal map PDF, the capetown.gov.za Blaauwberg page) are not in the 29 Oct cache file and were not re-checked here, so the 'fishing (permit)' claim for Blaauwberg Nature Reserve rests on the writer's own fetch.

Evidence holds but only for bait fishing. sealine.co.za/threads/west-coast-derdesteen-to-melkbos.93896/ (fetched 2 Nov 2026) confirms the core claims. jacques9 (19 May 2016) fishes Bontkop almost every weekend in winter and has never had car problems there. craig3007 (20 May 2016) calls Bontkop 'n great area wat meer as n paar spesies produce'. jacques9 names wonder worm, white mussel and prawn as Bontkop baits. Odysseus2016 (galjoen-fishing-west-coast, Jul 2018) landed one galjoen at Bontkop. Nobody in any source mentions lures or spinning, and Tool_Fan's lure question went unanswered. The only tackle named is an 11 ft scratch rod with an SL30 reel. That is the light end of galjoen scratching, so it fits 'light bait' only marginally. The description should say plainly that this is a bait (scratching) spot, not a lure spot.

Quotes in the record are translated from Afrikaans but shown as if verbatim. 'almost every weekend in winter' is jacques9's 'Ek hengel amper elke naweek daar in die winter' and 'never had car trouble' is 'Ek het nog nooit probleme gehad met my kar by bontkop nie'. Mark both as translations. 'a great area' and 'produces more than a few species' are craig3007's words (code-mixed), not jacques9's.

Conditions advice is slightly embellished. jacques9 wrote 'Die gate begin nou mooi lyk' (May 2016, the holes are starting to look good). He did not say the holes open after storms. He advised fishing 'voor die storm as die swell nie groot is nie' (before the storm, while the swell is small). The fetched summary does not show 'again as it drops'. The record also leaves out jacques9's 'Nw is jou beste wind' (NW is the best wind), which should go into access_notes or the conditions text. The '2h after low' tip is confirmed (jacques9, 16 and 18 May 2016, for the Kreeftebaai–Melkbos stretch). The spring-tide, flat-water remark is Chuck2103's (19 May 2016).

Galjoen abundance 'regular' looks overstated. Only one galjoen is reported caught at Bontkop itself (Odysseus2016: 'only got one gallie at Bontkop so far', plus one lost). jacques9's friend's galjoen (May 2016) was on the wider Kreeftebaai–Melkbos stretch, not named as Bontkop. 'occasional' fits the evidence better. Months 5–8 are consistent with the May and July 2016/2018 posts and 'in die winter'. Size is honestly given as not stated.

Coordinates are approximate but not refuted. A Nominatim reverse geocode of -33.7335, 18.434 (2 Nov 2026) returns Bontkop B&B, Livingsea Close, Melkbosstrand (-33.7326, 18.4363) as the nearest object, about 230 m away. That B&B is the only geocoded 'Bontkop' feature, so the stand cannot be shown to be more than 500 m off. The south-of-Melkbos placement is indirectly supported by Chuck2103 (19 May 2016), who asked whether to park 'by Haakgat of Vlei' and walk instead of parking at Bontkop. That puts Bontkop next to Haakgat, south of the town and not on the Koeberg side. No angling source gives the rocky point's exact position.

species.size: Not stated in the sources. Odysseus2016 (2018) landed one and lost 'a large one'.
species.bait: Wonder worm, white mussel and prawn (jacques9, 2016). The 2014 thread recommends worm, white mussel and freshly pumped sand prawn for this coast; red bait and frozen pink prawns are said not to work here.
species.notes: Odysseus2016, Jul 2018: "I have only got one gallie at Bontkop so far". jacques9 fishes Bontkop "almost every weekend in winter" and reported galjoen biting on the Kreeftebaai–Melkbos stretch in May 2016. The 2014 thread recommends an 11 ft scratch rod with an SL30-size reel for galjoen and other reef fish on this coast. Closed 15 Oct–end Feb.

name: Kreeftebaai and Kelpbaai
area: Blouberg to Melkbosstrand coast (West Coast), Cape Town
coord_source: Nominatim (fetched 30 Oct 2026) lists one feature: "Kreeftebaai, Melkbosstrand", type natural/bay, at -33.7333333, 18.4333333. That is a gazetteer point rounded to about 1 arc-minute, so it marks the bay rather than an exact rock and may sit just offshore. It puts the bay between Haakgat (about -33.752) and Melkbosstrand (about -33.718), which fits the forum's "from kreeftebaai to melkbos". The merge step's rough point (-33.69, 18.43) was about 5 km too far north, so I replaced it. A direct curl to Nominatim and Photon returned nothing, probably because of the corporate proxy. I could not find a car park point.

access.note: No separate car park coordinate was found. Anglers park beside the coastal road (Haakgat and "Vlei" are named) and walk to the gutters.

bottom: Sand beach with rock and kelp. The fishing is in the gutters ("holes") between them, which fill with sand for months at a time and open up again after winter storms.
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (marine). The national MLRA limits apply; for galjoen that means the closed season, minimum size and daily bag limit. No local by-law was found.
legality: Fishing is allowed with a permit. Kreeftebaai is on the mainland Atlantic shore north of Bloubergstrand. That is outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA, whose controlled zone ends at Mouille Point, and outside the Robben Island MPA, which covers only the waters around the island. It is also far from the Helderberg MPA. I found no MPA restricted zone on the Blouberg to Melkbosstrand coast. I did not check whether this shore falls inside the City of Cape Town's Blaauwberg Nature Reserve coastal section, or what rules that reserve would add.
description: A small bay on the open Atlantic shore between Haakgat and Melkbosstrand, fished from the sand and rock gutters, mainly for galjoen on bait. Local forum anglers say it fishes well in winter once storms have opened the holes ("kreeftebaai has been delivering very well recently", July 2018), but sand fills the holes for long spells and big swell makes the shore unfishable. Anglers describe the area as better suited to medium-to-heavy tackle. No source mentions lure fishing here.
hazards: Open Atlantic shore: in big swell "no catches" and the shoreline is unfishable (jacques9, 2016)
Gutters fill with sand for weeks or months; with the holes closed, anglers report blank sessions
Kelp in the holes (rofflign suggests fishing the holes in the kelp); expect snags
Personal safety: quiet after sundown, so fish with others after dark
Vehicle security at roadside parking was a concern anglers raised
access_notes: Reached from the coastal road between Bloubergstrand and Melkbosstrand. Anglers in the 2016 thread talk about parking at Haakgat or "Vlei" and walking along the shore, and asking whether cars are safe at the roadside spots. jacques9 says he has never had car problems at Bontkop. In April 2016 tadeo wrote that the spots are busy during the day but "empty quickly at sundown", and advised against going alone after dark. No gate fee or opening hours were found. Drive time (OSRM free-flow, merge step, 29 Oct 2026): about 40 min from Green Point and 53 min from Westlake.
unverified: Light-tackle fit: no source reports lure, dropshot or fly fishing at Kreeftebaai. Tool_Fan asked about lures in this area in 2018 and got no answer, and the 'Light tackle spots in blouberg?' thread says the area suits medium-to-heavy tackle.

The 2011 thread 'Derdesteen & Kreeftebaai Sunday advice' (51201) failed twice with 'socket hang up', and the 29 Oct cache of it was empty. Only its title and the search snippet are known: a cold north-westerly day, asking whether the holes have opened.
Exact location of Kelpbaai relative to Kreeftebaai (CV Padda names them together with Slip and Derdesteen).
Facing bearing of 255 degrees is estimated from the general orientation of the coast, not measured at the stand.
Whether this shore falls inside the City of Cape Town's Blaauwberg Nature Reserve coastal section, and any rules that would add.
Galjoen MLRA rules I believe apply but did not re-check this pass: closed season 15 October to end of February, 35 cm minimum size, 2 per person per day. If correct, galjoen is closed now (30 Oct).
Typical galjoen size at this spot.

Other species: kob, white steenbras and geelbek are said to turn up 'towards Melkbos' (M@rius, 2016, second-hand), but no source ties them to Kreeftebaai, so they are left out. The finders' notes say other anglers caught only shy sharks here; those are bait-caught sharks and not in the species list.

issues: Legality holds. The Blouberg-to-Melkbosstrand shore lies outside every MPA in the reference list: north of the TMNP controlled zone, which ends at Mouille Point; not part of the Robben Island MPA, which covers only the island; and far from the Helderberg MPA. The open gap is the City of Cape Town's Blaauwberg Nature Reserve, whose coastal section probably includes this shore. The record already flags that as unverified, but it should be checked before the spot is called simply 'allowed'. No evidence-file source refutes the record or confirms it either way.

Evidence holds, but the light-tackle fit is weak. The angling sources are real and spot-specific. Sealine 93896 page 1, fetched today, confirms jacques9 (14 May 2016, post #5): 'Worked my way up from kreeftebaai to melkbos today... Got some nice open holes and the gallies are on the bite'. It also confirms his three best baits, 'White mussels Prawns Wonder worm' (post #3, repeated in #18), and 'Best time is 2h after low', which he says in #10 applies to that stretch. The cached 99893 thread has Odysseus2016 (24 Jul 2018) saying 'kreeftebaai has been delivering very well recently'. Against the brief: this is standard surf-gutter galjoen bait fishing. No page mentions lure, dropshot, spinning or fly fishing at Kreeftebaai. Tool_Fan's 2018 question about lures went unanswered, and the 'Light tackle spots in blouberg?' snippet says the area suits medium-to-heavy tackle. The method label 'light bait' is the record's own reading; no source calls it light.

Coordinates are not verified. The evidence file holds no Nominatim result. The record's point (-33.7333333, 18.4333333) is exactly 33 deg 44'S, 18 deg 26'E, a gazetteer point rounded to the minute. My Overpass check returned HTTP 502. From the general line of the coast (Bloubergstrand about 18.458 at -33.80, Melkbosstrand beach about 18.44 at -33.725), the shoreline at -33.733 is likely near lon 18.44. That would put the point roughly 0.5 to 0.8 km offshore. I could not measure it, so I have not refuted the coordinates. However, access.lat/lon simply copies this probably offshore point and should not be presented as a place to park or stand.

The 'Derdesteen & Kreeftebaai Sunday advice' thread (51201) is listed under sources even though its cache is empty: the record body reads 'You've hit your session limit' and the record also lists the URL under blocked_urls. Only the search snippet (Jun 2011, holes opening on a cold north-westerly day) supports anything. Remove it from sources, or cite the search page instead.

The access note says anglers 'talk about parking at Haakgat or "Vlei"'. In the cached 93741 thread, rofflign (#13) asks 'whether anyone had tried the vlei' as a place to fish, not to park. Nothing in the evidence describes parking at the vlei. This looks like a misreading.

Several details are not confirmed by the evidence file or by today's page-1 fetch of 93896: the 'never had car problems at Bontkop' quote, the 'before a storm while the swell is still small, or after the swell drops' timing, and the 'better suited to medium-to-heavy tackle' attribution as applying to Kreeftebaai specifically (the snippet is about Derdesteen and Blouberg generally). They may be on page 2 of 93896, which I did not see. Treat them as unconfirmed.

species.size: Not stated by the sources.
species.bait: White mussel, prawn and Wonder worm, which jacques9 names as his three best baits for the Kreeftebaai-to-Melkbos stretch. Fish the open holes in the sand and kelp.
species.notes: Only winter catches are reported. In May 2016 jacques9 "worked my way up from kreeftebaai to melkbos" and found open holes with galjoen biting. In July 2018 Odysseus2016 wrote that "kreeftebaai has been delivering very well recently". jacques9 also says galjoen are plentiful in winter and he does not bother in summer. Several anglers blanked for weeks in April 2016 while the area was "heavily sanded up". Best time: two hours after low tide, before a storm while the swell is still small, or after the swell drops. Galjoen has a closed season and size and bag limits under the MLRA regulations, which I did not re-check here (see unverified).

name: Melkbosstrand
aka: Melkbosstrand (the slip, main strand and "die vlei")
area: Melkbosstrand, West Coast north of Table Bay
coord_source: Stand: OSM leisure=slipway node 7880491876 on Beach Road, Melkbosstrand, returned by a bounded Nominatim search run on 2026-10-30 (-33.7284015, 18.4388372). Access point: Nominatim "Melkbosstrand Beach" from the merge step (-33.7176, 18.4434), about 1.2 km north of the slipway. The City's page puts the beach parking, lifeguards and slipway at 7th Avenue; it was not checked on the ground which avenue the OSM slipway sits at.

access.note: Melkbosstrand Beach centroid (Nominatim, merge step) for the main strand and the City's 7th Avenue beach parking; the slipway stand is on Beach Road about 1.2 km south, with street parking.

bottom: Sand beach with kelp beds and rock-and-sand gullies offshore; reef at the slip and at "die vlei"; posters say the gullies sand up in calm spells and open after big seas
permit: DFFE recreational angling permit (Marine Living Resources Act, sold at Post Offices) for any rod-and-line fishing from the shore; national bag and size limits apply. Per the DFFE recreational fishing brochure (check the current edition): galjoen closed season 15 October to end February, bag 2 at 35 cm; elf/shad closed season 1 October to 30 November; white steenbras bag 1 at 60 cm, no sale. No City permit or entry fee for the beach; City dog-hour rules apply. Rock lobster needs its own permit and is strictly regulated here.
legality: Allowed. Melkbosstrand is on the open West Coast north of Table Bay: outside the Table Mountain National Park MPA (whose northern end is Mouille Point), outside the Robben Island MPA (which surrounds the island only) and nowhere near the Helderberg MPA. The City of Cape Town's own facility page for Melkbosstrand Beach, 7th Avenue, lists "fishing and angling" among the activities alongside a boat launch and slipway, lifeguards and parking, and states no no-fishing areas. The Robben Island rock-lobster closed area that a forum poster mentions concerns crayfish, not rod-and-line fishing. Checked against the 2004 TMNP MPA zoning, the Robben Island and Helderberg MPA extents in the brief, and the City beach page fetched 2026-10-30.
description: Melkbosstrand is an open, west-facing Atlantic beach about 30 km north of Cape Town, with sand in front of kelp beds and reef patches. Anglers single out three stands: "Melkbos by the slip", which is "very popular for kob and should be pretty safe... easier fishing than the strand reefs" and worth a long cast with braid "at low low tide or outgoing"; the main strand before the kelp; and "die vlei" reef in front of the fire station, which "produces some nice hotties" and is fished on dropshot "off the reef at low" for kob, elf and geelbek. A February 2025 report had kob, elf and white stumpnose coming out; white steenbras and galjoen are the cold-water winter fish.
hazards: Open Atlantic shore: cold water (12 C readings in April 2024), often dirty, with big winter seas; the gullies sand up in calm spells and posters expect fish only after big seas open them
Kelp beds off the sand and reef at the slip and at 'die vlei' snag lures and traces; fish the holes in the kelp
Boat launching and NSRI traffic on the slipway: keep casts clear of the launch lane
After dark: posters call Melkbos one of the safer night spots but say the beach empties at sundown and advise not going alone
Blue Flag bathing beach with lifeguards, bathers, kite- and windsurfers and dog walkers in season
Koeberg nuclear power station lies a few km north; its shoreline restrictions were not checked here, so stay on the town beaches
access_notes: City of Cape Town public beach at 7th Avenue off Beach Road, Melkbosstrand: parking, Blue Flag status, boat launch and slipway, disability access and lifeguards (season and hours not stated); no entry fee stated; general enquiries 021 521 2510. Dogs: not allowed 09:00 to 19:00 from 1 December to 31 March; on a lead from the 5th Avenue main beach to Slabbert se Klippie at all times 1 April to 30 November, and from 1st to 5th Avenue 19:00 to 09:00. The OSM slipway is on Beach Road at the southern end of town: park on Beach Road and walk onto the sand or reef. 'Die vlei' reef is 'in front of the fire station' (2011 post). Nearest tackle shops named by posters: Big Catch (Paarden Eiland) and Sea Port Supply; Melkbos Fisheries sponsored the SSEC kob derby. The Melkbosstrand Angling Club meets at the Melkbos Country Club, Robben Road, and runs the annual galjoen derby (late July, Kommetjie lighthouse to Yzerfontein harbour wall). Note: bait anglers along the Big Bay to Melkbos stretch also report 'skaam haai' (small sharks) on bait; not a light-tackle target.
unverified: Whether the OSM slipway node on Beach Road (-33.7284, 18.4388) is the same boat launch the City lists with the 7th Avenue beach, or a second launch; not checked on the ground
The exact position of 'die vlei' reef: 'in front of the fire station' rests on a single 2011 forum reply

The westerncape.gov.za ('steenbras, kob and blacktail') and fishingreminder ('rock-and-sand gullies and outer banks... galjoen, steenbras, and kob') quotes come from the finders' merged notes of the 29 October cache; those records were truncated out of the capped evidence file and were not re-fetched
Fishingreminder's 'pristine tidal lagoon with clear flats' and 'stumpnose and grunter' text is generic app copy and does not describe Melkbos
Best months and typical sizes are inferred from the dated posts and general West Coast patterns; no source states a season or a size for Melkbos
Geelbek is hearsay plus one dropshot-target mention; no catch report
The facing bearing (245) and shelter rating are read off the coastline, not stated by any source
Current closed seasons and bag limits quoted from memory of the DFFE brochure; confirm against the current edition
Koeberg shoreline restrictions north of the town were not checked
Melkbos Fisheries as a local bait or tackle source is known only as a derby sponsor

issues: LEGALITY HOLDS. Melkbosstrand (-33.73, 18.44) is on the open West Coast about 20 km north of Mouille Point. That puts it outside the TMNP MPA, outside the Robben Island MPA (which covers the island only) and far from Helderberg. The cached search summary of the City of Cape Town beach page (https://www.capetown.gov.za/Family%20and%20home/See-all-city-facilities/Our-recreational-facilities/Beaches/Melkbosstrand%20Beach) says it lists 'Fishing and angling' at the 7th Avenue beach. The westerncape.gov.za fishing page (cached in research_cache.jsonl) lists 'Melkbosstrand: steenbras, kob and blacktail' under shoreline fishing with a marine permit. The DFFE permit statement and the galjoen, elf and white steenbras rules quoted are correct as stated. The dog-hour and 'Slabbert se Klippie' details come from a 30 October page fetch that is not in the cache, so I could not check them.

KEY QUOTES ARE NOT IN ANY SOURCE I COULD FIND. Four quotes in the description, the kob and elf notes and tide_pref appear nowhere in the 29 October cache: 'I would try the slip in melkbos at low low tide or outgoing... a decent cast with braid an u could be into a fat cob', 'Melkbostrand die vlei off the reef at low' on dropshot at 11 to 16 C, subaruseun's 'cob, elf and geelbek' dropshot targets, and 'Melkbos vlei produces some nice hotties... in front of the fire station'. I searched every salvage/*.jsonl file for 'die vlei', 'fire station', 'low low tide', 'fat cob' and '56615' and got no hits. Thread 56615 (lure-fishing-cape-town-area) was never cached. The cached fetch of thread 51033 (fishing-for-hottentots) returned only 'You've hit your session limit', and its search snippet says 'No answers shown'. I tried a direct fetch of both threads on 2 November and both failed with HTTP 000 (corporate proxy), so they are effectively blocked.

LIGHT-TACKLE FIT IS THIN AND CONTESTED. The angling evidence I could verify: 'Melkbos by the slip... very popular for kob and should be pretty safe... Easier fishing than the strand reefs' and 'Melkbos main strand, before the kelp' (https://sealine.co.za/threads/cape-town-fishing-spot.102094/, Jan 2020); 'cob, elf and white stumpnose' caught at Melkbos 'since last weekend' (https://sealine.co.za/threads/spots-near-table-view.103901/, 27 Feb 2025); and 'Slip' named as a stand alongside Kreeftebaai, Kelpbaai and Derdesteen (https://sealine.co.za/threads/blouberg-melkbos.93741/). None of these names a lure or a tackle weight. The thread that actually asks about light tackle (https://sealine.co.za/threads/light-tackle-spots-in-blouberg.100585/) says the Derdesteen-to-Melkbos conditions 'looked like medium-to-heavy tackle' and that 'the fishing is tough that side'. The record leaves this caveat out. The only cached dropshot mention at Melkbos is from a KAYAK (Mahi mahi, https://sealine.co.za/threads/galjoen-fishing-west-coast.99893/), not the shore. The only cached light-spin advice (https://sealine.co.za/threads/new-to-sea-fishing-advice-needed.103348/) is generic beginner gear advice, not specific to Melkbos.
TIDE_PREF 'low' rests entirely on the uncached thread 56615 quotes. The cached threads give no tide at all (93741: 'No tide information was posted'; 102094: 'Tide advice is absent').

'DIE VLEI' AS A NAMED STAND IS UNSUPPORTED. The only cached mention is rofflign in 93741 (Apr 2016) asking 'whether anyone had tried the vlei'. It gives no location and no catch. The fire-station location and the hottentot claim both depend on the failed 51033 fetch.

HOTTENTOT: no cached source supports it at Melkbos. The 51033 fetch failed, and the Hotties thread (https://sealine.co.za/threads/hotties.61809/) explicitly says 'Kommetjie and Melkbos: Not discussed'. Its kelp-and-bait technique comes from Saunders Rock and the Blouberg side. The 'regular' abundance and 12 months of the year are invented.

species.size: No sizes given for Melkbos. West Coast shore kob are mostly school fish under 60 cm, with a 'fat cob' possible on a long cast (general knowledge, not a Melkbos measurement).
species.method: spinning (dropshot or paddle-tail on braid) and light bait
species.bait: dropshot and paddle-tail soft plastics bumped along the sandbanks and worked off the reef; bait anglers use pilchard and bonito strip
species.notes: 'Melkbos by the slip... very popular for kob and should be pretty safe', 'easier fishing than the strand reefs' (Jan 2020). 'I would try the slip in melkbos at low low tide or outgoing... a decent cast with braid an u could be into a fat cob' (Nov 2011). 'Melkbostrand die vlei off the reef at low' on dropshot/artlure, best in medium-visibility water at 11 to 16 C (Nov 2011). 'Cob, elf and white stumpnose' coming out since the previous weekend (27 Feb 2025). 'Cob and steenbras currently around in numbers' (Apr 2016). A kayak angler 'caught a lot of kob on dropshot' at Melkbos. Kob tagged off Strandfontein were recaptured 'between Melkbos and Gaanzekraal'. Months inferred from the dated reports; no source states a season.

species.size: Not stated for Melkbos; Cape surf elf typically 30 to 50 cm (general).
species.bait: spoons and small plugs retrieved fast; dropshot soft plastics off the reef; bait anglers use pilchard or bonito strip
species.notes: 'Cob, elf and white stumpnose' caught at Melkbos (27 Feb 2025). Subaruseun targets 'cob, elf and geelbek' on dropshot at 'die vlei off the reef at low' (Nov 2011). Fishingreminder's generic text says 'summer elf/shad'. Closed season 1 October to 30 November per the DFFE brochure (check current).

species.size: Not stated; typical 30 to 45 cm, bag 2 at 35 cm minimum (general).
species.bait: red bait (rooiaas, which washes up at Melkbos) and white mussel fished in foamy water along the reef edges and kelp holes
species.notes: 'Galjoen are plentiful in winter' and the poster no longer bothers in summer (Jan 2017). The Melkbosstrand Angling Club hosts an annual galjoen derby in late July, weighed in at its clubhouse. 'Heard of occasional galjoen... towards Melkbos' (Apr 2016). Closed season 15 October to end February.

species.size: Not stated for Melkbos; mostly 40 to 70 cm fish, bag limit 1 at 60 cm minimum (general).
species.bait: prawn, white mussel and bloodworm or sand worm cast into the gullies; prawn is the bait named for the Derdesteen side
species.notes: 'Derdesteen, Melkbos side... steenbras' from years of fishing there, with the stretch 'all the way down to the slip' quiet at the time (Jan 2020). 'Cob and steenbras currently around in numbers' (Apr 2016). Western Cape Government fishing page lists Melkbosstrand for 'steenbras, kob and blacktail'. 2de Steen steenbras are the likely catch 'if the water is very cold' (Feb 2024). 'Blouberg to Melkbos for steenbras in winter?' was asked but not answered. A bait fish on medium surf tackle rather than a lure target.
